    • Negation marking (alternative) — nums[abs(x) - 1] ko negative kar do; jo positive bache unke indices missing hain. Same O(n)/O(1), lekin input ke signs corrupt karta hai aur restore karna padta hai. Cyclic sort cleaner hai.
    • Missing numbers ka count sirf — k count karo, list mat banao.
    • Range 0..n-1 — mapping se -1 hata do.

    Interview answer: "The obvious solution marks presence in a boolean array of size n plus one, which is O(n) time but O(n) space. The point of this problem is to use the input array itself as the marker.

    I run cyclic sort: for each position, the value v belongs at index v minus one, so I swap it there. With duplicates present, not everything can reach its home — and that's exactly what I want. After the placement pass, any index whose value isn't index plus one tells me that index plus one is missing.

    The condition inside the swap has to compare values, not indices. If I wrote 'if i is not the correct index, swap', then an array like two-comma-two would swap two identical values forever and hang. Comparing the values means a duplicate is recognised as already-satisfied and the loop advances.

    One thing that trips people up in the scan: I append index plus one, not the value sitting there. The value there is some duplicate — the number that's actually missing is the one that should have been at that index.

    O(n) time, O(1) extra space beyond the output.

    There's an alternative that negates nums at index abs(v) minus one as a presence marker. Same complexity, but it corrupts the sign of the input and needs a restore pass, so I prefer the cyclic sort."

    Problem 5.4 — Find All Duplicates¶

    Problem statement

    Array of length n, values 1 se n. Kuch numbers exactly do baar aate hain, baaki ek baar. Saare duplicates lauta do.

    Input:  [4, 3, 2, 7, 8, 2, 3, 1]     Output: [2, 3]
Input:  [1, 1, 2]                    Output: [1]
Input:  [1]                          Output: []

    Constraint: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Counter banao.

    from collections import Counter

def find_duplicates_brute(nums):
    counts = Counter(nums)                        # 1: har value ka count, O(n) space
    result = []                                   # 2
    for value, count in counts.items():           # 3: har unique value
        if count > 1:                             # 4: ek se zyada baar aayi?
            result.append(value)                  # 5
    return result                                 # 6

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. Counter(nums) — ek hi pass mein counts. Internally dict hai, O(n) space. 2-5. Filter. count > 1 likha, count == 2 nahi — problem "exactly twice" kehti hai lekin > 1 zyada general hai aur agar constraint dheela ho jaaye toh bhi kaam karta hai.
    2. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Wahi — space. Aur note ki Counter ki iteration order Python 3.7+ mein insertion order hai, toh output order input-dependent hai; problem usually order matter nahi karti lekin yeh clarify karna chahiye.

    The insight

    Bilkul Problem 5.3 wala hi placement pass. Farq sirf scan pass mein hai.

    Placement ke baad: agar index i par expected value i + 1 nahi hai, toh: - i + 1 missing hai (5.3 ka answer), aur - jo value nums[i] wahan padi hai, woh ek duplicate hai (kyunki uski asli copy pehle se apne ghar par baithi hai, aur yeh extra copy kahin aur phas gayi).

    Toh 5.3 aur 5.4 ek hi placement pass se dono answers de sakte hain — bas scan mein i + 1 collect karo ya nums[i].

    Yeh do problems ka relationship interview mein bolna bahut strong impression deta hai.

    Optimal solution

    def find_duplicates(nums):
    i = 0                                         # 1: placement pass -- 5.3 se identical
    n = len(nums)                                 # 2
    while i < n:                                  # 3
        correct = nums[i] - 1                     # 4
        if nums[i] != nums[correct]:              # 5: value comparison
            nums[i], nums[correct] = nums[correct], nums[i]   # 6
        else:                                     # 7
            i += 1                                # 8
    duplicates = []                               # 9: SCAN pass -- yahan farq hai
    for i in range(n):                            # 10
        if nums[i] != i + 1:                      # 11: galat value yahan padi hai
            duplicates.append(nums[i])            # 12: WOH VALUE duplicate hai
    return duplicates                             # 13

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-8. Problem 5.3 se bilkul same. Ek hi placement, do alag questions. 9. duplicates = []. 10. Scan. 11. if nums[i] != i + 1: — same check. 12. duplicates.append(nums[i]) — nums[i], na ki i + 1. Yeh line hi 5.3 se ekmatra difference hai. Yahan padi hui value duplicate hai; i + 1 missing hai. 13. Return.

    Kya har mismatched position ek unique duplicate deti hai? Haan, agar problem guarantee kare ki har number at most do baar aata hai. Kyunki har extra copy exactly ek "wrong slot" occupy karti hai. Agar koi number teen baar aa sakta hai toh yeh do baar report hoga — tab set() lagana padega ya count track karna padega. Yeh clarifying question hai.

    Dry run — [4, 3, 2, 7, 8, 2, 3, 1] (n = 8)

    Placement pass bilkul 5.3 wala hi hai — final array [1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 7, 8]. (Poora trace 5.3 mein dekh lo; yahan repeat nahi kar raha kyunki ek hi cheez hai — lekin scan alag hai.)

    Scan pass on [1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 7, 8]:

    i nums[i] i + 1 Match? 5.3 would append 5.4 appends
    0 1 1 Yes — —
    1 2 2 Yes — —
    2 3 3 Yes — —
    3 4 4 Yes — —
    4 3 5 No 5 3
    5 2 6 No 6 2
    6 7 7 Yes — —
    7 8 8 Yes — —

    Result [3, 2]. Expected [2, 3] — order alag hai lekin content same. Problem usually order-agnostic hai; agar sorted output chahiye toh sorted(duplicates) lagao (O(k log k)).

    Yeh table dono problems ka relationship ek hi jagah dikhati hai — ek placement, do answers.

    Dry run — [1, 1, 2] (n = 3)

    Placement:

    Step i nums nums[i] correct nums[correct] Equal? Action nums after i after
    1 0 [1,1,2] 1 0 1 Yes i→1 [1,1,2] 1
    2 1 [1,1,2] 1 0 1 Yes i→2 same 2
    3 2 [1,1,2] 2 1 1 No swap(2,1) [1,2,1] 2
    4 2 [1,2,1] 1 0 1 Yes i→3 same 3

    Scan on [1, 2, 1]:

    i nums[i] i+1 Match? Append
    0 1 1 Yes —
    1 2 2 Yes —
    2 1 3 No 1

    Result [1]. Sahi.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n).
    • Space: O(1) extra.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    No duplicates [1,2,3] [] Scan clean
    All duplicates [1,1,2,2] [1,2] ya [2,1] Order placement-dependent
    Single [1] []
    One value repeated thrice [2,2,2] [2, 2] Do baar report — constraint clarify karo
    Max duplicates [1,1,1,1] [1,1,1] Same issue
    Already sorted with dup [1,2,2,4] [2]

    Teesri aur chauthi row important hain — problem "at most twice" guarantee deti hai toh yeh case aata hi nahi, lekin interview mein poochhna chahiye. Agar guarantee nahi hai toh line 12 ke baad return list(set(duplicates)) ya scan mein ek seen set — jo O(k) space hai.

    Variations

    • Sirf ek duplicate hai, use dhoondo (LeetCode 287) — Problem 3.6 (Floyd) agar array read-only ho; cyclic sort agar modify kar sakein.
    • Duplicate aur missing dono (645) — Problem 5.5.
    • Duplicates aur unke counts — cyclic sort se counts nahi milte; Counter chahiye.
    • Negation marking — nums[abs(x)-1] already negative hai toh abs(x) duplicate hai. Same complexity.
    • First duplicate (jo pehle repeat hota hai) — cyclic sort order preserve nahi karta, toh yeh alag problem hai (set chahiye).

    Interview answer: "This is the same placement pass as finding all the missing numbers — literally the identical loop. Only the scan differs.

    After cyclic sort, every value that could reach its home index did. Any index where the value doesn't equal index plus one is telling me two things at once: index plus one is missing, and the value actually sitting there is a duplicate — because its first copy already claimed the correct slot, so this extra copy got stranded.

    So for missing numbers I collect index plus one, and for duplicates I collect the value. One pass, two possible answers.

    I'd clarify one thing: the problem says each number appears at most twice. If a number could appear three times I'd report it twice, so I'd either dedupe with a set — which costs O(k) space — or track counts.

    Also worth noting the output order is whatever the placement happened to produce, not sorted. If sorted output is required that's an extra O(k log k).

    O(n) time, O(1) extra space."

    Problem 5.5 — Find The Corrupt Pair (Set Mismatch)¶

    Problem statement

    Array mein 1 se n tak ke numbers hone chahiye the, lekin ek number duplicate ho gaya hai aur ek missing ho gaya hai. Dono lauta do: [duplicate, missing].

    Input:  [3, 1, 2, 5, 2]     Output: [2, 4]     (2 do baar, 4 missing)
Input:  [1, 2, 3, 3, 5]     Output: [3, 4]
Input:  [2, 2]              Output: [2, 1]

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Counter banao aur dono dhoondo.

    from collections import Counter

def find_corrupt_brute(nums):
    counts = Counter(nums)                        # 1: O(n) space
    duplicate = missing = -1                      # 2: dono ke liye sentinels
    for v in range(1, len(nums) + 1):             # 3: 1 se n tak har expected value
        c = counts.get(v, 0)                      # 4: kitni baar aayi (default 0)
        if c == 2:                                # 5: do baar -> duplicate
            duplicate = v                         # 6
        elif c == 0:                              # 7: zero baar -> missing
            missing = v                           # 8
    return [duplicate, missing]                   # 9

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. Counter(nums) — O(n) space.
    2. duplicate = missing = -1 — sentinels. Constraints guarantee dete hain ki dono milenge, lekin explicit initialisation defensive hai.
    3. range(1, len(nums) + 1) — expected values.
    4. counts.get(v, 0) — .get with default use kiya, counts[v] nahi. Counter par counts[v] bhi 0 return karta hai missing keys ke liye (KeyError nahi), lekin .get intent zyada saaf karta hai aur normal dict par bhi safe hai. 5-8. Classification.
    5. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n).

    Ek aur — math (sum aur sum-of-squares)

    Do unknowns hain (d = duplicate, m = missing), toh do equations chahiye: - sum(nums) - expected_sum = d - m - sum(x^2) - expected_square_sum = d^2 - m^2 = (d-m)(d+m)

    Dono se d + m nikal jaata hai, aur phir d aur m alag ho jaate hain. Time O(n), Space O(1) — valid hai, lekin overflow-prone aur algebra live derive karna risky hai.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Counter O(n) space leta hai. Math version O(1) hai lekin nazuk hai aur interview pressure mein galti hone ka chance zyada hai.

    The insight

    Cyclic sort ke baad exactly ek position mismatch karegi (kyunki exactly ek duplicate aur ek missing hai). Us position i par:

    • nums[i] duplicate hai (extra copy jo phas gayi),
    • i + 1 missing hai (jo yahan hona chahiye tha).

    Dono answers ek hi position se mil jaate hain. Yeh 5.3 aur 5.4 ka combination hai, aur poora placement pass wahi hai.

    Optimal solution

    def find_corrupt_pair(nums):
    i = 0                                         # 1: placement pass
    n = len(nums)                                 # 2
    while i < n:                                  # 3
        correct = nums[i] - 1                     # 4
        if nums[i] != nums[correct]:              # 5
            nums[i], nums[correct] = nums[correct], nums[i]   # 6
        else:                                     # 7
            i += 1                                # 8
    for i in range(n):                            # 9: SCAN -- pehla mismatch hi kaafi
        if nums[i] != i + 1:                      # 10
            return [nums[i], i + 1]               # 11: [duplicate, missing]
    return [-1, -1]                               # 12: array already perfect tha

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-8. Standard placement pass. 9. for i in range(n). 10. if nums[i] != i + 1:. 11. return [nums[i], i + 1] — dono ek saath, ek hi position se. nums[i] woh galat value hai (duplicate), i + 1 woh expected value (missing). Aur yahan return hai, append nahi — kyunki problem guarantee deti hai ki exactly ek mismatch hai. Agar zyada ho sakti toh 5.3/5.4 wala loop chahiye. Early return isliye correct hai aur thoda faster bhi. 12. return [-1, -1] — defensive. Constraints ke hisaab se yahan nahi pahunchna chahiye, lekin function ko total banana acchi habit hai (aur agar test data invalid ho toh silent None se better hai).

    Dry run — [3, 1, 2, 5, 2] (n = 5, expected [2, 4])

    Placement pass:

    Step i nums nums[i] correct nums[correct] Equal? Action nums after i after
    1 0 [3,1,2,5,2] 3 2 2 No swap(0,2) [2,1,3,5,2] 0
    2 0 [2,1,3,5,2] 2 1 1 No swap(0,1) [1,2,3,5,2] 0
    3 0 [1,2,3,5,2] 1 0 1 Yes i→1 same 1
    4 1 same 2 1 2 Yes i→2 same 2
    5 2 same 3 2 3 Yes i→3 same 3
    6 3 [1,2,3,5,2] 5 4 2 No swap(3,4) [1,2,3,2,5] 3
    7 3 [1,2,3,2,5] 2 1 2 Yes i→4 same 4
    8 4 [1,2,3,2,5] 5 4 5 Yes i→5 same 5
    exit 5 [1,2,3,2,5] — — — — — — —

    Step 7 dekho — 2 position 3 par phansa hai kyunki uska ghar (index 1) already 2 se occupied hai. Yehi "stranded duplicate" hai.

    Scan pass on [1, 2, 3, 2, 5]:

    i nums[i] i + 1 Match? Action
    0 1 1 Yes —
    1 2 2 Yes —
    2 3 3 Yes —
    3 2 4 No return [2, 4]

    Answer [2, 4]. Sahi.

    Dry run — [2, 2] (n = 2, expected [2, 1])

    Placement:

    Step i nums nums[i] correct nums[correct] Equal? Action i after
    1 0 [2,2] 2 1 2 Yes i→1 1
    2 1 [2,2] 2 1 2 Yes i→2 2

    Array unchanged [2, 2].

    Scan:

    i nums[i] i+1 Match? Action
    0 2 1 No return [2, 1]

    Answer [2, 1]. Sahi.

    Yeh dry run dikhata hai ki placement pass ne kuch bhi nahi kiya aur phir bhi answer sahi aaya — kyunki value-based condition ne duplicate ko turant recognise kar liya. Agar i != correct likhte toh step 1 par 0 != 1 True hota, swap hota (array wahi rehta), i nahi badhta — infinite loop.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n).
    • Space: O(1).

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Duplicate at start [1,1] [1, 2] index 1 par 1 padi hai
    Duplicate at end [1,2,2] [2, 3]
    Perfect array (invalid input) [1,2,3] [-1,-1] Line 12
    Two elements [2,2] [2,1] Upar
    Missing 1 [2,2,3] [2, 1]
    Missing n [1,1,2] [1, 3]
    Large n — — Same

    Variations

    • Do duplicates aur do missing — scan mein return ki jagah do lists collect karo (5.3 + 5.4 combine).
    • Sirf missing chahiye — 5.3.
    • Sirf duplicate chahiye — 5.4, ya Floyd (Problem 3.6) agar read-only.
    • Math version — sum aur sum-of-squares se do equations. O(1) space bina array modify kiye. Interview mein alternative ke roop mein bolna acha.
    • XOR version (LeetCode 645 hard variant) — d XOR m nikaal kar bit partitioning se alag karo. Elegant lekin explain karna mushkil.

    Interview answer: "After a cyclic sort placement pass, exactly one index will be wrong — because there's exactly one duplicate and one missing value. And that single index gives me both answers at once: the value sitting there is the duplicate, since its real copy already claimed the correct slot and this extra copy got stranded, and index plus one is the missing value, since nothing was left to fill it.

    So the code is the standard placement loop followed by a scan that returns on the first mismatch. I use return rather than collect because the problem guarantees exactly one.

    The value-based swap condition is doing real work here. On an input like two-comma-two, the placement pass correctly does nothing at all and the scan still finds the answer. If the condition compared indices instead, that input would swap forever.

    O(n) time, O(1) space.

    There's also a pure-math solution: the sum tells me duplicate minus missing, and the sum of squares tells me duplicate squared minus missing squared, which factors into the difference times the sum — two equations, two unknowns. Same complexity, doesn't modify the array, but it's easier to fumble the algebra under pressure and it can overflow in a fixed-width integer language."

    Problem 5.6 — First Missing Positive¶

    Problem statement

    Ek unsorted array diya hai jismein koi bhi integers ho sakte hain — negatives, zeroes, duplicates, aur n se bade numbers. Sabse chhota positive integer dhoondo jo array mein nahi hai.

    Input:  [1, 2, 0]           Output: 3
Input:  [3, 4, -1, 1]       Output: 2
Input:  [7, 8, 9, 11, 12]   Output: 1
Input:  [1, 1]              Output: 2

    Constraint: O(n) time, O(1) space. Yeh LeetCode par "hard" hai, aur poori difficulty is constraint mein hai.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    1 se shuru karo aur har number check karo.

    def first_missing_brute(nums):
    candidate = 1                                 # 1: sabse chhota positive
    while candidate in nums:                      # 2: array mein hai? -> agla try karo
        candidate += 1                            # 3
    return candidate                              # 4

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. candidate = 1 — answer hamesha 1 se n+1 ke beech hota hai. Kyun? Kyunki n elements hain; agar woh exactly 1..n hain toh answer n+1, warna koi 1..n missing hai.
    2. while candidate in nums: — in on a list is O(n). Yeh line hi problem hai. 3-4.

    Complexity: Time O(n^2) worst case (n candidates × O(n) search). Space O(1).

    Ek behtar brute force — set

    def first_missing_set(nums):
    present = set(nums)                           # 5: O(n) space, O(1) lookups
    candidate = 1                                 # 6
    while candidate in present:                   # 7: ab O(1)
        candidate += 1                            # 8
    return candidate                              # 9

    Time O(n), Space O(n) — constraint todta hai.

    Sorting version

    def first_missing_sort(nums):
    nums.sort()                                   # 10: O(n log n)
    candidate = 1                                 # 11
    for x in nums:                                # 12: sorted order mein
        if x == candidate:                        # 13: expected mil gaya
            candidate += 1                        # 14: agla expect karo
        elif x > candidate:                       # 15: aage nikal gaye -> gap mila
            break                                 # 16
        # x < candidate (negative ya duplicate) -> ignore
    return candidate                              # 17

    Time O(n log n), Space O(1). Line 15 ka elif important hai — sorted array mein pehla gap hi answer hai.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Set O(n) space, sort O(n log n) time. Dono constraint todte hain. Interviewer specifically dono chahta hai.

    The insight

    Answer guaranteed 1 se n + 1 ke beech hai (upar wala argument). Toh:

    1. n se bade numbers, zeroes aur negatives ko bilkul ignore kar do — woh answer ko affect nahi kar sakte.
    2. Baaki numbers 1..n range mein hain — cyclic sort chalao.
    3. Scan karo: pehla index jiska value i + 1 nahi hai, wahan i + 1 hi answer hai.
    4. Agar sab sahi hain, answer n + 1 hai.

    Difficulty sirf ek jagah hai: placement loop ko out-of-range values ke saath safely deal karna hai bina infinite loop mein phase.

    Optimal solution

    def first_missing_positive(nums):
    n = len(nums)                                 # 1
    i = 0                                         # 2
    while i < n:                                  # 3: placement pass
        correct = nums[i] - 1                     # 4: value v ka ghar index v-1
        if 0 <= correct < n and nums[i] != nums[correct]:   # 5: in-range AND galat aadmi
            nums[i], nums[correct] = nums[correct], nums[i] # 6: swap
        else:                                     # 7: out of range, ya already sahi/duplicate
            i += 1                                # 8: aage badho -- INFINITE LOOP se bachav
    for i in range(n):                            # 9: SCAN
        if nums[i] != i + 1:                      # 10
            return i + 1                          # 11: pehla gap
    return n + 1                                  # 12: array exactly 1..n tha

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Init. 3. while i < n:. 4. correct = nums[i] - 1 — mapping 1..n → 0..n-1. Note ki nums[i] negative ya bada ho sakta hai, toh correct bhi out of range ho sakta hai — isliye line 5 ka guard. 5. if 0 <= correct < n and nums[i] != nums[correct]: — yeh line hi is problem ki poori difficulty hai. Teen cheezein ek saath: - 0 <= correct — nums[i] ke <= 0 hone par correct negative ho jaata. Python mein negative index crash nahi karta, silently array ke end se index karta hai — toh yeh check na hone par code galat answers deta, exception nahi. Yeh sabse khatarnak bug hai kyunki silent hai. - correct < n — nums[i] ke > n hone par IndexError. - nums[i] != nums[correct] — value comparison, duplicates safe. Aur teenon and se jude hain, jo short-circuit karta hai — toh nums[correct] tabhi evaluate hota hai jab index valid ho. Order badalna crash karega. 6. Swap. 7-8. Else → i += 1. Yeh else branch teen alag situations handle karta hai — out-of-range value, already-correct value, aur duplicate. Teenon ka jawab ek hi hai: is position ko chhod do. 9. Scan pass. 10. if nums[i] != i + 1:. 11. return i + 1 — pehla gap. 12. return n + 1 — yeh line bhoolna sabse common bug hai. [1,2,3] par scan clean hoga aur bina is line ke None return hota.

    Ek concrete example jahan line 5 ka 0 <= correct bachaata hai: nums = [-1, 4, 2, 1, 9, 10], n = 6. Jab i -1 par pahunchega: correct = -2. Bina guard ke nums[-2] = nums[4] = 9. -1 != 9 → swap → [9, 4, 2, 1, -1, 10]. Ab nums[0] = 9, correct = 8, jo >= n hai → IndexError ya aur galat swaps. Guard ke saath: -2 < 0 → else → i += 1, -1 wahin pada rehta hai aur scan use gap ke roop mein pakad leti hai.

    Dry run — [3, 4, -1, 1] (n = 4, expected 2)

    Placement pass:

    Step i nums nums[i] correct 0<=c<n? nums[correct] Swap? nums after i after
    1 0 [3,4,-1,1] 3 2 Yes -1 3 != -1 Yes [-1,4,3,1] 0
    2 0 [-1,4,3,1] -1 -2 No (-2 < 0) — No same 1
    3 1 [-1,4,3,1] 4 3 Yes 1 4 != 1 Yes [-1,1,3,4] 1
    4 1 [-1,1,3,4] 1 0 Yes -1 1 != -1 Yes [1,-1,3,4] 1
    5 1 [1,-1,3,4] -1 -2 No — No same 2
    6 2 [1,-1,3,4] 3 2 Yes 3 3 != 3 No same 3
    7 3 [1,-1,3,4] 4 3 Yes 4 Equal same 4
    exit 4 [1,-1,3,4] — — — — — — —

    Steps 2 aur 5 dekho — -1 ne guard trigger kiya aur i aage badh gaya. Bina guard ke step 2 par nums[-2] access hota aur array corrupt ho jaata.

    Scan pass on [1, -1, 3, 4]:

    i nums[i] i + 1 Match? Action
    0 1 1 Yes —
    1 -1 2 No return 2

    Answer 2. Sahi.

    Dry run — [7, 8, 9, 11, 12] (n = 5, expected 1)

    Placement: har value >= 7 > 5 = n, toh correct >= 6 >= n — har baar guard fail, i badhta jaata hai. Array unchanged, 5 iterations.

    Scan: nums[0] = 7 != 1 → return 1. Sahi.

    Dry run — [1, 2, 3] (n = 3, expected 4)

    Placement: har value already sahi jagah par → 3 iterations, no swaps. Scan: sab match. Loop khatam → line 12: return 3 + 1 = 4. Sahi.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har swap ek element permanently place karta hai (at most n swaps), plus n increments. Out-of-range values ek hi baar dekhe jaate hain.
    • Space: O(1). Array in-place modify hota hai. Agar caller ka array preserve karna ho toh copy chahiye — yeh trade-off mention karna chahiye.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty [] 1 Loops skip, return 0 + 1
    Single positive [1] 2 Scan clean → n+1
    Single non-positive [0] 1 correct = -1 → guard → scan mismatch
    All negatives [-1,-2,-3] 1 Sab guard par ruk jaate
    Perfect 1..n [1,2,3,4] 5 Line 12
    All duplicates [1,1,1] 2 Value comparison se terminate
    Huge values [10**9] 1 correct bahut bada → guard
    Mixed [0,-1,3,1] 2
    Contains n+1 [2,3,4] (n=3) 1 4 out of range

    Variations

    • Kth missing positive (LeetCode 1539) — Problem 5.7.
    • First missing non-negative — mapping correct = nums[i], answer i ya n.
    • Array read-only — cyclic sort possible nahi; O(n) space set, ya values ko in-place mark karne ke liye sign-flipping (jo bhi write hai). Read-only plus O(1) space plus O(n) time — is problem ke liye possible nahi hai aur yeh bolna sahi answer hai.
    • Negation marking version — pehle sab non-positive ko n+1 se replace karo, phir nums[abs(x)-1] ko negative mark karo. Same complexity, thoda alag flavour.
    • Sorted input — trivial O(n) scan.

    Interview answer: "The first thing to establish is the answer's range: with n elements, the answer has to be between one and n plus one. If the array holds exactly one through n, the answer is n plus one; otherwise some value in one through n is missing. That means everything outside that range — negatives, zero, and anything above n — is irrelevant and can be ignored.

    So I run a cyclic sort placing value v at index v minus one, then scan for the first index where the value isn't index plus one. If the scan finds nothing, I return n plus one.

    All the difficulty is in the swap guard. I check that the destination index is in bounds before comparing values, and the and short-circuits so the out-of-range case never dereferences. The lower bound check matters most: in Python a negative index doesn't raise, it silently wraps to the end of the array. Without that check the code produces wrong answers instead of crashing, which is much harder to catch.

    The else branch covers three different situations with one action — out-of-range value, already-correct value, and duplicate. In all three, the right move is to leave it and advance, and advancing is what guarantees termination.

    O(n) time by the usual argument that each swap permanently places an element, and O(1) space. The trade-off is that it mutates the input; if the array had to stay read-only I'd need O(n) space, and I'd say so — read-only plus O(1) space plus linear time isn't achievable here."

    Problem 5.7 — Find The First K Missing Positive Numbers¶

    Problem statement

    Unsorted array diya hai (koi bhi integers), aur ek number k. Sabse chhote k missing positive numbers lauta do.

    Input:  nums = [3, -1, 4, 5, 5], k = 3
Output: [1, 2, 6]
        (positives present: 3, 4, 5. Missing: 1, 2, 6, 7, ... -> pehle 3 chahiye)

Input:  nums = [2, 3, 4], k = 3
Output: [1, 5, 6]

Input:  nums = [-2, -3, 4], k = 2
Output: [1, 2]

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Set banao aur 1 se ginte jao.

    def k_missing_brute(nums, k):
    present = set(nums)                           # 1: O(n) space
    result = []                                   # 2
    candidate = 1                                 # 3: 1 se shuru
    while len(result) < k:                        # 4: jab tak k na mil jaayein
        if candidate not in present:              # 5: array mein nahi hai
            result.append(candidate)              # 6: missing
        candidate += 1                            # 7
    return result                                 # 8

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. set(nums) — O(1) lookups ke liye, O(n) space. 2-3. Init.
    2. while len(result) < k: — k par loop, array par nahi. Yeh important hai kyunki missing numbers array ke bahar bhi ho sakte hain (jaise [1,2,3] ke liye missing 4,5,6...). 5-7. Standard.
    3. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n + k + m) jahan m = kitne extra numbers scan karne pade; practically O(n + k). Space O(n) — set ki wajah se.

    Yeh solution bilkul theek hai aur interview mein acceptable bhi. Problem sirf space constraint hai.

    Isme problem kya hai

    O(n) extra space. Aur asli baat: yeh problem Problem 5.6 ka natural extension hai, aur interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap 5.6 ke solution ko generalise kar sakte ho ya nahi.

    The insight

    5.6 mein hum pehla gap dhoondh kar ruk jaate the. Yahan saare gaps chahiye — aur agar array ke andar k gaps nahi mile, toh n ke aage se continue karo.

    Do phases:

    1. Array ke andar ke gaps: cyclic sort chalao, phir scan karo. Har mismatch position i par i + 1 ek missing number hai.
    2. Array ke bahar ke numbers: agar abhi bhi k nahi mile, toh n + 1, n + 2, ... continue karo. Lekin ek catch hai — un numbers mein se kuch array mein already ho sakte hain! Jaise [2, 3, 4], n = 3. Placement ke baad array [?, 2, 3] type hoga aur 4 kahin extra slot mein pada hoga. Toh 4 ko skip karna padega.

    Catch ka solution: jo values scan ke dauraan "galat jagah" par mili thi, unhe ek chhote set mein rakho. Woh set at most k size ka hai (kyunki hum k gaps ke baad ruk jaate hain), toh O(k) space — jo O(n) se accha hai jab k << n.

    Optimal solution

    def find_first_k_missing_positive(nums, k):
    n = len(nums)                                 # 1
    i = 0                                         # 2
    while i < n:                                  # 3: PHASE 1 -- cyclic sort placement
        correct = nums[i] - 1                     # 4
        if 0 <= correct < n and nums[i] != nums[correct]:   # 5: 5.6 wala hi guard
            nums[i], nums[correct] = nums[correct], nums[i] # 6
        else:                                     # 7
            i += 1                                # 8

    missing = []                                  # 9: output
    extras = set()                                # 10: array ke andar mile "bahar ke" numbers
    for i in range(n):                            # 11: PHASE 2 -- array ke andar ke gaps
        if len(missing) == k:                     # 12: k mil gaye -> aur nahi chahiye
            break                                 # 13
        if nums[i] != i + 1:                      # 14: gap
            missing.append(i + 1)                 # 15: yeh number missing hai
            extras.add(nums[i])                   # 16: jo yahan pada hai woh "extra" hai
    candidate = n + 1                             # 17: PHASE 3 -- array ke aage
    while len(missing) < k:                       # 18: abhi bhi kam hain
        if candidate not in extras:               # 19: yeh number array mein toh nahi tha?
            missing.append(candidate)             # 20
        candidate += 1                            # 21
    return missing                                # 22

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-8. Problem 5.6 ka bilkul same placement pass, guard sameta. Yeh reuse deliberate hai. 9. missing = []. 10. extras = set() — yeh set kyun chahiye, iska poora reason phase 3 mein hai. Jab hum n+1, n+2, ... par jaate hain, toh un values mein se kuch array mein present ho sakti hain (out-of-range positives jo place nahi ho paaye). Unhe skip karna padega, warna galat answer aayega. 11. for i in range(n):. 12-13. if len(missing) == k: break — early exit. Zaroori nahi hai correctness ke liye (extra entries baad mein trim kar sakte the), lekin extras ko chhota rakhta hai (O(k) instead of O(n)) — jo poore solution ka space advantage hai. 14. if nums[i] != i + 1: — mismatch. 15. missing.append(i + 1) — 5.3 wali hi baat: i + 1 missing hai, nums[i] nahi. 16. extras.add(nums[i]) — aur jo nums[i] yahan pada hai woh ya toh duplicate hai ya n se bada positive. Dono cases mein woh "phase 3 mein skip karne wala candidate" ban sakta hai. Negatives bhi is set mein aa jaayenge lekin woh phase 3 ke candidates (> n) se kabhi match nahi karenge, toh harmless hain. 17. candidate = n + 1 — phase 3 n + 1 se shuru hota hai, 1 se nahi, kyunki 1..n ka poora hisaab phase 2 mein ho chuka hai. 18. while len(missing) < k: — jab tak k na mil jaayein. 19. if candidate not in extras: — yehi woh check hai jiske liye set banaya. Example [2,3,4], n=3: phase 2 mein missing=[1], extras={4}. Phase 3: candidate=4 → 4 in extras → skip. candidate=5 → append. candidate=6 → append. Result [1,5,6]. Sahi. Bina extras ke [1,4,5] aata — galat, kyunki 4 array mein hai. 20-21. Append aur aage. 22. Return.

    Termination guarantee: phase 3 ka while hamesha khatam hoga kyunki extras finite hai (at most k entries) toh at most k skips ke baad naye numbers milte rahenge.

    Dry run — nums = [3, -1, 4, 5, 5], k = 3 (expected [1, 2, 6]), n = 5

    Phase 1 (placement):

    Step i nums nums[i] correct 0<=c<n? nums[correct] Swap? nums after i after
    1 0 [3,-1,4,5,5] 3 2 Yes 4 Yes [4,-1,3,5,5] 0
    2 0 [4,-1,3,5,5] 4 3 Yes 5 Yes [5,-1,3,4,5] 0
    3 0 [5,-1,3,4,5] 5 4 Yes 5 5 != 5 No same 1
    4 1 [5,-1,3,4,5] -1 -2 No — No same 2
    5 2 [5,-1,3,4,5] 3 2 Yes 3 Equal same 3
    6 3 same 4 3 Yes 4 Equal same 4
    7 4 same 5 4 Yes 5 Equal same 5
    exit 5 [5,-1,3,4,5] — — — — — — —

    Phase 2 (scan for gaps):

    i nums[i] i+1 Match? missing extras len(missing)==k?
    0 5 1 No [1] {5} 1 < 3, continue
    1 -1 2 No [1,2] {5,-1} 2 < 3, continue
    2 3 3 Yes [1,2] {5,-1} continue
    3 4 4 Yes same same continue
    4 5 5 Yes same same loop khatam

    Phase 3:

    candidate in extras? Action missing len < k?
    6 No append [1,2,6] 3 < 3 False → exit

    Result [1, 2, 6]. Sahi.

    Dry run — nums = [2, 3, 4], k = 3 (expected [1, 5, 6]), n = 3

    Phase 1:

    Step i nums nums[i] correct 0<=c<3? nums[correct] Swap? nums after i
    1 0 [2,3,4] 2 1 Yes 3 Yes [3,2,4] 0
    2 0 [3,2,4] 3 2 Yes 4 Yes [4,2,3] 0
    3 0 [4,2,3] 4 3 No (3 < 3 False) — No same 1
    4 1 [4,2,3] 2 1 Yes 2 Equal same 2
    5 2 [4,2,3] 3 2 Yes 3 Equal same 3

    Phase 2:

    i nums[i] i+1 Match? missing extras
    0 4 1 No [1] {4}
    1 2 2 Yes [1] {4}
    2 3 3 Yes [1] {4}

    Phase 3:

    candidate in extras? Action missing
    4 Yes skip [1]
    5 No append [1,5]
    6 No append [1,5,6] → len == k → exit

    Result [1, 5, 6]. Sahi.

    Yeh dusra dry run hi extras set ka poora justification hai. Bina uske candidate = 4 append ho jaata aur answer [1,4,5] aata — galat, kyunki 4 array mein maujood hai.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n + k). Placement O(n), scan O(n) (early break se aur kam), phase 3 at most O(k + |extras|) = O(k) iterations.
    • Space: O(k). extras set at most k entries rakhta hai (kyunki hum k missing milte hi break kar dete hain), plus output O(k).

    Yeh brute force ke O(n) space se better hai jab k << n. Agar k bada ho toh dono barabar. Yeh nuance interview mein bolna chahiye — "O(k) space, which beats O(n) when k is small, and is the same order otherwise."

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty array [], k=3 [1,2,3] Phase 1/2 skip, phase 3 se sab
    All negatives [-1,-2], k=2 [1,2] Guard se sab skip, phase 2 dono gaps
    Perfect 1..n [1,2,3], k=2 [4,5] Phase 2 clean, phase 3 se dono
    k = 0 [1,2], k=0 [] Phase 2 mein turant break, phase 3 skip
    Duplicates [1,1,1], k=2 [2,3] Phase 2 se dono
    Big out-of-range [1000], k=2 [1,2] extras={1000}, kabhi match nahi
    Extras exactly at n+1 [2,3,4], k=1 [1] Phase 3 chalta hi nahi
    k bigger than gaps [1], k=5 [2,3,4,5,6] Phase 3 se paanch

    Variations

    • Kth Missing Positive Number (LeetCode 1539) — array sorted hai; tab binary search se O(log n). Section 11 mein.
    • Sirf kth missing chahiye, saare nahi — same code, missing[-1] return karo (ya missing[k-1]).
    • Kth missing non-negative — mapping shift karo.
    • Missing numbers in a range [a, b] — offset subtract karke same technique.
    • Streaming version — cyclic sort possible nahi; bitset ya sorted structure chahiye.

    Interview answer: "This generalises the first-missing-positive problem. There I stopped at the first gap; here I need k gaps, and if the array doesn't contain k of them I have to keep counting past the end of the array.

    So: cyclic sort placement with the same in-bounds guard, then scan for mismatches — each mismatched index i contributes i plus one as a missing number.

    The part that's easy to get wrong is continuing past n. Once I run out of gaps inside the array, I start at n plus one — but some of those values might actually be present, sitting in the array as out-of-range positives that couldn't be placed. If I don't skip them I'll report a number that's really there.

    So while scanning, I also record the value that was occupying each mismatched slot into a small set. Those are exactly the candidates I need to skip later. Because I stop as soon as I have k missing numbers, that set holds at most k entries, so the extra space is O(k) rather than O(n).

    Concretely: for the array two, three, four with k equal to three, the answer is one, five, six — not one, four, five — because four is present. That set is the only thing preventing that bug.

    O(n plus k) time, O(k) space. That beats the straightforward hash-set solution when k is small relative to n, and matches it otherwise."

    Aur cyclic sort problems — practice list¶

    1. Cyclic Sort (base pattern) — Problem 5.1. Pehle yeh, phir baaki.
    2. Missing Number (LeetCode 268) — Problem 5.2. Zaroor karo.
    3. Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array (448) — Problem 5.3.
    4. Find All Duplicates in an Array (442) — Problem 5.4.
    5. Set Mismatch (645) — Problem 5.5.
    6. First Missing Positive (41) — Problem 5.6. Sabse important, "hard" tag ke saath.
    7. Kth Missing Positive Number (1539) — Problem 5.7 (sorted version binary search se).
    8. Find the Duplicate Number (287) — cyclic sort se bhi hota hai agar mutation allowed; warna Floyd (Problem 3.6).
    9. Couples Holding Hands (765) — cyclic sort ka swap-counting variant.
    10. Minimum Number of Swaps to Sort an Array — same swap counting.
    11. Missing Ranges (163) — sorted array, gaps as ranges.
    12. Find Missing Observations (2028) — arithmetic, cyclic sort nahi, lekin same "expected vs actual" soch.

    Ek line mein poore pattern ka summary: Placement pass ek hi hai; sirf scan pass badalta hai. i + 1 collect karo toh missing milte hain, nums[i] collect karo toh duplicates.

    6. In Place Linked List Reversal¶

    Recognition signals — aap linked list reversal dekh rahe ho jab problem bole¶

    • "reverse the linked list" — obviously.
    • "reverse the sub-list between position m and n", "reverse every k nodes", "reverse alternating groups".
    • "rotate the list by k" — reversal ka cousin (ya cut-and-reattach).
    • "swap nodes in pairs" — k = 2 ka special case.
    • "palindrome linked list", "reorder list" — reversal ek sub-step ke roop mein (Section 3 mein dekh chuke).
    • "add two numbers where digits are in forward order" — reverse karo, add karo, wapas reverse karo.
    • Constraint bole "O(1) space" aur aapka instinct array/stack use karne ka ho.

    Yeh pattern kaam kyun karta hai — asli intuition¶

    Linked list mein reversal ka matlab hai: har node ka next ulta kar do. A -> B -> C ko A <- B <- C banana hai, aur phir head ko C bata dena hai.

    Dikkat ek hi hai: jaise hi aap B.next = A karte ho, aapne C ka raasta kho diya — kyunki C tak pahunchne ka ekmatra tarika B.next tha.

    Iska hal ek hi hai aur hamesha wahi hai: next ko badalne se PEHLE agla node ek temporary variable mein bacha lo.

    Isliye har reversal loop mein teen pointers hote hain:

    prev  ->  current  ->  next_node
(reversed part ka head)  (jise abhi ulta karna hai)  (jahan aage jaana hai)

    Aur loop body hamesha yehi chaar lines hoti hain, isi order mein:

    next_node = current.next     # 1. bacha lo (warna kho jaayega)
current.next = prev          # 2. ulta karo (yeh line hi asli reversal hai)
prev = current               # 3. prev ko aage sarkao
current = next_node          # 4. current ko aage sarkao

    Yeh chaar lines ratne layak hain — na isliye ki ratna acha hai, balki isliye ki poore section ki har problem inhi chaar lines ke aas paas ghoomti hai. Order badalna hamesha bug deta hai:

    Agar aap yeh karo Kya tootega
    Line 1 ko line 2 ke baad likho next_node galat value (prev) le lega, baaki list hamesha ke liye gum
    Line 3 aur 4 swap kar do prev ko next_node mil jaayega, arrow galat node par lagega
    prev ko head se initialise karo Original head ka next kabhi None nahi hoga → cycle ban jaayega

    Dummy node — yeh trick har list problem mein kaam aati hai¶

    Bahut si problems mein head khud badal jaata hai, aur "agar head badla toh alag code" wali if conditions bahut ho jaati hain. Iska standard hal: ek fake node banao jo asli head se pehle baithe.

    dummy = ListNode(0)          # value matter nahi karti
dummy.next = head            # ab dummy hamesha exist karta hai
# ... jo bhi manipulation karni hai ...
return dummy.next            # asli (possibly naya) head

    Fayda: ab "pehla node" ka koi special case nahi bacha — har node ka ek prev hai (dummy sabse pehle wale ka prev hai). Yeh code se 5-10 lines ki if conditions hata deta hai. Interview mein dummy node use karna maturity ka signal hai.

    Template code¶

    class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, nxt=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = nxt


def reverse(head):
    """Poori list reverse -- yeh baaki sabki base hai."""
    prev = None                        # reversed part ka head; None isliye ki purana head naya tail banega
    current = head                     # jise abhi process karna hai
    while current:                     # jab tak node bacha hai
        next_node = current.next       # 1. bacha lo
        current.next = prev            # 2. arrow ulta
        prev = current                 # 3. prev aage
        current = next_node            # 4. current aage
    return prev                        # loop ke baad current = None, prev = naya head


def reverse_k_nodes(head, k):
    """Exactly k nodes reverse karo, (naya_head, naya_tail, agla_node) lauta do."""
    prev = None
    current = head
    count = 0
    while current and count < k:       # ab count-bounded hai, poori list nahi
        next_node = current.next
        current.next = prev
        prev = current
        current = next_node
        count += 1
    return prev, head, current         # prev = naya head, head = naya tail, current = k ke baad wala

    Template ka core idea: reverse_k_nodes teen cheezein lautata hai kyunki reversal ke baad aapko teen references chahiye hote hain — naya head (taaki pichhle segment se jod sako), naya tail (taaki agle segment se jod sako), aur agla unprocessed node (taaki loop continue kar sako). head variable reversal ke baad automatically naya tail ban jaata hai, jo ek chhoti si elegance hai.

    Problem 6.1 — Reverse A Linked List¶

    Problem statement

    Linked list ka head diya hai. Poori list reverse karke naya head lauta do.

    Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> None
Output: 5 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> None

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Saari values array mein nikaalo, reverse karo, aur wapas likh do.

    def reverse_brute(head):
    values = []                        # 1: saari values
    current = head                     # 2
    while current:                     # 3: pehla pass -- collect
        values.append(current.val)     # 4
        current = current.next         # 5
    current = head                     # 6: reset
    for v in reversed(values):         # 7: dusra pass -- write back ulte order mein
        current.val = v                # 8: NODE ki value badal rahe hain
        current = current.next         # 9
    return head                        # 10: head same rehta hai (values badli, structure nahi)

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. Values collect. Nodes nahi, values — kyunki hum structure nahi badal rahe. 6. Reset to head. 7. reversed(values) — ek iterator deta hai, naya list nahi banata (memory-friendly). 8-9. Values overwrite. 10. return head — head badalta hi nahi is approach mein, kyunki nodes wahin hain, sirf unke andar ka data badla.

    Complexity: Time O(n) (do passes), Space O(n) — values array.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Do dikkatein. Pehli, O(n) space. Dusri, aur zyada important: yeh nodes ko rewire nahi karta, sirf values copy karta hai. Agar nodes mein bade objects hon, ya agar koi aur code purane node references pakde baitha ho, toh yeh galat behaviour deta hai. Aur agar list immutable values (jaise frozen objects) rakhti ho toh yeh chalega hi nahi.

    Interviewer almost hamesha "reverse the links, not the values" specify karta hai.

    The insight

    Har node ke liye ek hi kaam karna hai: uska next ulta kar do. Poori list ko ek saath sochne ki zaroorat nahi — ek node par focus karo.

    Lekin current.next = prev karte hi aage ka raasta gum ho jaayega. Toh pehle bacha lo, phir todo. Yeh ek line ka insight hai aur poore section par apply hota hai.

    Optimal solution

    def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None                        # 1: reversed portion ka head; shuru mein khaali
    current = head                     # 2: jise abhi ulta karna hai
    while current is not None:         # 3: jab tak koi node bacha hai
        next_node = current.next       # 4: BACHA LO -- line 5 ise destroy kar degi
        current.next = prev            # 5: ARROW ULTA -- asli kaam yehi hai
        prev = current                 # 6: prev ab is node par
        current = next_node            # 7: current bachaye hue node par
    return prev                        # 8: current None hai, prev aakhri node = naya head

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. prev = None — None hi kyun? Kyunki original list ka pehla node reversal ke baad aakhri node banega, aur aakhri node ka next None hona chahiye. Line 5 pehli iteration mein head.next = None set karti hai — exactly yehi chahiye. Agar prev = head se initialise karte toh head.next = head ho jaata → self loop → infinite list.
    2. current = head.
    3. while current is not None: — while current: bhi bilkul same hai (None falsy hai). is not None explicit aur safe hai.
    4. next_node = current.next — yeh line line 5 se pehle honi hi chahiye. Agar swap kar dein toh next_node = current.next par current.next already prev ho chuka hoga, aur baaki poori list unreachable ho jaayegi — memory leak (Python mein garbage collect ho jaayegi, C++ mein leak).
    5. current.next = prev — poore algorithm ki ekmatra "asli" line. Baaki teen lines bookkeeping hain.
    6. prev = current — current ab reversed part ka naya head hai.
    7. current = next_node — saved reference se aage. Lines 6 aur 7 ka order matter karta hai. Ulta karein (current = next_node pehle) toh line 6 prev = current galat node (agla wala) le lega.
    8. return prev — loop exit par current None hai, aur prev woh aakhri node hai jise process kiya — yaani original tail, jo ab naya head hai. return current likhna None return karega — yeh common typo hai.

    Recursive version (interviewer aksar maangta hai):

    def reverse_recursive(head):
    if head is None or head.next is None:   # 9: base case -- 0 ya 1 node
        return head                         # 10: wahi head naya head hai
    new_head = reverse_recursive(head.next) # 11: baaki list reverse karo (trust the recursion)
    head.next.next = head                   # 12: apne aage wale ka next apne aap par lagao
    head.next = None                        # 13: apna next todo -- warna cycle
    return new_head                         # 14: naya head neeche se propagate hota hai

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    9-10. Do base cases ek saath. head is None empty list ke liye, head.next is None single node ke liye. Single node ka case zaroori hai kyunki wahi "naya head" ban kar upar propagate hota hai. 11. new_head = reverse_recursive(head.next) — recursion par bharosa karo. Yeh call head ke aage wali poori list reverse kar chuki hogi, aur uska naya head lauta degi. Isko "kaise kiya" sochna mana hai — bas maan lo ho gaya. 12. head.next.next = head — yeh line samajhna zaroori hai. Recursion ke baad head.next abhi bhi purane agle node ko point karta hai (recursion ne use nahi badla — usne uske aage waalon ko badla). Aur woh node ab reversed sub-list ka tail hai. Toh uske next ko head par lagana matlab "mujhe apne peeche jodo." Example: 1 -> 2 -> 3. reverse(2->3) ke baad list 3 -> 2 hai aur head.next abhi bhi 2 hai. head.next.next = head matlab 2.next = 1 → 3 -> 2 -> 1. Sahi. 13. head.next = None — agar yeh line hata do toh cycle ban jaayega. Upar ke example mein 1.next abhi bhi 2 hai, aur 2.next ab 1 hai → 1 <-> 2 infinite loop. None set karna 1 ko naya tail banata hai. 14. return new_head — head return karna galat hoga. Naya head sabse gehri call se aata hai aur bina badle upar tak propagate hota hai.

    Recursive version ka trade-off: O(n) space call stack ke liye, aur Python mein 1000+ nodes par RecursionError. Iterative version production-safe hai. Interview mein dono likh dena aur trade-off bolna best hai.

    Dry run — iterative — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> None (nodes A, B, C)

    Iter prev (before) current (before) next_node After current.next = prev prev (after) current (after) List state
    init None A — — None A A->B->C->None
    1 None A B A.next = None A B A->None, B->C->None
    2 A B C B.next = A B C B->A->None, C->None
    3 B C None C.next = B C None C->B->A->None
    exit C None — — — — return C

    Har row mein dekho — list do tukdon mein hai: reversed part (prev se shuru) aur baaki (current se shuru). Har iteration ek node ko pehle tukde mein transfer karti hai.

    Dry run — recursive — same list A(1) -> B(2) -> C(3)

    Call head Action Return
    rev(A) A A.next = B, recurse on B (pending)
    rev(B) B B.next = C, recurse on C (pending)
    rev(C) C C.next is None → base case C
    back in rev(B) B new_head = C. B.next.next = B → C.next = B. B.next = None C
    back in rev(A) A new_head = C. A.next.next = A → B.next = A. A.next = None C

    Final: C -> B -> A -> None. Head C. Sahi.

    Dhyaan do ki new_head (= C) har level par bina badle wapas jaata hai — yeh line 14 ka poora point hai.

    Complexity

    Iterative: - Time: O(n). Har node exactly ek baar visit. - Space: O(1). Teen pointers.

    Recursive: - Time: O(n). - Space: O(n) — call stack n deep jaata hai.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None None Loop chalta nahi, prev = None return
    Single node A A Ek iteration: A.next = None, return A
    Two nodes A->B B->A Do iterations
    All same values 1->1->1 1->1->1 Structure ulti, values same dikhti
    Very long (10^5) — reversed Iterative fine; recursive RecursionError
    List with cycle — Infinite loop Function acyclic maanta hai

    Variations

    • Reverse a sub-list — Problem 6.2.
    • Reverse in groups of k — Problem 6.3.
    • Check palindrome — reverse second half (Problem 3.5).
    • Recursive version — upar.
    • Doubly linked list reverse — prev aur next dono swap karne hain har node par.
    • Reverse karo lekin original preserve karo — naye nodes banao (O(n) space).

    Interview answer: "The trap is that the moment I set current.next to point backwards, I lose the rest of the list — because current.next was my only way forward. So the loop body is always four steps in a fixed order: save the next node, flip the pointer, advance prev, advance current.

    I initialise prev to None specifically because the original head becomes the new tail, and a tail's next must be None. Initialising prev to head instead would make the head point at itself and create a cycle.

    At the end, current is None and prev is the last node I processed, which is the new head — so I return prev, not current.

    O(n) time, O(1) space.

    I can also write it recursively: recurse to the end, then on the way back set head.next.next to head and head.next to None. The second assignment is essential — without it you get a two-node cycle. But that version is O(n) stack space and would hit Python's recursion limit around a thousand nodes, so for production I'd ship the iterative one.

    One more thing I'd confirm: whether they want the links reversed or just the values. Copying values into an array and writing them back reversed is easier, but it's O(n) space and it doesn't actually restructure the list, which matters if anything else holds references to these nodes."

    Problem 6.2 — Reverse A Sub-List¶

    Problem statement

    Linked list aur do positions left aur right diye hain (1-indexed). Sirf left se right tak ke nodes reverse karo, baaki list waisi ki waisi rahe. Ek hi pass mein karo.

    Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, left = 2, right = 4
Output: 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 5

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3, left = 1, right = 3
Output: 3 -> 2 -> 1

Input:  5, left = 1, right = 1
Output: 5

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Sub-list ke values nikaalo, reverse karo, wapas likh do.

    def reverse_sub_brute(head, left, right):
    values = []                                   # 1: sub-list ki values
    current = head                                # 2
    pos = 1                                       # 3: 1-INDEXED position counter
    while current:                                # 4: pehla pass -- collect
        if left <= pos <= right:                  # 5: range ke andar hai?
            values.append(current.val)            # 6
        current = current.next                    # 7
        pos += 1                                  # 8
    values.reverse()                              # 9: in-place reverse, O(k)
    current = head                                # 10: reset
    pos = 1                                       # 11
    idx = 0                                       # 12: values array mein position
    while current:                                # 13: dusra pass -- write back
        if left <= pos <= right:                  # 14
            current.val = values[idx]             # 15
            idx += 1                              # 16
        current = current.next                    # 17
        pos += 1                                  # 18
    return head                                   # 19

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-8. Collect phase. Line 3 pos = 1 — problem 1-indexed hai, aur yeh sabse common off-by-one source hai. Line 5 ka chained comparison left <= pos <= right Python mein valid hai aur left <= pos and pos <= right ke barabar. 9. values.reverse() — in-place, values[::-1] se ek copy bachti hai. 10-18. Write-back phase. 19. return head — head kabhi badalta nahi kyunki sirf values badli.

    Complexity: Time O(n) (do passes), Space O(k) jahan k = sub-list ki length. Aur phir wahi values-vs-links wala objection.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Do passes, O(k) space, aur links reverse nahi hote. Problem specifically one pass, O(1) space, links reverse maangti hai.

    The insight

    Do hisse hain:

    1. Reversal khud — Problem 6.1 wala hi loop, bas right - left + 1 baar chalao (poori list par nahi).

    2. Reconnection — yeh asli mushkil hai. Reversal ke baad char nodes matter karte hain:

    3. prev_left — left se ek pehle wala node. Uska next reversed part ke naye head par lagega.
    4. left_node — original left wala node. Reversal ke baad yeh sub-list ka tail ban jaata hai. Uska next right ke baad wale node par lagega.
    5. right_node — original right wala node = reversed part ka naya head.
    6. after_right — right ke baad wala node.

    Aur ek edge case jo sab jagah dikkat karta hai: agar left == 1 toh prev_left exist hi nahi karta (head se pehle koi node nahi). Iska hal dummy node hai — ek fake node head se pehle laga do, ab prev_left hamesha exist karta hai. Dummy node ka poora justification yahi hai.

    Optimal solution

    def reverse_between(head, left, right):
    if head is None or left == right:             # 1: kuch reverse karna hi nahi
        return head                               # 2

    dummy = ListNode(0)                           # 3: fake node -- left==1 ka case handle karta hai
    dummy.next = head                             # 4: asli list dummy ke peeche
    prev_left = dummy                             # 5: `left` se ek pehle wala node

    for _ in range(left - 1):                     # 6: prev_left ko sahi jagah le jao
        prev_left = prev_left.next                # 7

    left_node = prev_left.next                    # 8: reversal ke baad yeh TAIL banega
    prev = None                                   # 9: standard reversal ke teen pointers
    current = left_node                           # 10
    for _ in range(right - left + 1):             # 11: exactly itne nodes reverse karne hain
        next_node = current.next                  # 12: bacha lo
        current.next = prev                       # 13: arrow ulta
        prev = current                            # 14
        current = next_node                       # 15
    # ab: prev = reversed part ka naya head, current = right ke baad wala node

    prev_left.next = prev                         # 16: pehla jod -- bahar se andar
    left_node.next = current                      # 17: dusra jod -- andar se bahar
    return dummy.next                             # 18: dummy ka next hi asli head hai

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guard. left == right matlab ek hi node reverse karna hai, jo no-op hai. Yeh guard na hota toh code phir bhi sahi chalta (loop ek baar chalta aur kuch nahi badalta), lekin explicit guard intent saaf karta hai aur ek chhota sa optimisation hai. 3. dummy = ListNode(0) — value irrelevant hai. Iska ekmatra kaam left == 1 case ko normal banana hai. 4. dummy.next = head. 5. prev_left = dummy — shuruaat. 6. for _ in range(left - 1): — left - 1 steps kyun? prev_left ko position left - 1 par pahunchna hai. dummy position 0 par hai (imaginary), toh left - 1 steps se woh position left - 1 par pahunch jaata hai. Check: left = 2 → 1 step → prev_left = node 1. Sahi. left = 1 → 0 steps → prev_left = dummy. Sahi — yehi dummy ka fayda hai. 7. prev_left = prev_left.next. 8. left_node = prev_left.next — yeh reference bachana zaroori hai kyunki reversal ke baad yeh node sub-list ka tail ban jaayega aur uska next set karna hoga (line 17). Reversal ke dauraan ise track karne ka koi aur tarika nahi hai. 9-10. Reversal pointers. prev = None — reversal ke baad left_node.next None ho jaayega, jise line 17 theek kar degi. 11. for _ in range(right - left + 1): — +1 inclusive count ke liye. left=2, right=4 → 4-2+1 = 3 nodes (2, 3, 4). Bina +1 ke 2 nodes reverse hote — classic off-by-one. for yahan safe hai (cyclic sort ke while wali baat yahan nahi) kyunki hum exact count jaante hain aur conditional advance nahi hai. 12-15. Standard 6.1 wala loop. 16. prev_left.next = prev — reversal ke baad prev reversed part ka head hai (original right_node). prev_left ko usse jodo. 17. left_node.next = current — reversal ke baad current right ke baad wala node hai (ya None agar right last node tha). left_node ab tail hai, use aage se jodo. Lines 16 aur 17 ka order matter nahi karta (dono independent assignments hain), lekin dono chahiye. Ek bhool jaana list todta hai. 18. return dummy.next — head return karna galat ho sakta hai. Agar left == 1 toh original head ab tail hai, naya head koi aur hai. dummy.next hamesha sahi hai.

    Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, left = 2, right = 4 (nodes A,B,C,D,E)

    Setup: dummy -> A -> B -> C -> D -> E.

    Line 6-7: range(2 - 1) = range(1) → 1 step → prev_left = A. Line 8: left_node = A.next = B. Line 11: range(4 - 2 + 1) = range(3) → 3 iterations.

    Reversal loop:

    Iter prev current next_node After current.next = prev prev after current after
    init None B — — None B
    1 None B C B.next = None B C
    2 B C D C.next = B C D
    3 C D E D.next = C D E
    exit D E — — — —

    Ab state: dummy -> A -> B -> None (A ka next abhi bhi B), aur alag se D -> C -> B chain, aur E -> None. Actually precisely: A.next = B, B.next = None, C.next = B, D.next = C, E.next = None. prev = D, current = E.

    Line 16: prev_left.next = prev → A.next = D. Line 17: left_node.next = current → B.next = E.

    Final: A(1) -> D(4) -> C(3) -> B(2) -> E(5) = 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 5. Sahi.

    Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3, left = 1, right = 3 (A,B,C) — dummy ka test

    Setup: dummy -> A -> B -> C. Line 6: range(1 - 1) = range(0) → 0 steps → prev_left = dummy. Yahi dummy ka poora point hai — bina dummy ke prev_left None hota aur line 16 crash karti. Line 8: left_node = dummy.next = A. Line 11: range(3 - 1 + 1) = range(3).

    Iter prev current next_node Assignment prev after current after
    1 None A B A.next = None A B
    2 A B C B.next = A B C
    3 B C None C.next = B C None

    Line 16: dummy.next = C. Line 17: A.next = None. Line 18: return dummy.next = C.

    Final: C(3) -> B(2) -> A(1) -> None = 3 -> 2 -> 1. Sahi, aur head bhi badal gaya — jo return head likhne par galat hota.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). left - 1 steps traversal, plus right - left + 1 steps reversal. Worst case (left=1, right=n) → O(n). Ek hi pass — koi node do baar visit nahi hota.
    • Space: O(1). Dummy ek node hai (constant), baaki sab pointers.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    left == right 1->2->3, 2, 2 1->2->3 Guard line 1
    Poori list 1->2->3, 1, 3 3->2->1 Dummy handle karta hai
    Head se shuru 1->2->3, 1, 2 2->1->3 prev_left = dummy
    Tail tak 1->2->3, 2, 3 1->3->2 current = None line 17 mein
    Single node 1, 1, 1 1 Guard
    Two nodes 1->2, 1, 2 2->1
    Empty None, 1, 1 None Guard
    Invalid range (left > right) — Undefined Clarify karo — code range negative par 0 iterations karega

    Variations

    • Reverse every k nodes — Problem 6.3.
    • Reverse alternating k nodes — Problem 6.4.
    • Positions ki jagah values se range — pehle nodes dhoondo, phir wahi logic.
    • Recursive version — left/right decrement karke; likhna mushkil aur padhna aur mushkil.
    • Reverse nodes in even-length groups (LeetCode 2074) — same skill, alag grouping rule.

    Interview answer: "There are two halves to this: the reversal itself, which is the standard four-line loop but bounded to right minus left plus one iterations rather than the whole list; and the reconnection, which is where the actual difficulty is.

    After reversing, four nodes matter. The node before the sub-list needs to point at the new head of the reversed part. And the original left node — which is now the tail of the reversed part — needs to point at whatever came after right. So I save a reference to the left node before reversing, because I have no way to find it afterwards.

    The awkward case is left equals one, where there is no node before the sub-list. I handle that with a dummy node in front of the head. Then 'the node before' always exists, the loop that walks to it works uniformly, and I return dummy.next at the end — which is important, because when left is one the original head is no longer the head.

    Two off-by-ones to watch: I walk left minus one steps to reach the predecessor, and I reverse right minus left plus one nodes — the plus one because the range is inclusive.

    One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space."

    Problem 6.3 — Reverse Every K-Element Sub-List¶

    Problem statement

    Linked list aur ek number k diya hai. Har k consecutive nodes ke group ko reverse karo. Agar aakhir mein k se kam nodes bachein, unhe waise hi rehne do.

    Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8, k = 3
Output: 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 7 -> 8
        (7, 8 bache -- sirf 2 nodes, k se kam, toh unchanged)

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 2
Output: 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3, k = 1
Output: 1 -> 2 -> 3    (k=1 matlab kuch nahi badalta)

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Values array mein nikaalo, chunks mein reverse karo, wapas likho.

    def reverse_k_brute(head, k):
    values = []                                   # 1: saari values
    current = head                                # 2
    while current:                                # 3
        values.append(current.val)                # 4
        current = current.next                    # 5
    for start in range(0, len(values), k):        # 6: har k-size chunk ka start index
        if start + k <= len(values):              # 7: poora group hai? (partial skip karna hai)
            values[start:start + k] = reversed(values[start:start + k])   # 8: slice reverse
    current = head                                # 9: write back
    for v in values:                              # 10
        current.val = v                           # 11
        current = current.next                    # 12
    return head                                   # 13

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. Collect. 6. range(0, len(values), k) — step k se chunk starts milte hain: 0, k, 2k, ... 7. if start + k <= len(values): — partial group skip. Bina is check ke aakhri adhoora group bhi reverse ho jaata, jo problem ke against hai. 8. values[start:start+k] = reversed(...) — slice assignment. Right side ek iterator hai; Python use consume karke slice replace kar deta hai. 9-12. Write back. 13. Return head (badalta nahi).

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n). Aur phir wahi values-vs-links objection.

    Isme problem kya hai

    O(n) space, aur links reverse nahi hote. Problem O(1) space maangti hai.

    The insight

    Problem 6.2 ko baar baar chalana hai, har group par. Lekin do naye challenges hain:

    1. Har group ke baad reconnection. Group i ka tail group i+1 ke naye head se judna chahiye. Toh har iteration mein "pichhle group ka tail" yaad rakhna padta hai.

    2. Partial group detect karna — reverse karne se PEHLE. Kyunki agar aapne reverse kar diya aur phir pata chala ki group adhoora tha, toh undo karna padega. Solution: pehle ginno ki k nodes hain ya nahi, tabhi reverse karo.

    Aur dummy node phir se chahiye, kyunki pehla group reverse hone se head badal jaata hai.

    Optimal solution

    def reverse_k_group(head, k):
    if head is None or k <= 1:                    # 1: k=1 ya khaali -> kuch nahi karna
        return head                               # 2

    dummy = ListNode(0)                           # 3: head badalne wala hai
    dummy.next = head                             # 4
    group_prev = dummy                            # 5: pichhle group ka TAIL (ya dummy)

    while True:                                   # 6: har group ke liye
        # STEP 1: check karo ki k nodes bache hain ya nahi
        kth = group_prev                          # 7: group_prev se k steps chal kar
        for _ in range(k):                        # 8
            kth = kth.next                        # 9
            if kth is None:                       # 10: k nodes nahi hain
                return dummy.next                 # 11: bache hue nodes as-is chhod do

        group_next = kth.next                     # 12: group ke BAAD wala node

        # STEP 2: group ko reverse karo
        prev = group_next                         # 13: CHALAAKI -- None se nahi, group_next se
        current = group_prev.next                 # 14: group ka pehla node
        while current is not group_next:          # 15: group ke andar tak
            next_node = current.next              # 16: bacha lo
            current.next = prev                   # 17: arrow ulta
            prev = current                        # 18
            current = next_node                   # 19

        # STEP 3: reconnect
        new_group_prev = group_prev.next          # 20: reversal se PEHLE yeh head tha, ab TAIL hai
        group_prev.next = kth                     # 21: pichhla group naye head (kth) se jodo
        group_prev = new_group_prev               # 22: agle round ke liye tail yaad rakho

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guards. k <= 1 — k=1 matlab har group ek node ka, reversal no-op. k=0 ya negative invalid hai, guard crash se bachaata. 3-4. Dummy, kyunki pehla group reverse hone par head badal jaayega. 5. group_prev = dummy — poore algorithm ka state variable. Yeh hamesha "abhi tak process ho chuke hisse ka aakhri node" hota hai. 6. while True: — exit line 11 se hota hai (jab k nodes na bachein). 7-11. Step 1 — pehle ginno, phir reverse karo. - kth = group_prev, phir k steps. - if kth is None: return dummy.next — partial group mila, aur humne use chhua tak nahi. Yeh design decision hi is problem ki elegance hai. - Loop ke baad kth group ka aakhri node hai (group_prev se k steps). 12. group_next = kth.next — group ke baad wala node. kth.next ko abhi save karna zaroori hai kyunki reversal use badal degi. 13. prev = group_next — yeh line poore solution ka sabse clever hissa hai. Normally reversal prev = None se shuru hoti hai. Yahan group_next se shuru karte hain, jiska matlab hai: reversal ke baad group ka tail automatically group_next ko point karega. Yaani line 17 ka reconnection free mein ho jaata hai — alag se tail.next = group_next likhne ki zaroorat nahi. Agar group_next None hai (aakhri poora group) toh yeh exactly prev = None ban jaata hai — standard case. Ek line do cases handle kar leti hai. 14. current = group_prev.next — group ka pehla node. 15. while current is not group_next: — is not identity comparison. Yeh "group khatam" ka signal hai. Count-based loop (for _ in range(k)) bhi kaam karta, lekin yeh version zyada readable hai aur group_next ko naturally use karta hai. 16-19. Standard reversal chaar lines. 20. new_group_prev = group_prev.next — yeh line line 21 se PEHLE honi chahiye. Reversal ke baad group_prev.next abhi bhi group ke original pehle node ko point kar raha hai, jo ab group ka tail hai. Wahi agle round ka group_prev banega. Line 21 group_prev.next ko overwrite kar degi, toh pehle save karna zaroori hai. 21. group_prev.next = kth — kth reversal ke baad group ka naya head hai. Pichhle hisse ko usse jodo. 22. group_prev = new_group_prev — agle round ke liye state update.

    Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 2 (nodes A,B,C,D,E)

    Setup: dummy -> A -> B -> C -> D -> E. group_prev = dummy.

    Round 1:

    Step 1: kth = dummy → A → B. Koi None nahi mila. kth = B. Line 12: group_next = B.next = C. Line 13: prev = C. Line 14: current = dummy.next = A.

    Reversal loop:

    Iter current prev current is not C? next_node Assignment prev after current after
    1 A C Yes B A.next = C A B
    2 B A Yes C B.next = A B C
    3 C B No → exit — — — —

    Ab: A.next = C, B.next = A. Dhyaan do — A.next = C line 17 se hua, alag reconnection ki zaroorat nahi padi. Yeh line 13 ka fayda hai.

    Step 3: new_group_prev = dummy.next = A. dummy.next = kth = B. group_prev = A.

    State: dummy -> B -> A -> C -> D -> E.

    Round 2:

    Step 1: kth = A → C → D. kth = D. Line 12: group_next = D.next = E. Line 13: prev = E. Line 14: current = A.next = C.

    Iter current prev is not E? next_node Assignment prev after current after
    1 C E Yes D C.next = E C D
    2 D C Yes E D.next = C D E
    3 E D No → exit — — — —

    Step 3: new_group_prev = A.next = C. A.next = kth = D. group_prev = C.

    State: dummy -> B -> A -> D -> C -> E.

    Round 3:

    Step 1: kth = C → E → E.next = None → kth is None → return dummy.next.

    Final: B(2) -> A(1) -> D(4) -> C(3) -> E(5) = 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5. Sahi, aur E bilkul untouched raha.

    Dry run — 1 -> 2 -> 3, k = 5 (group k se chhota hai)

    Round 1, Step 1: kth = dummy → A → B → C → C.next = None → kth is None → return dummy.next = A. List bilkul unchanged. Sahi.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node exactly do baar touch hota hai — ek baar counting loop mein (step 1), ek baar reversal mein (step 2). 2n = O(n). Follow-up jo poocha jaata hai: "counting pass hata sakte ho?" Haan — agar list ki length pehle se pata ho, ya agar aap reverse karke undo karne ko taiyaar ho. Practically 2n bilkul theek hai.
    • Space: O(1). Dummy plus constant pointers.

    Edge cases

    Case Input k Output Kyun
    k = 1 1->2->3 1 1->2->3 Guard
    k = n 1->2->3 3 3->2->1 Ek hi group
    k > n 1->2->3 5 1->2->3 Step 1 turant None
    Empty None 2 None Guard
    Exact multiple 1->2->3->4 2 2->1->4->3 Koi leftover nahi
    Leftover of 1 1->2->3 2 2->1->3 3 untouched
    Single node 1 2 1
    k = 0 1->2 0 1->2 Guard (warna infinite loop)

    Variations

    • Leftover ko bhi reverse karo (LeetCode 25 ka variant) — step 1 mein None milne par bhi reverse kar do, kth ko aakhri node bana kar.
    • Alternating groups reverse karo — Problem 6.4.
    • Swap Nodes in Pairs (24) — k = 2 ka special case; yehi code kaam karta hai.
    • Recursive version — har group reverse karke head.next = recurse(rest). Padhna aasan, lekin O(n/k) stack.
    • Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups (2074) — group sizes 1,2,3,4,... aur sirf even-length groups reverse.

    Interview answer: "This is repeated sub-list reversal, so the two things that make it non-trivial are stitching groups together and handling the incomplete tail group.

    For the tail: I check before reversing whether k nodes exist, by walking k steps from the group's predecessor. If I hit None, I return immediately and the leftover nodes stay exactly as they are — I never touched them, so there's nothing to undo.

    For the stitching, there's a trick I like. Instead of initialising the reversal's prev pointer to None, I initialise it to the node after the group. That means when the reversal flips the group's first node, it automatically points at the node after the group — so the tail-side reconnection happens for free inside the reversal loop, with no extra assignment. And when the group is the last one, that node is None, which degenerates to the ordinary case. One line covers both.

    The other reconnection is explicit: the predecessor points at the group's new head. And I have to save the group's original first node before that assignment, because after reversal it's the group's tail and becomes the predecessor for the next round.

    I keep a dummy node in front so the first group, which changes the head, needs no special case.

    O(n) time — each node is touched twice, once counting and once reversing — and O(1) space."

    Problem 6.4 — Reverse Alternating K-Element Sub-Lists¶

    Problem statement

    Har k nodes ko reverse karo, phir agle k nodes ko skip karo, phir agle k reverse karo — aur aise hi chalta rahe. Agar aakhir mein k se kam nodes bachein toh unhe jo bhi phase chal raha ho uske hisaab se treat karo (reverse phase mein bache hue nodes ko bhi reverse kar do).

    Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8, k = 2
Output: 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 6 -> 5 -> 7 -> 8
        (1,2 reverse | 3,4 skip | 5,6 reverse | 7,8 skip)

Input:  1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 2
Output: 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5
        (1,2 reverse | 3,4 skip | 5 bacha, reverse phase, akela hai toh waisa hi)

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Values array mein, alternating chunks reverse karo, wapas likho.

    def alt_reverse_brute(head, k):
    values = []                                   # 1
    current = head                                # 2
    while current:                                # 3
        values.append(current.val)                # 4
        current = current.next                    # 5
    i = 0                                         # 6: current chunk ka start
    reverse_this = True                           # 7: PHASE flag -- alternate karega
    while i < len(values):                        # 8
        end = min(i + k, len(values))             # 9: chunk ka end (clamp for partial)
        if reverse_this:                          # 10: reverse phase?
            values[i:end] = values[i:end][::-1]   # 11: chunk reverse
        i = end                                   # 12: agle chunk par
        reverse_this = not reverse_this           # 13: PHASE TOGGLE
    current = head                                # 14: write back
    for v in values:                              # 15
        current.val = v                           # 16
        current = current.next                    # 17
    return head                                   # 18

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. Collect. 6-7. reverse_this = True — pehla chunk hamesha reverse hota hai. Yeh problem definition se aata hai. 8. while i < len(values):. 9. end = min(i + k, len(values)) — min partial chunk ko clamp karta hai. Bina iske slice out of range chala jaata (Python mein slice safe hai lekin end variable galat hota). 10-11. Sirf reverse phase mein reverse. 12. i = end — i += k nahi likha, kyunki partial chunk mein end - i < k hota hai. min se end already sahi hai. 13. reverse_this = not reverse_this — phase toggle. Yeh ek line poori "alternating" behaviour deti hai. 18. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n). Aur values-vs-links objection.

    The insight

    Yeh Problem 6.3 hi hai plus ek toggle. Har round mein do kaam karne hain:

    1. k nodes reverse karo (6.3 ka step).
    2. k nodes skip karo — yaani sirf traverse karo bina kuch badle.

    Aur while loop dono ko ek saath karta hai. Skip phase mein bas group_prev ko k steps aage le jao.

    Ek design decision: partial group ko reverse karein ya nahi? 6.3 mein humne partial group chhod diya tha. Yahan problem kehti hai partial ko bhi reverse karo (agar reverse phase mein ho). Toh counting logic thoda dheela karna padega — "at least 1 node hai" check karo, "exactly k" nahi.

    Optimal solution

    def reverse_alternate_k(head, k):
    if head is None or k <= 1:                    # 1: kuch nahi karna
        return head                               # 2

    dummy = ListNode(0)                           # 3
    dummy.next = head                             # 4
    group_prev = dummy                            # 5: processed hisse ka aakhri node

    while group_prev.next is not None:            # 6: jab tak nodes bache hain
        # PHASE 1: agle k nodes reverse karo (ya jitne bhi bache hon)
        prev = None                               # 7: standard reversal init
        current = group_prev.next                 # 8: group ka pehla node
        group_start = current                     # 9: reversal ke baad yeh TAIL banega
        count = 0                                 # 10: kitne reverse kiye
        while current is not None and count < k:  # 11: at most k, aur list khatam hone tak
            next_node = current.next              # 12
            current.next = prev                   # 13
            prev = current                        # 14
            current = next_node                   # 15
            count += 1                            # 16
        group_prev.next = prev                    # 17: pichhla hissa naye head se jodo
        group_start.next = current                # 18: naya tail bache hue list se jodo

        # PHASE 2: agle k nodes skip karo
        group_prev = group_start                  # 19: ab tail hi naya group_prev hai
        for _ in range(k):                        # 20: k steps aage
            if group_prev.next is None:           # 21: list khatam
                return dummy.next                 # 22
            group_prev = group_prev.next          # 23
    return dummy.next                             # 24

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. 6.3 jaisa setup. 6. while group_prev.next is not None: — while True nahi, kyunki yahan exit condition natural hai (nodes khatam). Yeh 6.3 se alag hai kyunki 6.3 mein "exactly k chahiye" check tha. 7. prev = None — 6.3 wali prev = group_next trick yahan use NAHI ki. Kyun? Kyunki yahan hum pehle se nahi jaante ki group kitna bada hoga (partial ho sakta hai), toh group_next ka pata nahi. Isliye standard None init aur explicit reconnection (line 18). 8. current = group_prev.next. 9. group_start = current — reversal ke baad yeh tail banega. Save karna zaroori hai. 10. count = 0. 11. while current is not None and count < k: — do conditions. current is not None partial group handle karta hai (list k se pehle khatam ho gayi), count < k normal case.
