    Ek line mein poore pattern ka summary: Chaar lines — save, flip, advance prev, advance current — aur ek dummy node. Baaki har problem sirf yeh decide karti hai ki loop kab rukega aur reconnection kahan hoga.

    7. Tree BFS¶

    Recognition signals — aap tree BFS dekh rahe ho jab problem bole¶

    • "level by level", "level order", "each level", "per level" — sabse direct signal.
    • "minimum depth", "shortest path" — BFS pehli baar jab target tak pahunchta hai, wahi shortest hota hai. DFS yeh guarantee nahi deta.
    • "right side view", "left side view" — har level ka aakhri/pehla node.
    • "zigzag", "spiral", "alternate direction" — level order plus direction flip.
    • "connect siblings", "next right pointer" — same level ke nodes ko jodna.
    • "width of the tree", "maximum level sum", "average of levels" — level-wise aggregation.
    • "closest node to root that satisfies X" — BFS pehle milne wale ko lauta dega.

    Kab BFS aur kab DFS — yeh decision hi aadha interview hai¶

    Chahiye Use Kyun
    Level-wise grouping BFS Queue naturally levels deti hai
    Shortest path / minimum depth BFS Pehla hit hi shortest hai
    Kisi bhi path ka existence DFS Stack/recursion se simple
    Saare paths enumerate karna DFS Backtracking natural hai
    Tree ki height/depth (maximum) Dono DFS ka code chhota
    Har node par uske subtree ka info DFS (postorder) Bachchon ka result pehle chahiye
    Memory constraint, tree bahut wide DFS BFS queue O(width) hoti hai
    Memory constraint, tree bahut deep BFS DFS stack O(depth) hoti hai

    Yeh table interview mein bolna bahut strong hai — kyunki zyadatar candidates BFS/DFS ka choice bina reason ke karte hain.

    BFS ka core mechanism — level ko "freeze" karna¶

    BFS ka poora concept ek line mein: queue mein daalo, queue se nikaalo, bachchon ko queue mein daalo. Lekin level-wise grouping ke liye ek extra trick chahiye.

    Problem: agar hum bas queue chalate rahein toh saare nodes ek hi flat sequence mein aa jaayenge — level ka pata nahi chalega.

    Solution: har outer iteration ke shuru mein queue ka size le lo, aur exactly utne nodes process karo. Kyunki us waqt queue mein exactly ek poora level hota hai.

    level_size = len(queue)          # is waqt queue mein exactly ek level hai
for _ in range(level_size):      # exactly utne process karo
    node = queue.popleft()
    # ... bachche add karo (yeh agle level mein jaate hain)

    Yeh level_size snapshot lena hi poore pattern ka dil hai. Agar aap for _ in range(len(queue)) ke bajaye while queue andar likh doge, toh loop kabhi nahi rukega kyunki bachche add hote rahenge.

    Template code¶

    from collections import deque

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


def bfs_template(root):
    if root is None:                        # khaali tree guard -- hamesha chahiye
        return []
    result = []                             # har level ka result
    queue = deque([root])                   # deque, list NAHI -- popleft O(1) hai
    while queue:                            # jab tak nodes bache hain
        level_size = len(queue)             # SNAPSHOT -- yeh line hi sab kuch hai
        current_level = []                  # is level ke values
        for _ in range(level_size):         # exactly ek level process karo
            node = queue.popleft()          # FIFO -- pehla aaya, pehla nikla
            current_level.append(node.val)  # is node ko record karo
            if node.left:                   # bachche AGLE level mein jaate hain
                queue.append(node.left)
            if node.right:
                queue.append(node.right)
        result.append(current_level)        # poora level ek saath
    return result

    Template ke do critical choices:

    Pehla — deque, list nahi. Python list par pop(0) O(n) hai, kyunki baaki saare elements ek jagah shift hote hain. n nodes par yeh poora BFS O(n^2) bana deta hai. deque.popleft() O(1) hai. Yeh interview mein pakda jaata hai aur bahut se candidates yahan phansate hain.

    Dusra — bachche add karne se pehle if node.left check. None ko queue mein daalne se agli iteration mein node.val par AttributeError aayega. Alternative: None allow karo aur pop ke baad check karo — dono chalega, lekin add se pehle check karna queue ko chhota rakhta hai.

    Problem 7.1 — Binary Tree Level Order Traversal¶

    Problem statement

    Binary tree ka root diya hai. Har level ke nodes ko ek alag list mein, top se bottom, left se right — poora nested list lauta do.

    Input:      3
           / \
          9  20
             / \
            15  7

Output: [[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]]

Input: root = None
Output: []

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Pehle tree ki height nikaalo, phir har level ke liye alag se DFS chalao.

    def level_order_brute(root):
    def height(node):                             # 1: tree ki depth
        if node is None:                          # 2: base case
            return 0                              # 3
        return 1 + max(height(node.left),         # 4: 1 + gehre bachche ki height
                       height(node.right))        # 5

    def collect(node, level, acc):                # 6: level `level` ke nodes collect karo
        if node is None:                          # 7
            return                                # 8
        if level == 0:                            # 9: yahi woh level hai
            acc.append(node.val)                  # 10
            return                                # 11: aur neeche jaane ki zaroorat nahi
        collect(node.left, level - 1, acc)        # 12: ek level neeche
        collect(node.right, level - 1, acc)       # 13

    h = height(root)                              # 14
    result = []                                   # 15
    for lvl in range(h):                          # 16: har level ke liye
        acc = []                                  # 17
        collect(root, lvl, acc)                   # 18: POORA tree traverse -- yeh mehnga hai
        result.append(acc)                        # 19
    return result                                 # 20

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. height — classic recursion. Line 4 1 + max(...) matlab "khud ka ek level plus jo bachcha zyada gehra hai." 6-13. collect — level 0 par pahunchte hi record karo. Line 11 ka return important hai — us level ke neeche jaana zaroori nahi. 14-19. Har level ke liye poora tree traverse hota hai. Yehi problem hai. 20. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n * h) — worst case skewed tree par h = n, toh O(n^2). Space O(h) recursion stack.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Har node ko h baar visit karte hain jabki ek baar kaafi hai. Aur balanced tree par bhi O(n log n).

    The insight

    Level order traversal ka matlab hi hai "jo pehle aaya usko pehle process karo" — yeh FIFO queue ki exact definition hai.

    Aur "levels ko alag rakhna" ke liye ek chhota sa observation: jab hum ek level ke saare nodes queue mein daal chuke hote hain aur agla level abhi shuru nahi hua, us waqt queue mein exactly ek poora level hota hai. Toh us moment par len(queue) le lo — wahi us level ka size hai.

    Ek pass, har node ek baar. O(n).

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def level_order(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: khaali tree -> khaali result
        return []                                 # 2
    result = []                                   # 3: levels ka list of lists
    queue = deque([root])                         # 4: deque -- popleft O(1)
    while queue:                                  # 5: jab tak koi node bacha hai
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 6: SNAPSHOT -- abhi queue mein ek poora level
        current_level = []                        # 7: is level ke values
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 8: exactly utne hi process karo
            node = queue.popleft()                # 9: FIFO se nikaalo
            current_level.append(node.val)        # 10: record
            if node.left is not None:             # 11: bachche AGLE level ke liye
                queue.append(node.left)           # 12
            if node.right is not None:            # 13: left pehle, right baad -- ORDER matter
                queue.append(node.right)          # 14
        result.append(current_level)              # 15: poora level result mein
    return result                                 # 16

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Empty guard. deque([None]) banana aur phir line 10 par None.val — crash. Guard sabse pehle. 3. result = []. 4. queue = deque([root]) — deque kyun: list.pop(0) O(n) hai (memory shift), deque.popleft() O(1). n nodes par yeh O(n^2) vs O(n) ka farq hai. deque([root]) — single element se initialise. deque(root) likhna galat hai (woh root ko iterate karne ki koshish karega). 5. while queue: — deque falsy hoti hai jab khaali ho. 6. level_size = len(queue) — poore solution ki sabse important line. Is moment par queue mein exactly current level ke saare nodes hain aur agle level ka koi nahi (kyunki bachche line 12/14 mein andar wale loop mein hi add hote hain). Agar yeh line na ho aur hum while queue andar likh dein, toh andar wala loop agle level ko bhi kha jaayega aur saare levels ek hi list mein mil jaayenge. 7. current_level = []. 8. for _ in range(level_size): — level_size ek snapshot hai, live value nahi. range() apna argument ek hi baar evaluate karta hai, isliye andar queue badalne se yeh loop affect nahi hota. Yeh Python ka behaviour hi is pattern ko kaam karne deta hai. 9. node = queue.popleft() — left se nikaalna FIFO deta hai. pop() (right se) likhne se DFS-ish behaviour aa jaata aur levels galat ban jaate. 10. current_level.append(node.val) — value, node nahi (output values maangta hai). 11-14. Bachche add. left pehle, right baad — kyunki output mein har level left-to-right chahiye. Order ulta karne se har level reversed aayega. is not None explicit likha; if node.left: bhi kaam karta hai jab tak node ki value falsy na ho — lekin yeh check node object par hai, value par nahi, toh dono safe hain. Explicit form habit ke liye behtar. 15. result.append(current_level) — andar wale loop ke BAAD, andar nahi. 16. Return.

    Dry run — tree:

          3
     / \
    9  20
       / \
      15  7
    Outer iter queue (start) level_size Inner steps queue (end) current_level result
    1 [3] 1 pop 3 → add 9, 20 [9, 20] [3] [[3]]
    2 [9, 20] 2 pop 9 (no children) → pop 20 → add 15, 7 [15, 7] [9, 20] [[3],[9,20]]
    3 [15, 7] 2 pop 15 (none) → pop 7 (none) [] [15, 7] [[3],[9,20],[15,7]]
    4 [] — while queue False → exit — — —

    Outer iteration 2 ko detail mein dekho:

    Inner step queue before popped Children added queue after current_level
    1 [9, 20] 9 none [20] [9]
    2 [20] 20 15, 7 [15, 7] [9, 20]

    Dhyaan do — step 2 mein queue mein 15, 7 add hue, lekin for _ in range(2) sirf 2 iterations karta hai, toh woh is level mein process nahi hue. Yeh exactly level_size snapshot ka fayda hai.

    Dry run — skewed tree 1 -> 2 (left) -> 3 (left)

    Outer iter queue level_size Popped Added result
    1 [1] 1 1 2 [[1]]
    2 [2] 1 2 3 [[1],[2]]
    3 [3] 1 3 — [[1],[2],[3]]
    4 [] — exit — —

    Har level mein ek node — sahi.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node exactly ek baar enqueue aur ek baar dequeue hota hai. deque operations O(1) hain. Total O(n).
    • Space: O(w) jahan w = tree ki maximum width. Perfect binary tree mein last level mein n/2 nodes hote hain, toh worst case O(n). Skewed tree mein w = 1, toh O(1) — jo DFS ke O(n) stack se better hai. Yeh trade-off bolna acha lagta hai: "BFS is O(width), DFS is O(depth) — which one wins depends on the tree's shape."

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty tree None [] Guard
    Single node 1 [[1]] Ek level
    Left skewed 1->2->3 (left) [[1],[2],[3]] Har level ek node
    Right skewed 1->2->3 (right) [[1],[2],[3]] Same
    Perfect tree (depth 3) 7 nodes [[1],[2,3],[4,5,6,7]]
    Only left child at root 1 with left 2 [[1],[2]] right None skip
    Negative values -1 with -2, -3 [[-1],[-2,-3]] Values koi bhi ho sakti
    Duplicate values 1,1,1 [[1],[1,1]] Values duplicate ho sakti

    Variations

    • Bottom-up level order (LeetCode 107) — Problem 7.2.
    • Zigzag (103) — Problem 7.3.
    • Level averages (637) — Problem 7.4.
    • Right side view (199) — Problem 7.6.
    • N-ary tree level order (429) — node.children par loop karo.
    • Level order without a queue — DFS with level index; result[level].append(val). O(n) time, lekin recursion stack.
    • Har level ka maximum / minimum / sum — current_level par aggregate.

    DFS-based alternative (interviewer aksar poochta hai "can you do it recursively?"):

    def level_order_dfs(root):
    result = []                                   # 17: index = level
    def dfs(node, level):                         # 18: level ko parameter mein carry karo
        if node is None:                          # 19
            return                                # 20
        if level == len(result):                  # 21: is level ki list abhi bani nahi
            result.append([])                     # 22: bana do
        result[level].append(node.val)            # 23: sahi level mein daalo
        dfs(node.left, level + 1)                 # 24: left pehle -> left-to-right order
        dfs(node.right, level + 1)                # 25
    dfs(root, 0)                                  # 26: root level 0 par
    return result                                 # 27

    Line 21 ka level == len(result) clever hai: kyunki hum har level par pehli baar left-most node se pahunchte hain (line 24 pehle chalti hai), toh naya level exactly tab banta hai jab level current length ke barabar ho. Aur line 24 pehle hone se har level mein order left-to-right rehta hai. Time O(n), Space O(h) recursion ke liye.

    Interview answer: "Level order is by definition first-in-first-out, so this is a queue-based BFS.

    The one non-obvious part is separating the levels. If I just drain the queue node by node, I get one flat sequence with no level boundaries. The fix is to snapshot the queue's length at the start of each outer iteration and process exactly that many nodes. At that moment the queue holds exactly one complete level, because children are only enqueued inside the inner loop.

    That works in Python specifically because range evaluates its argument once, so growing the queue inside the loop doesn't extend it.

    Two implementation points. I use collections.deque rather than a list, because list.pop of index zero is O(n) — it shifts everything — which would make the whole traversal quadratic. And I enqueue the left child before the right so each level comes out left to right.

    O(n) time since every node is enqueued and dequeued once. Space is O of the maximum width, which is n over two for a perfect tree but only one for a skewed tree. That's the interesting contrast with DFS, which is O of the depth — so which one uses less memory depends entirely on the tree's shape.

    I can also do this with DFS by passing the level down and appending into result at that index, creating a new sublist the first time I reach a level. Same linear time, but O(height) stack instead."

    Problem 7.2 — Reverse Level Order Traversal¶

    Problem statement

    Level order traversal karo lekin neeche se upar — sabse gehra level pehle, root aakhir mein.

    Input:      3
           / \
          9  20
             / \
            15  7

Output: [[15, 7], [9, 20], [3]]

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Problem 7.1 chalao, phir result ko reverse kar do.

    def reverse_level_order_brute(root):
    levels = level_order(root)                    # 1: 7.1 ka result -- top to bottom
    return levels[::-1]                           # 2: poora list reverse

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. level_order(root) — reuse. Interview mein reuse bolna bilkul valid hai.
    2. levels[::-1] — ek naya list banata hai, O(L) space jahan L = levels ki count. levels.reverse() in-place hota aur yeh copy bachaata.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) output plus O(L) extra copy.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Technically kuch galat nahi hai — yeh acceptable answer hai. Lekin interviewer aksar poochta hai "can you avoid the second pass?", aur asli baat yeh hai ki [::-1] ek extra copy banata hai jabki appendleft se woh copy bilkul nahi chahiye.

    The insight

    Result ko ek deque bana do aur har level ko appendleft karo, append nahi.

    deque.appendleft() O(1) hai (list ka insert(0, x) O(n) hai — yeh farq exactly wahi hai jo popleft vs pop(0) mein tha). Toh levels natural top-to-bottom order mein generate hote hain lekin result mein ulte jamā hote hain — bina kisi reversal pass ke.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def reverse_level_order(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return []                                 # 2
    result = deque()                              # 3: LIST nahi -- appendleft O(1) chahiye
    queue = deque([root])                         # 4: BFS queue
    while queue:                                  # 5
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 6: snapshot
        current_level = []                        # 7
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 8
            node = queue.popleft()                # 9
            current_level.append(node.val)        # 10
            if node.left is not None:             # 11
                queue.append(node.left)           # 12
            if node.right is not None:            # 13
                queue.append(node.right)          # 14
        result.appendleft(current_level)          # 15: SHURU mein daalo, aakhir mein nahi
    return list(result)                           # 16: deque ko list mein convert

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guard. 3. result = deque() — list nahi. list.insert(0, x) O(n) hai kyunki saare elements shift hote hain; L levels par yeh O(L^2) ho jaata. deque.appendleft O(1) hai. 4-14. Problem 7.1 se bilkul identical. Ek hi BFS. 15. result.appendleft(current_level) — poore solution ki ekmatra badli hui line. Har naya (gehra) level shuru mein jaata hai, toh purane (upar wale) levels neeche khiskte jaate hain. 16. list(result) — problem list maangti hai, deque nahi. Yeh O(L) conversion hai. Agar caller deque accept karta ho toh yeh line bhi nahi chahiye — mention karne layak.

    Dry run — same tree

    Outer iter current_level appendleft ke baad result
    1 [3] deque([[3]])
    2 [9, 20] deque([[9,20], [3]])
    3 [15, 7] deque([[15,7], [9,20], [3]])

    list(result) → [[15,7],[9,20],[3]]. Sahi.

    Compare with 7.1 jahan append tha:

    Outer iter 7.1 (append) 7.2 (appendleft)
    1 [[3]] [[3]]
    2 [[3],[9,20]] [[9,20],[3]]
    3 [[3],[9,20],[15,7]] [[15,7],[9,20],[3]]

    Ek hi traversal, sirf jamā karne ki direction alag.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). BFS O(n), appendleft O(1) per level, final conversion O(L).
    • Space: O(w) queue ke liye plus O(n) output.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None [] Guard
    Single 1 [[1]] Ek level, reversal se koi farq nahi
    Skewed 1->2->3 (left) [[3],[2],[1]] Har level ek node
    Two levels 1 with 2,3 [[2,3],[1]]
    Perfect depth 3 7 nodes [[4,5,6,7],[2,3],[1]]

    Variations

    • Har level ko andar se bhi reverse karo — current_level.reverse() line 15 se pehle.
    • Sirf sabse gehra level chahiye — BFS chalao aur aakhri current_level rakho (O(w) space).
    • Bottom-up sum — levels ko reverse order mein aggregate karo.
    • DFS version — level index se result bharo, phir reverse.

    Interview answer: "This is the same BFS as level order — I don't change the traversal at all. The only change is how I accumulate the levels.

    I could run the normal traversal and reverse the result at the end, which is perfectly fine and I'd say so. But if I use a deque for the result and appendleft each level instead of appending, the levels land in reverse order as they're produced, with no second pass and no extra copy.

    The reason it has to be a deque and not a list is the same reason the BFS queue is a deque: inserting at index zero of a list is O(n) because everything shifts, so doing it once per level would be O of levels squared. Appendleft on a deque is O(1).

    O(n) time, O(width) space for the queue plus the output."

    Problem 7.3 — Zigzag Level Order Traversal¶

    Problem statement

    Level order karo, lekin direction alternate ho: pehla level left-to-right, dusra right-to-left, teesra left-to-right, aur aise hi.

    Input:      3
           / \
          9  20
             / \
            15  7

Output: [[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]
        (level 0 L->R, level 1 R->L, level 2 L->R)

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    7.1 chalao, phir alternate levels ko reverse kar do.

    def zigzag_brute(root):
    levels = level_order(root)                    # 1: normal level order
    for i in range(len(levels)):                  # 2: har level
        if i % 2 == 1:                            # 3: ODD levels reverse karne hain
            levels[i].reverse()                   # 4: in-place reverse
    return levels                                 # 5

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. Reuse. 2-3. i % 2 == 1 — level 0 (root) left-to-right rehta hai, level 1 reverse, level 2 normal. Agar i % 2 == 0 likhte toh root wala level ulta ho jaata (jo single node par dikhta nahi, lekin logically galat hai).
    2. .reverse() in-place — [::-1] copy banata.
    3. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n) (har element at most ek baar reverse hota), Space O(n) output. Yeh bilkul valid solution hai.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Kuch bhi nahi, honestly. Yeh interview mein pass ho jaayega. Lekin do baatein:

    1. Do passes hain (traverse, phir reverse).
    2. Interviewer aksar bolta hai "can you build each level already in the right order?" — aur uska jawab sikhna is problem ka point hai.

    The insight

    Do options hain aur dono bolne layak hain:

    Option A — deque ke dono ends use karo. Har level ke liye current_level ek deque rakho. Left-to-right level mein append karo, right-to-left level mein appendleft karo. Ek boolean flag direction toggle karta hai.

    Option B — traversal ki direction hi badal do. Level ko queue se ulte order mein nikaalo. Yeh zyada complicated hai aur bug-prone; Option A better hai.

    Option A ka fayda: BFS bilkul nahi badalta (hamesha left child pehle add hota hai), sirf collection direction badalta hai. Isse mental model simple rehta hai.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def zigzag_level_order(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return []                                 # 2
    result = []                                   # 3
    queue = deque([root])                         # 4
    left_to_right = True                          # 5: PHASE flag -- pehla level normal
    while queue:                                  # 6
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 7: snapshot
        current_level = deque()                   # 8: DEQUE -- dono ends chahiye
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 9
            node = queue.popleft()                # 10: traversal HAMESHA same
            if left_to_right:                     # 11: direction ke hisaab se jamā karo
                current_level.append(node.val)    # 12: aakhir mein
            else:
                current_level.appendleft(node.val)# 13: shuru mein
            if node.left is not None:             # 14: bachche HAMESHA left pehle
                queue.append(node.left)           # 15
            if node.right is not None:            # 16
                queue.append(node.right)          # 17
        result.append(list(current_level))        # 18: deque -> list
        left_to_right = not left_to_right         # 19: TOGGLE
    return result                                 # 20

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-4. Standard setup. 5. left_to_right = True — root wala level (level 0) hamesha left-to-right hota hai. False se shuru karna problem definition ke against hai. 6-7. Standard. 8. current_level = deque() — list nahi, kyunki line 13 appendleft maangti hai. 9-10. Traversal bilkul nahi badalta. popleft hamesha, queue.append hamesha left-pehle. Yeh deliberate hai — agar aap traversal ki direction badalne ki koshish karoge toh bachchon ka order bhi ulta karna padega aur do cheezein ek saath sambhalni padengi. Isse bug lagta hai. 11-13. Sirf collection direction badalti hai. - left_to_right True → append → nodes jis order mein aaye usi order mein. - False → appendleft → nodes ulte order mein jamā. 14-17. Bachche hamesha left pehle. Isse agle level ka natural order left-to-right rehta hai, aur agar us level ko reverse chahiye toh appendleft woh kaam kar deti hai. 18. list(current_level) — output list of lists chahiye. 19. left_to_right = not left_to_right — toggle, andar wale loop ke baahar. Andar likhne se har node par direction badalti aur output bakwaas hota. 20. Return.

    Dry run — tree:

          3
     / \
    9  20
       / \
      15  7
    Outer iter left_to_right queue (start) Nodes popped (order) Collection ops current_level result
    1 True [3] 3 append(3) [3] [[3]]
    2 False [9, 20] 9, then 20 appendleft(9) → [9]; appendleft(20) → [20, 9] [20, 9] [[3],[20,9]]
    3 True [15, 7] 15, then 7 append(15) → [15]; append(7) → [15,7] [15, 7] [[3],[20,9],[15,7]]
    4 False [] exit — — —

    Result [[3],[20,9],[15,7]]. Sahi.

    Outer iteration 2 ko ghor se dekho — nodes 9 phir 20 order mein pop hue (traversal normal), lekin appendleft ki wajah se [20, 9] bana. Traversal same, collection ulti.

    Dry run — 4-level perfect tree (values 1..15)

    Level left_to_right Popped order Result level
    0 True 1 [1]
    1 False 2, 3 [3, 2]
    2 True 4, 5, 6, 7 [4, 5, 6, 7]
    3 False 8, 9, ..., 15 [15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9, 8]

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node ek baar. appendleft O(1). Final list() conversion per level O(level size), total O(n).
    • Space: O(w) queue plus O(w) current_level, plus O(n) output.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None [] Guard
    Single 1 [[1]] Ek level, direction se koi farq nahi
    Two levels 1 with 2,3 [[1],[3,2]] Level 1 reversed
    Left skewed 1->2->3 (left) [[1],[2],[3]] Har level ek node, reversal invisible
    Only right children 1->2->3 (right) [[1],[2],[3]] Same
    Perfect depth 3 7 nodes [[1],[3,2],[4,5,6,7]]
    Asymmetric root with only right child having two kids [[1],[2],[4,3]]

    Variations

    • Root level right-to-left se shuru karo — left_to_right = False.
    • Har level ko andar se sort karo — sorted(current_level).
    • Spiral matrix traversal (LeetCode 54) — same "alternate direction" idea, matrix par. Section 22.
    • Vertical order traversal (987) — column index track karo, alag problem lekin same BFS backbone.
    • Do stacks se karo — classic alternative: ek stack current level ke liye, ek next ke liye, aur children ka push order alternate karo. Kaam karta hai lekin children ka order bhi flip karna padta hai, jo ek extra cheez hai jo galat ho sakti hai.

    Interview answer: "The simplest version is a plain level order followed by reversing every odd-indexed level. That's linear and I'd offer it first — nothing wrong with it.

    If they want each level built already in the right order, I keep the BFS completely unchanged — always dequeue from the left, always enqueue the left child first — and only change how I collect each level. I make the level a deque and, depending on a direction flag, either append or appendleft. Then I flip the flag once per level, outside the inner loop.

    The reason I don't flip the traversal direction instead is that it forces me to also flip the order I enqueue children, so I'd be juggling two coupled things. Keeping the traversal fixed and moving the variation into a single append-versus-appendleft choice keeps it to one decision.

    There's also a two-stack version people use. It works, but it has the same coupling problem — you have to alternate the child push order — so I prefer this one.

    O(n) time, O(width) space."

    Problem 7.4 — Level Averages In A Binary Tree¶

    Problem statement

    Har level ke nodes ka average nikaalo aur ek list mein lauta do.

    Input:      3
           / \
          9  20
             / \
            15  7

Output: [3.0, 14.5, 11.0]
        (level 0: 3/1 = 3.0
         level 1: (9+20)/2 = 14.5
         level 2: (15+7)/2 = 11.0)

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    7.1 chalao, phir har level ka average nikaalo.

    def level_averages_brute(root):
    levels = level_order(root)                    # 1: nested list
    result = []                                   # 2
    for level in levels:                          # 3: har level
        result.append(sum(level) / len(level))    # 4: average
    return result                                 # 5

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. Reuse 7.1. 2-4. sum(level) / len(level) — / true division hai, // nahi. // integer division deta aur 14.5 ke bajaye 14 aata. Yeh chhoti si galti test fail kara deti hai. len(level) kabhi 0 nahi hoga kyunki BFS khaali level nahi banata.
    2. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) — poora nested list banta hai jabki humein sirf averages chahiye.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Hum poora [[3],[9,20],[15,7]] structure banate hain aur phir usse [3.0, 14.5, 11.0] mein squeeze kar dete hain. Beech ka structure zaroorat se zyada memory leta hai — bade tree par yeh O(n) hai jabki O(1) possible tha (output ke alawa).

    The insight

    Har level ke values store karne ki zaroorat hi nahi hai — sirf sum aur count chahiye. Aur count toh level_size mein pehle se hai.

    Toh current_level list ko ek single level_sum variable se replace kar do. Yeh generalise karta hai: jo bhi per-level aggregate chahiye (sum, max, min, count of even numbers), usko ek running variable se calculate karo, list banane ki zaroorat nahi.

    Yeh chhota sa change lagta hai lekin ek asli principle hai: jo data aapko chahiye nahi, use materialise mat karo.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def level_averages(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return []                                 # 2
    result = []                                   # 3: har level ka average
    queue = deque([root])                         # 4
    while queue:                                  # 5
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 6: snapshot -- yeh DENOMINATOR bhi hai
        level_sum = 0                             # 7: LIST ki jagah ek accumulator
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 8
            node = queue.popleft()                # 9
            level_sum += node.val                 # 10: values store nahi, seedha jodo
            if node.left is not None:             # 11
                queue.append(node.left)           # 12
            if node.right is not None:            # 13
                queue.append(node.right)          # 14
        result.append(level_sum / level_size)     # 15: TRUE division, aur snapshot use karo
    return result                                 # 16

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-6. Standard BFS setup. 7. level_sum = 0 — current_level = [] ki jagah. Ek integer ek list se bahut sasta hai. 10. level_sum += node.val — values kahin store nahi ho rahi. 15. result.append(level_sum / level_size) — do baatein: - / (true division), // nahi. Python 3 mein / hamesha float deta hai. 7 / 2 = 3.5, 7 // 2 = 3. - level_size denominator hai, aur woh line 6 ka snapshot hai. len(queue) yahan likhna bilkul galat hoga, kyunki is waqt queue mein agla level hai, current nahi. Yeh ek bahut aasan aur bahut khatarnak galti hai. 16. Return.

    Overflow ke baare mein: Python mein integers unbounded hain toh level_sum kabhi overflow nahi karta. Java/C++ mein long chahiye hota, aur agar values bahut badi hon toh incremental averaging (avg += (x - avg) / count) use karna padta. Yeh mention karna interview mein acha lagta hai.

    Dry run — same tree

    Outer iter queue (start) level_size Nodes level_sum Average result
    1 [3] 1 3 3 3 / 1 = 3.0 [3.0]
    2 [9, 20] 2 9, 20 0+9=9, 9+20=29 29 / 2 = 14.5 [3.0, 14.5]
    3 [15, 7] 2 15, 7 0+15=15, 15+7=22 22 / 2 = 11.0 [3.0, 14.5, 11.0]
    4 [] — exit — — —

    Result [3.0, 14.5, 11.0]. Sahi.

    Iteration 2 ke andar ka detail (yeh dikhata hai ki level_size snapshot kyun zaroori hai):

    Inner step queue before popped level_sum Children added queue after len(queue) ab
    1 [9, 20] 9 9 none [20] 1
    2 [20] 20 29 15, 7 [15, 7] 2

    Loop ke baad len(queue) = 2 hai — jo sanyog se sahi denominator hai is case mein, lekin general mein nahi. Agar level 1 mein 3 nodes hote aur unke 5 bachche hote, toh len(queue) = 5 hota aur 29 / 5 galat aata. Isliye line 6 ka snapshot mandatory hai.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node ek baar; sum incremental.
    • Space: O(w) queue ke liye. Brute force ke O(n) intermediate structure se better. Output O(L) hai jahan L = levels.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None [] Guard
    Single 5 [5.0] 5 / 1
    Negative values -1 with -2,-4 [-1.0, -3.0] Average negative ho sakta
    Mixed signs 0 with -5, 5 [0.0, 0.0]
    Large values 10**18 nodes exact in Python Java mein overflow risk
    Skewed 1->2->3 [1.0, 2.0, 3.0] Har level ek node
    Zeros 0 with 0,0 [0.0, 0.0] 0/1 aur 0/2
    Floats in nodes 1.5 with 2.5 [1.5, 2.5] Kaam karta hai

    Variations

    • Har level ka maximum (LeetCode 515) — level_sum ki jagah level_max = float('-inf'), aur max().
    • Har level ka minimum — float('inf') se seed.
    • Maximum level sum lauta do, aur uska level number (1161) — level_sum ko track karo, best ke saath level index bhi.
    • Sirf ek level ka average — us level tak BFS karo aur ruk jao.
    • Weighted average (depth ke hisaab se) — same skeleton, alag formula.
    • Median per level — tab list banani hi padegi (median ke liye saare values chahiye). Yeh dikhata hai ki kab optimisation possible nahi hai.

    Interview answer: "The straightforward version runs a full level order and then averages each sublist. That's linear, but it materialises the entire tree as a nested list when all I actually need per level is a sum and a count.

    So I replace the per-level list with a single running sum. The count I already have — it's the level-size snapshot I take at the top of each outer iteration. That drops the intermediate structure entirely; space becomes O of the width for the queue, rather than O(n).

    Two things to be careful about. I divide with a single slash, not a double slash — integer division would turn fourteen point five into fourteen. And the denominator must be the snapshot, not len of the queue at that moment, because by then the queue holds the next level. That one is easy to write and hard to spot.

    The general principle here is: don't materialise data you don't need. The same skeleton gives per-level max, min, or sum by swapping the accumulator. It stops working for something like a per-level median, where you genuinely need all the values — which is a useful thing to notice out loud.

    O(n) time, O(width) space."

    Problem 7.5 — Minimum Depth Of A Binary Tree¶

    Problem statement

    Root se sabse nazdeek leaf tak ki depth nikaalo. Leaf woh node hai jiske dono bachche None hain.

    Input:      3
           / \
          9  20
             / \
            15  7
Output: 2       (3 -> 9, aur 9 ek leaf hai)

Input:   2
          \
           3
            \
             4
Output: 3       (koi shortcut nahi, 2->3->4 aur sirf 4 hi leaf hai)

    Pehla instinct — brute force (recursive DFS)

    def min_depth_naive(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: khaali subtree
        return 0                                  # 2: depth 0
    return 1 + min(min_depth_naive(root.left),    # 3: GALAT -- neeche dekho
                   min_depth_naive(root.right))   # 4

    Line by line — aur yahan ek asli bug hai

    1-2. Base case. 3-4. 1 + min(left, right) — yeh galat hai aur yeh sabse classic tree bug hai.

    Kyun galat hai: tree 2 -> 3 (right only) par. root = 2. min_depth(2.left) = min_depth(None) = 0. min_depth(2.right) = min_depth(3) = 1. Toh 1 + min(0, 1) = 1. Answer 1 aaya, lekin 2 ek leaf nahi hai — uska ek bachcha hai. Sahi answer 2 hai.

    Problem yeh hai ki None ko "depth 0 ka valid raasta" maan liya, jabki None koi leaf nahi hai — woh ek missing child hai.

    Sahi recursive version:

    def min_depth_dfs(root):
    if root is None:                              # 5: khaali tree
        return 0                                  # 6
    if root.left is None and root.right is None:  # 7: ASLI leaf
        return 1                                  # 8
    if root.left is None:                         # 9: sirf right subtree hai
        return 1 + min_depth_dfs(root.right)      # 10: min lene ka koi matlab nahi
    if root.right is None:                        # 11: sirf left subtree hai
        return 1 + min_depth_dfs(root.left)       # 12
    return 1 + min(min_depth_dfs(root.left),      # 13: DONO hain -> ab min valid hai
                   min_depth_dfs(root.right))     # 14

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    5-6. Empty tree → 0. 7-8. Asli leaf ki definition: dono bachche None. Depth 1. 9-10. Sirf ek bachcha hai (right). Yahan min galat hoga kyunki left side koi leaf nahi deti — woh raasta hi nahi hai. Toh seedha right ki depth lo. 11-12. Symmetric. 13-14. Dono bachche hain → ab dono valid raaste hain → min sahi hai.

    Complexity: Time O(n) — poora tree traverse hota hai, chahe answer level 1 par hi mil jaaye. Space O(h) recursion stack.

    Isme problem kya hai

    DFS ko poora tree dekhna padta hai, kyunki woh nahi jaanta ki kahin aur koi chhota raasta hai ya nahi. Ek tree jismein left side 1 node ka hai aur right side 10^6 nodes ka — DFS phir bhi poore right side ko traverse karega.

    The insight

    BFS level by level neeche jaata hai. Toh jo pehla leaf mile, wahi minimum depth par hai — kyunki us se kam depth par koi leaf hota toh BFS use pehle pahunch chuka hota.

    Toh: BFS chalao, level counter rakho, aur pehla leaf milte hi turant return kar do. Poora tree traverse karne ki zaroorat nahi.

    Yeh "BFS finds the shortest first" wala property hi is problem ka poora point hai, aur yehi BFS vs DFS ka sabse saaf example hai.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def min_depth(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: khaali tree
        return 0                                  # 2
    queue = deque([root])                         # 3
    depth = 0                                     # 4: kitne levels utar chuke hain
    while queue:                                  # 5
        depth += 1                                # 6: naya level shuru -- PEHLE badhao
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 7: snapshot
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 8
            node = queue.popleft()                # 9
            if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 10: LEAF mila?
                return depth                      # 11: TURANT return -- yahi minimum hai
            if node.left is not None:             # 12
                queue.append(node.left)           # 13
            if node.right is not None:            # 14
                queue.append(node.right)          # 15
    return depth                                  # 16: theoretically unreachable

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guard. Empty tree ki depth 0. 3. queue = deque([root]). 4. depth = 0 — 0 se shuru, 1 se nahi, kyunki line 6 loop ke andar sabse pehle badhati hai. Root wale level par depth 1 ban jaata hai — sahi. 5. while queue:. 6. depth += 1 — level_size lene se pehle badhaya. Yeh order deliberate hai: is waqt queue mein jo level hai, uski depth depth hai. Agar loop ke aakhir mein badhate toh line 11 galat value return karti. 7-9. Standard. 10. if node.left is None and node.right is None: — leaf ki poori definition. and hai, or nahi. Ek bachcha wala node leaf nahi hai. 11. return depth — early return, yehi poora optimisation hai. Kyun yeh sahi hai: BFS levels ko strictly badhte order mein visit karta hai. Toh pehla leaf jo mile, uski depth se kam koi leaf ho hi nahi sakta. 12-15. Bachche add. 16. return depth — defensive. Har non-empty binary tree mein kam se kam ek leaf hota hai (kyunki tree finite hai aur cycles nahi hain), toh line 11 hamesha hit hoti hai. Lekin function ko total banana acchi habit hai.

    Dry run — 3 / (9, 20), 20 / (15, 7) (expected 2)

    Outer iter depth (after line 6) level_size queue (start) Nodes checked Leaf? Action
    1 1 1 [3] 3 (left=9, right=20) No add 9, 20
    2 2 2 [9, 20] 9 (left=None, right=None) Yes return 2

    Answer 2. Aur dhyaan do — 20, 15, 7 kabhi visit hi nahi hue. DFS ko woh sab dekhne padte.

    Dry run — right-skewed chain 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 (har node ka sirf right child), expected 5

    Yeh case deliberately chuna hai kyunki yahan BFS ka early-return koi fayda nahi deta — poora tree traverse hota hai. Har algorithm ka worst case dekhna zaroori hai, sirf best case nahi.

    Outer iter depth level_size queue Node Leaf? Action
    1 1 1 [2] 2 (right=3) No add 3
    2 2 1 [3] 3 (right=4) No add 4
    3 3 1 [4] 4 (right=5) No add 5
    4 4 1 [5] 5 (right=6) No add 6
    5 5 1 [6] 6 (no children) Yes return 5

    Answer 5. Sahi.

    Dry run — jahan naive DFS fail hota — root 1 with only right child 2

    Naive DFS: 1 + min(min_depth(None), min_depth(2)) = 1 + min(0, 1) = 1. Galat. Sahi DFS: line 9 (root.left is None) → 1 + min_depth_dfs(2) = 1 + 1 = 2. Sahi. BFS:

    Outer iter depth Node Leaf? Action
    1 1 1 (left=None, right=2) left is None and right is None → False add 2
    2 2 2 (no children) Yes return 2

    Answer 2. BFS ne yeh bug automatically avoid kar diya, kyunki None bachche queue mein add hi nahi hote.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n) worst case, lekin practically bahut kam — sirf minimum depth tak ke levels visit hote hain. Ek tree jismein root ka left child leaf hai aur right subtree mein 10^6 nodes hain: BFS 3 nodes dekhta hai, DFS 10^6. Worst case kab O(n) hai: perfect binary tree, jahan pehla leaf sabse aakhri level par hai — tab lagbhag saare nodes visit hote hain.
    • Space: O(w). Skewed tree par O(1); perfect tree par O(n/2).

    BFS vs DFS yahan:

    BFS DFS
    Nodes visited minimum depth tak poora tree
    Space O(width) O(height)
    Skewed tree O(1) space, O(n) time O(n) space, O(n) time
    Wide shallow tree O(n) space, fast O(log n) space, poora traverse

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None 0 Guard
    Single node 1 1 Root hi leaf hai
    Only left child 1 with left 2 2 Line 10 root par False
    Only right child 1 with right 2 2 Same — naive DFS yahan galat hota
    Perfect tree depth 3 7 nodes 3 Sabhi leaves level 3 par
    One shallow leaf root, left leaf, huge right subtree 2 BFS turant ruk jaata
    Left skewed 10^5 — 10^5 Space O(1), time O(n)

    Variations

    • Maximum depth (LeetCode 104) — yahan DFS behtar hai kyunki poora tree waise bhi dekhna hai, aur DFS ka code teen line ka hai: 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). Aur None wala bug nahi aata kyunki max sahi kaam karta hai.
    • Minimum depth ka path bhi lauta do — har queue entry mein (node, path) rakho, ya parent map.
    • N-ary tree ki min depth — node.children par loop; leaf = not node.children.
    • Graph mein shortest path — bilkul yehi BFS, plus visited set (tree mein cycles nahi hote isliye set nahi chahiye).
    • Depth of the deepest leaf — max depth.

    Interview answer: "This is the cleanest example of when BFS beats DFS. BFS visits levels in strictly increasing order, so the first leaf I encounter is at the minimum depth by construction — I return immediately and never look at the rest of the tree. DFS has to explore everything, because it can't know whether a shallower leaf exists somewhere else.

    Concretely: a root whose left child is a leaf and whose right subtree has a million nodes. BFS reads three nodes. DFS reads a million.

    There's a specific bug I'd flag in the recursive version. Writing one plus the min of the two subtree depths is wrong, because a null child returns zero and gets treated as a valid path of length zero — so a node with only one child reports depth one even though it isn't a leaf. The recursive solution has to special-case a missing child and just descend the side that exists. BFS sidesteps that entirely because I never enqueue null children.

    Two ordering details in my loop: I increment the depth before taking the level-size snapshot, so the depth I return matches the level I'm currently draining. And the leaf test is 'both children are null' — with an and, not an or.

    Worst case O(n) time, but typically far less. Space is O of the width.

    Worth contrasting: for maximum depth I'd use DFS instead, since I have to see the whole tree anyway and the recursive version is three lines — and the null-child problem doesn't arise there because max handles it correctly."

    Problem 7.6 — Binary Tree Right Side View¶

    Problem statement

    Kalpana karo ki aap tree ke dayein taraf khade ho. Jo nodes aapko dikhenge, unhe upar se neeche ke order mein lauta do.

    Input:      1
           / \
          2   3
           \   \
            5   4

Output: [1, 3, 4]
        (level 0 se 1 dikhta hai, level 1 se 3, level 2 se 4)

Input:      1
           /
          2
         /
        3
Output: [1, 2, 3]
        (koi right child nahi, toh left wale hi dikhte hain)

    Dhyaan do: "right side view" ka matlab "sirf right children" nahi hai — matlab hai har level ka aakhri (right-most) node, chahe woh left child ho.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    7.1 chalao, phir har level ka aakhri element lo.

    def right_view_brute(root):
    levels = level_order(root)                    # 1: nested list
    return [level[-1] for level in levels]        # 2: har level ka aakhri element

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. Reuse.
    2. level[-1] — Python ka negative indexing aakhri element deta hai. level[len(level)-1] bhi wahi hai lekin lamba. levels mein koi khaali level nahi hota (BFS khaali level nahi banata), toh [-1] safe hai.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) — poora nested list.

    Isme problem kya hai

    Wahi Problem 7.4 wali baat — hum har level ke saare nodes store karte hain jabki sirf ek chahiye. Bade wide tree par yeh O(n) space hai jabki O(w) queue ke alawa kuch nahi chahiye.

    The insight

    BFS mein har level left-to-right process hota hai. Toh level ka aakhri processed node hi right-most hai.

    Inner loop mein index track karo: if i == level_size - 1 par node ko record karo. Bas.

    Aur ek alternative bhi hai jo bolna acha lagta hai: current_level list banao hi mat, bas ek variable mein "last seen node" rakho aur level khatam hone par usko record karo. Dono barabar hain; index-based version zyada explicit hai.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import deque

def right_side_view(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return []                                 # 2
    result = []                                   # 3
    queue = deque([root])                         # 4
    while queue:                                  # 5
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 6: snapshot
        for i in range(level_size):               # 7: INDEX chahiye, isliye `_` nahi
            node = queue.popleft()                # 8
            if i == level_size - 1:               # 9: is level ka AAKHRI node?
                result.append(node.val)           # 10: yehi dikhta hai right se
            if node.left is not None:             # 11: bachche add -- ORDER matter karta hai
                queue.append(node.left)           # 12
            if node.right is not None:            # 13
                queue.append(node.right)          # 14
    return result                                 # 15

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-6. Standard BFS setup. 7. for i in range(level_size): — i chahiye, isliye _ nahi likha. Yeh chhoti si baat hai lekin _ ka matlab "yeh variable use nahi hoga" hota hai, aur yahan hoga. 8. node = queue.popleft(). 9. if i == level_size - 1: — level_size - 1 last index hai (0-indexed). i == level_size kabhi True nahi hoga (loop pehle hi khatam), aur i == level_size - 1 exactly ek baar per level True hota hai. Yeh check kaam karta hai kyunki BFS left-to-right process karta hai — jo lines 11-14 guarantee karti hain. 10. result.append(node.val). 11-14. left pehle, right baad — yeh line 9 ki correctness ke liye zaroori hai. Agar order ulta kar dein toh har level ka "aakhri" node actually left-most ho jaata aur yeh function left side view de deta. 15. Return.

    Left side view chahiye toh: line 9 ko if i == 0: kar do. Ek character ka change.

    DFS alternative (interviewer aksar poochta hai, aur yeh version thoda counter-intuitive hai isliye samajhna zaroori hai):

    def right_side_view_dfs(root):
    result = []                                   # 16: index = level
    def dfs(node, level):                         # 17
        if node is None:                          # 18
            return                                # 19
        if level == len(result):                  # 20: is level par PEHLI baar aaye?
            result.append(node.val)               # 21: toh yehi right-most hai
        dfs(node.right, level + 1)                # 22: RIGHT PEHLE -- yehi trick hai
        dfs(node.left, level + 1)                 # 23
    dfs(root, 0)                                  # 24
    return result                                 # 25

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. result — index level par us level ka answer.
    2. if level == len(result): — matlab "is level ka koi node abhi tak record nahi hua." Kyunki result hamesha contiguous bharta hai (level 0, phir 1, phir 2...), len(result) hi agla khaali level hai.
    3. result.append(node.val). 22-23. right pehle, left baad — yeh order hi poora solution hai. Kyunki hum right subtree mein pehle utarte hain, har level par sabse pehle jo node milta hai woh right-most hota hai. Aur line 20 sirf pehli baar record karta hai. Toh baad mein left side se aane wale nodes ignore ho jaate hain. Agar order ulta karein (left pehle) toh yeh left side view de dega. 24-25.

    Time O(n), Space O(h) recursion stack. Skewed tree par O(n) stack — BFS ki O(w) space wahan better hai.

    Dry run — BFS — tree:

          1
     / \
    2   3
     \   \
      5   4
    Outer iter queue (start) level_size i node i == size-1? Recorded Children added
    1 [1] 1 0 1 0 == 0 Yes 1 2, 3
    2 [2, 3] 2 0 2 0 == 1 No — 5 (right only)
    2 [3, 5] 2 1 3 1 == 1 Yes 3 4 (right only)
    3 [5, 4] 2 0 5 0 == 1 No — none
    3 [4] 2 1 4 1 == 1 Yes 4 none
    4 [] — — exit — — —

    Result [1, 3, 4]. Sahi.

    Dry run — BFS — left-only chain 1 -> 2 -> 3 (sab left children)

    Outer iter queue level_size i node i == size-1? Recorded
    1 [1] 1 0 1 Yes 1
    2 [2] 1 0 2 Yes 2
    3 [3] 1 0 3 Yes 3

    Result [1, 2, 3]. Sahi — koi right child nahi hai lekin phir bhi answer aaya, jo confirm karta hai ki "right side view" ka matlab "right children" nahi hai.

    Dry run — DFS — pehla wala tree

    Call order node level level == len(result)? result after
    1 1 0 0 == 0 Yes [1]
    2 3 (right of 1) 1 1 == 1 Yes [1, 3]
    3 4 (right of 3) 2 2 == 2 Yes [1, 3, 4]
    4 None (right of 4) 3 — return
    5 None (left of 4) 3 — return
    6 None (left of 3) 2 — return
    7 2 (left of 1) 1 1 == 2 No [1, 3, 4]
    8 5 (right of 2) 2 2 == 3 No [1, 3, 4]
    9 None × 2 — — return
    10 None (left of 2) — — return

    Result [1, 3, 4]. Sahi.

    Steps 7 aur 8 dekho — 2 aur 5 visit toh hue lekin record nahi hue, kyunki unke levels pehle hi bhare ja chuke the. Line 20 ka check hi filter hai.

    Complexity

    BFS: - Time: O(n). - Space: O(w). Wide tree par O(n/2), skewed par O(1).

    DFS: - Time: O(n). - Space: O(h). Skewed par O(n), balanced par O(log n).

    Kaunsa chunein: agar tree deep aur narrow hai toh BFS; agar wide aur shallow hai toh DFS. Yeh trade-off bolna bahut acha lagta hai.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None [] Guard
    Single 1 [1] Ek level
    Only left children 1->2->3 (left) [1,2,3] Har level mein ek hi node
    Only right children 1->2->3 (right) [1,2,3] Same
    Perfect tree 7 nodes [1,3,7] Har level ka right-most
    Left subtree deeper root, left chain of 3, right leaf [1, right, left2, left3] Deep left level ka aakhri node left hi hai
    Duplicate values 1,1,1 [1,1] Values matter nahi

    Row 6 sabse important hai — jab right subtree khatam ho jaata hai toh left subtree ke nodes hi "right side view" ban jaate hain. Yeh exactly woh case hai jo naive "sirf right children follow karo" solution ko todta hai.

    Variations

    • Left side view — BFS mein i == 0, ya DFS mein left pehle.
    • Har level ka aakhri node ka poora node object (value nahi) — result.append(node).
    • Bottom view / top view — horizontal distance track karni padti hai, alag problem (hash map with column index).
    • Vertical order traversal (LeetCode 987) — column index plus sorting.
    • Boundary traversal (545) — left boundary + leaves + right boundary reversed.
    • N-ary tree right view — node.children[-1] se recurse.

    Interview answer: "First I'd clarify what the right side view means, because the name misleads: it's the last node of every level, not the chain of right children. If the right subtree ends early, left-side nodes become visible.

    With BFS it's a one-line addition to level order. I already snapshot the level size, so inside the inner loop I just check whether the index equals level size minus one, and record that node. That works because I enqueue left children before right, which makes each level come out left to right — flip that and I'd get the left side view instead. So a right side view is i == level_size - 1 and a left side view is i == 0.

    I could also run the plain level order and take the last element of each sublist. Same time, but it materialises every level when I only need one node from each.

    There's a neat DFS version too: recurse right child first, and record a node only when its level index equals the current result length — meaning it's the first node I've reached at that depth. Because I always go right first, the first node reached at any depth is the right-most one. It reads a little backwards but it's four lines.

    Which one I'd ship depends on shape: BFS is O(width) space, DFS is O(height). For a deep narrow tree BFS wins; for a wide shallow tree DFS wins. Both are O(n) time."

    Problem 7.7 — Connect Level Order Siblings (Next Right Pointers)¶

    Problem statement

    Har node mein ek extra pointer next hai. Use apne right side ke padosi (same level ka agla node) se jodo. Har level ke aakhri node ka next None rahega.

    Input:      1                    Output:      1 -> None
           / \                               / \
          2   3                             2 -> 3 -> None
         / \   \                           / \    \
        4   5   7                         4->5 -> 7 -> None

    Do versions hain aur unka farq important hai: - Perfect binary tree (LeetCode 116) — har node ke ya toh 0 ya 2 bachche, aur saare leaves ek hi level par. Yeh O(1) space mein possible hai. - Koi bhi binary tree (LeetCode 117) — gaps ho sakte hain. Yeh mushkil hai.

    Main dono karunga.

    Pehla instinct — brute force (BFS)

    Level order karo aur har level ke andar consecutive nodes jodo.

    class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None, nxt=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.next = nxt                           # extra pointer


from collections import deque

def connect_bfs(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return root                               # 2
    queue = deque([root])                         # 3
    while queue:                                  # 4
        level_size = len(queue)                   # 5: snapshot
        prev = None                               # 6: is level ka pichhla node
        for _ in range(level_size):               # 7
            node = queue.popleft()                # 8
            if prev is not None:                  # 9: pehla node nahi hai?
                prev.next = node                  # 10: pichhle ko current se jodo
            prev = node                           # 11: current ab pichhla ban gaya
            if node.left is not None:             # 12
                queue.append(node.left)           # 13
            if node.right is not None:            # 14
                queue.append(node.right)          # 15
        # prev ab level ka aakhri node hai; uska next None hi rehta hai (default)
    return root                                   # 16

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guard. return root (na ki return None) — signature consistent rakhta hai. 3-5. Standard. 6. prev = None — har level ke shuru mein reset. Yeh line andar wale loop ke bahar aur outer loop ke andar honi chahiye. Agar isko outer loop ke bahar rakh dete toh ek level ka aakhri node agle level ke pehle node se jud jaata — cross-level connection, jo bilkul galat hai. 9-10. if prev is not None: prev.next = node — pehle node ke liye prev None hai, toh kuch nahi hota. Baaki sab ke liye pichhle ko current se jod diya. 11. prev = node. 12-15. Standard. 16. return root — structure badla, head nahi.

    Aakhri node ka next: loop khatam hone par prev level ka aakhri node hai aur uska next kabhi set nahi hua — toh woh apni default value (None) par hi rehta hai. Explicit prev.next = None likhne ki zaroorat nahi, jab tak nodes recycled na ho rahe hon.

    Complexity: Time O(n), Space O(w) — queue. Perfect tree par O(n/2).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Problem constraint bolti hai O(1) extra space (recursion stack ko chhod kar). BFS ki queue O(w) hai, jo perfect tree par O(n) hai. Toh yeh solution constraint todta hai.

    The insight

    Yeh problem ka sabse pyaara idea hai: jo next pointers hum abhi bana rahe hain, unhe hum turant traversal ke liye use kar sakte hain.

    Yaani hum level k ke next pointers use karke level k par left-to-right chal sakte hain, aur chalte chalte level k+1 ke next pointers bana sakte hain. Queue ki zaroorat hi nahi — tree khud apni queue ban jaata hai.

    Perfect binary tree mein yeh aur bhi simple ho jaata hai kyunki do rules kaafi hain: 1. node.left.next = node.right — apne hi do bachchon ko jodo. 2. node.right.next = node.next.left — apne right bachche ko, apne padosi ke left bachche se jodo. (Aur node.next pehle se ban chuka hai kyunki hum upar wale level ko pehle process karte hain.)

    Optimal solution — perfect binary tree, O(1) space

    def connect_perfect(root):
    if root is None:                              # 1: guard
        return root                               # 2
    leftmost = root                               # 3: har level ka pehla node
    while leftmost.left is not None:              # 4: agla level exist karta hai?
        head = leftmost                           # 5: is level par chalne wala pointer
        while head is not None:                   # 6: level ke aakhir tak
            head.left.next = head.right           # 7: RULE 1 -- apne bachche jodo
            if head.next is not None:             # 8: dayein padosi hai?
                head.right.next = head.next.left  # 9: RULE 2 -- gap ke paar jodo
            head = head.next                      # 10: PICHHLE level ke next se aage badho
        leftmost = leftmost.left                  # 11: agle level ke pehle node par utro
    return root                                   # 12

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. Guard. 3. leftmost = root — har level ka left-most node. Yeh "level down" karne ka anchor hai. 4. while leftmost.left is not None: — leftmost.left check kar rahe hain, leftmost nahi. Kyun? Kyunki hum agle level ke pointers bana rahe hain. Agar leftmost.left None hai toh hum leaf level par hain aur neeche kuch nahi hai — kaam khatam. Perfect tree hone ki wajah se leftmost.left is None matlab leftmost.right bhi None. 5. head = leftmost — is level par chalne wala pointer. 6. while head is not None: — level ke aakhri node tak. 7. head.left.next = head.right — Rule 1. Perfect tree mein head.left aur head.right dono guaranteed exist karte hain (line 4 ne confirm kiya). 8. if head.next is not None: — kya head ka dayein padosi hai? Yeh pointer pichhle iteration mein bana tha (jab hum ek level upar the). 9. head.right.next = head.next.left — Rule 2, aur yeh poore solution ka dil hai. head ka right bachcha aur head.next ka left bachcha same level par padosi hain, lekin unka koi common parent nahi hai. Normal traversal se unhe jodna mushkil hai — lekin head.next pointer hi woh bridge hai jo pichhle round mein banaya tha. 10. head = head.next — is level par aage badhne ke liye next pointer use kar rahe hain, queue nahi. Yehi O(1) space ka poora raaz hai. 11. leftmost = leftmost.left — ek level neeche. Perfect tree mein left-most child hamesha leftmost.left hai. 12. Return.

    Kyun yeh perfect tree ke bina toot jaata hai: line 7 head.left.next maanti hai ki head.left exist karta hai. Agar kisi node ka sirf right child ho toh AttributeError. Aur line 9 maanti hai ki head.next.left exist karta hai. General tree mein dono assumptions galat hain.

    Optimal solution — koi bhi binary tree, O(1) space

    def connect_any(root):
    current = root                                # 1: is level par chalne wala pointer
    while current is not None:                    # 2: har level ke liye
        dummy = Node(0)                           # 3: AGLE level ka fake head
        tail = dummy                              # 4: agle level mein ab tak ka aakhri node
        while current is not None:                # 5: is level ko poora chalo
            if current.left is not None:          # 6: left bachcha hai?
                tail.next = current.left          # 7: agle level ki chain mein jodo
                tail = tail.next                  # 8: tail aage
            if current.right is not None:         # 9: right bachcha hai?
                tail.next = current.right         # 10
                tail = tail.next                  # 11
            current = current.next                # 12: is level par aage
        current = dummy.next                      # 13: agle level ke PEHLE node par utro
    return root                                   # 14

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. current = root.
    2. while current is not None: — outer loop har level ke liye.
    3. dummy = Node(0) — dummy node phir se, aur wajah wahi hai jo linked list mein thi. Agle level ka pehla node kaun hoga, yeh pehle se nahi pata (gaps ki wajah se). Dummy hone se hum bina if first_node is None type checks ke chain bana sakte hain, aur dummy.next hi answer de deta hai. Har level ke liye naya dummy banate hain — line 3 outer loop ke andar hai.
    4. tail = dummy — agle level ki chain ka aakhri node.
    5. while current is not None: — is level par next pointers use karke chal rahe hain (jo pichhle round mein bane the). Root level par root.next None hai toh ek hi iteration. 6-8. Left bachcha ho toh chain mein jodo. 9-11. Right bachcha ho toh chain mein jodo. Lines 6-11 ka poora point yeh hai ki hum "kya bachcha exist karta hai" check kar rahe hain — perfect tree wale version mein yeh assume kiya gaya tha.
    6. current = current.next — is level par aage.
    7. current = dummy.next — agle level ka pehla node. Agar agle level mein koi node nahi tha toh dummy.next None hai aur line 2 loop khatam kar degi. Yeh natural termination hai — alag se check nahi chahiye.
    8. Return.

    Yeh version perfect tree par bhi kaam karta hai — toh agar aap ek hi solution yaad rakhna chahte ho toh yehi rakho. Perfect-tree version thoda chhota aur thoda faster hai lekin universal nahi.

    Dry run — perfect tree version — tree:

            1
       / \
      2   3
     / \ / \
    4  5 6  7

    Outer iteration 1: leftmost = 1. 1.left = 2 (not None) → enter.

    Inner step head Rule 1 head.next? Rule 2 head after
    1 1 2.next = 3 1.next is None — None
    exit — — — — —

    Level 1 ke pointers: 2 -> 3 -> None. Line 11: leftmost = 1.left = 2.

    Outer iteration 2: 2.left = 4 (not None) → enter.

    Inner step head Rule 1 head.next? Rule 2 head after
    1 2 4.next = 5 2.next = 3 Yes 5.next = 3.left = 6 3
    2 3 6.next = 7 3.next is None — None
    exit — — — — —

    Level 2 ke pointers: 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> None.

    Dhyaan do step 1 par: 5.next = 6 — yeh do nodes alag parents ke bachche hain (5 ka parent 2, 6 ka parent 3). Unhe jodne ka ekmatra raasta 2.next = 3 tha, jo pichhle level par bana tha. Yehi Rule 2 ka poora point hai.

    Line 11: leftmost = 2.left = 4. Outer iteration 3: 4.left is None → loop exit. Return.

    Dry run — general version — non-perfect tree:

          1
     / \
    2   3
   /     \
  4       7

    Outer iteration 1: current = 1. dummy1, tail = dummy1.

    Inner step current left? right? Chain built tail current after
    1 1 2 → dummy1.next = 2, tail=2 3 → 2.next = 3, tail=3 dummy1 -> 2 -> 3 3 1.next = None
    exit None — — — — —

    Line 13: current = dummy1.next = 2. Level 1 connected: 2 -> 3 -> None.

    Outer iteration 2: current = 2. dummy2, tail = dummy2.

    Inner step current left? right? Chain built tail current after
    1 2 4 → dummy2.next = 4, tail=4 None → skip dummy2 -> 4 4 2.next = 3
    2 3 None → skip 7 → 4.next = 7, tail=7 dummy2 -> 4 -> 7 7 3.next = None
    exit None — — — — —

    Line 13: current = dummy2.next = 4. Level 2 connected: 4 -> 7 -> None.

    Step 2 sabse important hai — 4 aur 7 ke parents alag hain aur beech mein do missing children hain (2.right aur 3.left). Perfect-tree wale rules yahan crash karte. Dummy-plus-tail version bilkul naturally handle kar leta hai, kyunki woh sirf "jo bachche mile unhe chain mein jodta jao" karta hai.

    Outer iteration 3: current = 4. dummy3. 4 ke koi bachche nahi, 4.next = 7, 7 ke koi bachche nahi. Chain khaali. Line 13: current = dummy3.next = None → loop exit. Return.

    Complexity

    BFS version: - Time: O(n). Space: O(w) — perfect tree par O(n/2).

    Perfect-tree O(1) version: - Time: O(n). Har node ek baar visit. - Space: O(1). Sirf do pointers.

    General O(1) version: - Time: O(n). - Space: O(1). Ek dummy node per level, lekin ek waqt par ek hi zinda rehta hai — constant.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Behaviour Kyun
    Empty None Return None Guard / loop condition
    Single node 1 1.next stays None Koi agla level nahi
    Two levels perfect 1 with 2,3 2.next = 3 Rule 1
    Only left children 1->2->3 (left) Sab next None Har level mein ek node
    Missing middle children Upar wala dry run 4 -> 7 General version chahiye
    Perfect depth 4 15 nodes Har level poori chain
    Already connected — Overwrite ho jaate Function idempotent hai
    Single child at every node skewed Sab None Har level mein ek node

    Variations

    • Populating Next Right Pointers II (LeetCode 117) — general version, upar.
    • Left pointers connect karo — right-to-left traverse karo.
    • Har level ko linked list ke roop mein lauta do — dummy.next collect karte jao.
    • Next pointers ka use karke level order print karo — leftmost se shuru karke next follow karo. Yeh ek accha follow-up hai jo dikhata hai ki structure kaam kar raha hai.
    • Ek do-dishaon wala (prev bhi) version — doubly linked levels.

    Interview answer: "The BFS version is straightforward — level order, and inside each level I keep a previous pointer and link it to the current node. But that uses a queue, which is O of the width, and the problem asks for constant space.

    The idea that gets me there: the next pointers I'm building on one level are themselves a way to traverse that level. So I process levels top down, and to walk across a level I follow the next pointers I built during the previous round. The tree becomes its own queue.

    For a perfect binary tree that's two rules. A node links its own left child to its own right child. And it links its right child to its neighbour's left child — where 'its neighbour' is exactly the next pointer built one level up. That second rule is the interesting one, because those two nodes are adjacent but have different parents, and the only bridge between them is the link from the level above.

    For an arbitrary tree those rules break, because children can be missing on either side. There I use a dummy node per level plus a tail pointer: walk the current level via next pointers, and append whatever children exist onto the next level's chain. Then dummy.next is the start of the next level. If it's null, there is no next level and the loop ends naturally — no separate check needed. That's the same dummy-node technique from linked list problems, and it's what makes the gaps a non-issue.

    Both are O(n) time and O(1) extra space. The general version also handles perfect trees, so if I could only remember one, I'd remember that one."

    Ek line mein poore pattern ka summary: deque, while queue, level_size = len(queue) ka snapshot, aur ek inner for loop. Har problem sirf yeh badalti hai ki inner loop ke andar kya record karna hai aur level khatam hone par kya karna hai.

    8. Tree DFS¶

    Recognition signals — aap tree DFS dekh rahe ho jab problem bole¶

    • "root to leaf path" — kisi bhi tarah ka path, sum, ya sequence.
    • "all paths", "count paths", "path exists" — path ka matlab hi "ek raasta neeche tak", jo DFS ka natural output hai.
    • "maximum depth", "height", "balanced hai ya nahi" — subtree ki information chahiye.
    • "diameter", "maximum path sum" — har node par uske dono subtrees ka result chahiye.
    • "subtree" shabd aaye — jaise "identical subtree", "sum of subtree", "largest BST subtree".
    • "validate BST", "serialize/deserialize", "lowest common ancestor".
    • Problem mein har node par ek decision ho jo neeche ke results par depend karta ho.

    DFS ke teen orders — aur kab kaunsa¶

          1
     / \
    2   3
   / \
  4   5
    Order Rule Output Kab use karo
    Preorder node → left → right 1, 2, 4, 5, 3 Tree copy karna, serialize karna, path banate hue neeche jaana
    Inorder left → node → right 4, 2, 5, 1, 3 BST mein sorted order deta hai — yeh sabse important use hai
    Postorder left → right → node 4, 5, 2, 3, 1 Bachchon ka result chahiye node ka answer nikaalne ke liye (height, diameter, delete tree)

    Yeh choose karne ka rule ek line mein: agar node ka answer uske bachchon ke answers par depend karta hai, toh postorder. Agar aap upar se neeche information le ja rahe ho (jaise running sum ya path), toh preorder.

    Bahut si problems mein dono hote hain — preorder mein neeche state le jao, postorder mein upar result laao. Diameter aur max path sum exactly aise hain.

    Do tarah ke DFS problems — yeh distinction hi sab kuch hai¶

    Type A — top-down (information neeche le jao). Har call mein parent se kuch milta hai (running sum, current path, depth), aur leaf par pahunch kar decision hota hai.

    def dfs(node, state_from_parent):
    if node is None: return
    new_state = update(state_from_parent, node)
    if is_leaf(node): record(new_state)
    dfs(node.left, new_state)
    dfs(node.right, new_state)

    Type B — bottom-up (information upar laao). Har call bachchon se result maangti hai, phir apna result banati hai.

    def dfs(node):
    if node is None: return base_value
    left_result = dfs(node.left)
    right_result = dfs(node.right)
    return combine(left_result, right_result, node)

    Interview mein sabse pehle yeh decide karo ki problem Type A hai ya Type B ya dono — uske baad code apne aap likha jaata hai.

    Template code¶

    class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


def dfs_top_down(root, target):
    """Type A: root se leaf tak state carry karo."""
    def helper(node, remaining):
        if node is None:                     # khaali subtree -> koi path nahi
            return False
        remaining -= node.val                # state update (LOCAL copy, parent ka nahi badla)
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # leaf?
            return remaining == 0            # decision yahan hota hai
        return helper(node.left, remaining) or helper(node.right, remaining)
    return helper(root, target)


def dfs_bottom_up(root):
    """Type B: bachchon se result lo, apna banao."""
    def helper(node):
        if node is None:                     # base case -- neutral value
            return 0
        left = helper(node.left)             # bachche ka result
        right = helper(node.right)
        return 1 + max(left, right)          # apna result banao
    return helper(root)

    Recursion ke bina bhi DFS likh sakte hain — ek explicit stack se. Aur ismein ek chhoti si baat hai jo confuse karti hai: stack mein right pehle push karte hain taaki left pehle pop ho. Kyunki stack LIFO hai — jo aakhir mein daala woh pehle nikalta hai. BFS mein iska bilkul ulta tha (left pehle append, kyunki queue FIFO hai). Yeh do lines interview mein galat likhi jaati hain.

    def preorder_iterative(root):
    if root is None:
        return []
    result = []
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()                   # LIFO
        result.append(node.val)
        if node.right is not None:           # right PEHLE push
            stack.append(node.right)
        if node.left is not None:            # left BAAD mein push -> pehle pop hoga
            stack.append(node.left)
    return result

    Recursion limit — yeh production mein matter karta hai¶

    Python ka default recursion limit 1000 hai. Ek skewed tree (jo linked list jaisa ho) 10^5 nodes ka ho toh RecursionError aayega. Interview mein yeh mention karna maturity dikhata hai:

    import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(10 ** 6)     # quick fix, lekin stack overflow ka risk hai

    Asli fix iterative version likhna hai. Interview mein recursive likho (padhne mein aasan) aur bolo ki production mein iterative jaayega.

    Problem 8.1 — Binary Tree Path Sum¶

    Problem statement

    Ek binary tree aur ek number target diya hai. Bataao ki koi root-to-leaf path hai jiske saare values ka sum target ke barabar ho.

    Input:      5
           / \
          4   8
         /   / \
        11  13  4
       / \       \
      7   2       1
target = 22

Output: True    (5 -> 4 -> 11 -> 2 = 22)

Input: root = [1, 2], target = 1
Output: False   (1 akela leaf nahi hai; 1->2 ka sum 3 hai)

    Dhyaan do: path root se leaf tak poora hona chahiye. Beech mein ruk kar sum match hona count nahi hota.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Saare root-to-leaf paths generate karo, phir har ek ka sum check karo.

    def has_path_sum_brute(root, target):
    all_paths = []                                # 1: saare complete paths
    def collect(node, path):                      # 2
        if node is None:                          # 3
            return                                # 4
        path = path + [node.val]                  # 5: NAYA list -- copy banayi
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 6: leaf
            all_paths.append(path)                # 7: poora path save
            return                                # 8
        collect(node.left, path)                  # 9
        collect(node.right, path)                 # 10
    collect(root, [])                             # 11
    for path in all_paths:                        # 12: har path ka sum check
        if sum(path) == target:                   # 13
            return True                           # 14
    return False                                  # 15

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. all_paths = [] — saare paths store ho rahe hain. Yehi problem hai. 2-4. Standard.
    2. path = path + [node.val] — path.append(...) NAHI likha. + ek naya list banata hai, jo har branch ko apna independent copy deta hai. append shared list ko modify karta aur sibling branches ek dusre ka data dekh lete. (Sahi tarika append ke saath backtracking hai — Problem 8.2 mein.) Cost: har call par O(depth) copy → total O(n * h). 6-8. Leaf par path save. 9-10. Recurse.
    3. collect(root, []). 12-15. Sab paths ban jaane ke BAAD sum check. Yeh sabse bada waste hai — hum jaante hain ki jaise hi ek match mile hum ruk sakte hain.

    Complexity: Time O(n * h) paths banane ke liye plus O(total path lengths) checking ke liye. Space O(n * h) — saare paths store hote hain. Skewed tree par O(n^2).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Teen alag waste hain: 1. Saare paths store ho rahe hain jabki humein sirf ek boolean chahiye. 2. Har path ka sum baad mein calculate ho raha hai jabki neeche jaate waqt hi ho sakta tha. 3. Pehla match milne par bhi baaki paths banate rehte hain.

    The insight

    Path ka sum neeche jaate waqt hi track kar lo — ek running number, ek list nahi.

    Aur ek chhoti si elegance: sum badhane ke bajaye target ghatate jao. Toh leaf par sirf ek check bachta hai: remaining == 0. Yeh do variables (running sum aur target) ko ek variable (remaining) mein badal deta hai.

    Aur or short-circuit karta hai — toh jaise hi left subtree mein path mil jaaye, right subtree traverse hi nahi hoga. Early exit free mein mil jaata hai.

    Optimal solution

    def has_path_sum(root, target):
    if root is None:                              # 1: khaali tree mein koi path nahi
        return False                              # 2

    remaining = target - root.val                 # 3: is node ko "kharch" kar diya

    if root.left is None and root.right is None:  # 4: LEAF par pahunch gaye?
        return remaining == 0                     # 5: poora target kharch hua?

    return (has_path_sum(root.left, remaining)    # 6: left mein try karo
            or has_path_sum(root.right, remaining))   # 7: ya right mein

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. root is None par False, remaining == 0 nahi. Yeh critical hai. Ek node jiska sirf left child hai: uske right side par recursion None par pahunchegi. Agar hum wahan remaining == 0 check karte, toh ek adhoora path (jo leaf tak pahuncha hi nahi) galti se valid maan liya jaata. Example: tree 1 -> 2 (left only), target = 1. Agar None par remaining == 0 check karte: root 1, remaining = 0, root leaf nahi hai, toh has_path_sum(None, 0) → 0 == 0 → True. Galat — sahi answer False hai kyunki 1 leaf nahi hai. return False likhne se yeh bug nahi aata. 3. remaining = target - root.val — ghatate ja rahe hain, jodte nahi. Alternative current_sum + root.val bhi kaam karta lekin phir leaf par current_sum == target check karna padta — do variables carry karne padte. Subtract karne se ek hi variable chahiye.
