Aur ek local variable hai — parent ka target bilkul nahi badla, kyunki integers immutable hain aur yeh ek naya binding hai. Toh sibling calls ek dusre ko affect nahi karti. (Agar target ek mutable list hota toh yeh baat alag hoti — Problem 8.2 mein wohi issue aayega.) 4. if root.left is None and root.right is None: — leaf ki poori definition, and ke saath. 5. return remaining == 0 — leaf par hi decision hota hai, kahin aur nahi. Yeh "root-to-leaf" requirement ko enforce karta hai. 6-7. or — short-circuit. Agar left subtree mein path mil gaya toh right kabhi call hi nahi hoga. Yeh brute force ke "sab generate karo phir check karo" se fundamentally better hai. Aur note: yahan root.left None ho sakta hai — lekin line 1 use handle kar leti hai (False return), jo or ke liye neutral value hai. Isliye alag se if root.left is not None likhne ki zaroorat nahi.

    Negative values ke saath ek warning: agar tree mein negative values hon toh "remaining zero se neeche gaya toh ruk jao" wala pruning galat hoga, kyunki aage negative value se sum wapas badh sakta hai. Yeh solution woh pruning nahi karta, isliye safe hai. Yeh interview mein poochne wali cheez hai: "can values be negative?"

    Dry run — tree:

            5
       / \
      4   8
     /   / \
    11  13  4
   / \       \
  7   2       1
    target = 22

    Call node target in remaining Leaf? Action
    1 5 22 22-5 = 17 No recurse left(4, 17)
    2 4 17 17-4 = 13 No recurse left(11, 13)
    3 11 13 13-11 = 2 No recurse left(7, 2)
    4 7 2 2-7 = -5 Yes -5 == 0 → False
    5 2 (right of 11) 2 2-2 = 0 Yes 0 == 0 → True
    back 3 11 — — — False or True → True
    back 2 4 — — — True (left branch) → True
    back 1 5 — — — True → True, right subtree kabhi visit nahi hua

    Answer True. Aur dhyaan do — nodes 8, 13, 4, 1 bilkul touch nahi hue. Yeh or ka short-circuit hai.

    Dry run — 1 -> 2 (left only), target = 1 (expected False)

    Call node target in remaining Leaf? Action
    1 1 1 1-1 = 0 left=2 exists → No recurse both
    2 2 (left) 0 0-2 = -2 Yes -2 == 0 → False
    3 None (right) 0 — — line 2: return False
    back 1 1 — — — False or False → False

    Answer False. Sahi.

    Call 3 ko dhyaan se dekho — agar line 2 return remaining == 0 hoti toh 0 == 0 → True aata aur poora answer galat ho jaata. Yeh ek line poore solution ki correctness decide karti hai.

    Iterative version (deep tree ke liye):

    def has_path_sum_iterative(root, target):
    if root is None:                              # 8
        return False                              # 9
    stack = [(root, target - root.val)]           # 10: (node, remaining) pairs
    while stack:                                  # 11
        node, remaining = stack.pop()             # 12: LIFO
        if node.left is None and node.right is None and remaining == 0:   # 13: leaf + match
            return True                           # 14
        if node.right is not None:                # 15
            stack.append((node.right, remaining - node.right.val))   # 16
        if node.left is not None:                 # 17
            stack.append((node.left, remaining - node.left.val))     # 18
    return False                                  # 19

    Line 10 aur 16/18 mein state ko stack entry ke saath carry kar rahe hain — yeh recursion ke parameter passing ka exact equivalent hai. Line 13 mein teenon conditions ek saath (and chain). Time O(n), Space O(h) stack ke liye — lekin koi RecursionError nahi.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n) worst case. Har node at most ek baar. Short-circuit ki wajah se practically kam.
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack. Balanced tree par O(log n), skewed par O(n).

    Brute force ke O(nh) time aur O(nh) space se bahut better.

    Edge cases

    Case Input target Output Kyun
    Empty tree None 0 False Line 2 — 0 == 0 nahi!
    Single node match 5 5 True Leaf, 5-5 = 0
    Single node no match 5 3 False 3-5 = -2
    Only left child 1->2 3 True Path 1->2
    Only left child, partial 1->2 1 False 1 leaf nahi hai
    Negative values -2 -> -3 -5 True Subtraction negatives handle karta
    Zero target, zero nodes 0 0 True
    All zeros 0->0->0 0 True
    Deep skewed 10^5 — — RecursionError Iterative version chahiye

    Empty tree wala case sabse important hai — has_path_sum(None, 0) False hona chahiye, True nahi. Kyunki "no tree" mein "no path" hota hai. Kuch log target == 0 par True return kar dete hain — galat.

    Variations

    • Saare paths lauta do jinka sum target hai (LeetCode 113) — Problem 8.2.
    • Kitne paths hain jinka sum target hai, chahe kahin se kahin tak (437) — prefix sum plus hash map, Problem 8.5.
    • Minimum path sum root se leaf tak — or ki jagah min aur poora traverse.
    • Maximum path sum root se leaf tak — max.
    • Path sum in a BST — same, lekin pruning possible hai (agar sab values positive hon).
    • Any node se any node tak path sum (124) — Problem 8.7, bilkul alag technique.

    Interview answer: "I'd first confirm two things: does the path have to end at a leaf, and can node values be negative? Both change the code.

    Rather than building each path and summing it afterwards, I carry the target down and subtract each node's value as I descend. That way there's one number to pass, not a running sum plus a target, and at a leaf the check is just whether the remaining value is zero.

    The subtle part is the null base case. It must return false, not check whether the remaining is zero. If it checked, then a node with only one child would let the missing side count as a valid path — for example a root of one with a single child of two and a target of one would incorrectly report true, because the missing right child sees a remaining of zero. Returning false forces every path to actually terminate at a leaf.

    Then I combine the two subtrees with or, which short-circuits — so as soon as one side finds a path I stop exploring. That's a real saving over generating all paths and checking them afterwards.

    O(n) time worst case, O(height) space for the recursion stack. For a very deep skewed tree Python would hit its recursion limit around a thousand frames, so in production I'd write the iterative version with an explicit stack holding node-and-remaining pairs. That's the same algorithm with the state carried in the stack entry instead of the call frame."

    Problem 8.2 — All Paths For A Sum¶

    Problem statement

    Binary tree aur ek target diya hai. Saare root-to-leaf paths lauta do jinke values ka sum target hai.

    Input:      5
           / \
          4   8
         /   / \
        11  13  4
       / \     / \
      7   2   5   1
target = 22

Output: [[5, 4, 11, 2], [5, 8, 4, 5]]

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Har call mein path ka naya copy banao.

    def path_sum_brute(root, target):
    result = []                                   # 1: saare valid paths
    def dfs(node, remaining, path):               # 2
        if node is None:                          # 3
            return                                # 4
        path = path + [node.val]                  # 5: NAYA list har call mein
        remaining -= node.val                     # 6
        if node.left is None and node.right is None and remaining == 0:   # 7: leaf + match
            result.append(path)                   # 8: yeh path already ek copy hai
            return                                # 9
        dfs(node.left, remaining, path)           # 10
        dfs(node.right, remaining, path)          # 11
    dfs(root, target, [])                         # 12
    return result                                 # 13

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. result = [].
    2. def dfs(node, remaining, path): — teen state variables neeche jaate hain. 3-4. Null guard.
    3. path = path + [node.val] — har call ek naya list banati hai. Yeh correct hai, kyunki har branch ko apna independent path milta hai. Lekin cost: O(depth) copy per node, aur n nodes par O(n * h) total.
    4. remaining -= node.val — local rebinding, parent affected nahi.
    5. Leaf plus match.
    6. result.append(path) — yahan path[:] likhne ki zaroorat nahi, kyunki line 5 ne already ek fresh list banayi hai jo kisi aur ke saath share nahi hoti. 9-11. Recurse. 12-13.

    Complexity: Time O(n * h) — har node par O(h) ka list copy. Skewed tree par O(n^2). Space O(n * h) worst case (saare paths store).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Har node par ek naya list banana. Balanced tree mein h = log n toh O(n log n) — theek hai. Lekin skewed tree par O(n^2), aur zyada important: yeh ek pattern hai jo aage backtracking problems (Section 14) mein bar bar aayega, aur wahan yeh cost bardaasht nahi hoti.

    The insight

    Ek hi path list use karo, aur usko backtracking se manage karo:

    1. Node par aate waqt path.append(node.val) — choose.
    2. Bachchon ko explore karo — explore.
    3. Node se jaate waqt path.pop() — un-choose (backtrack).

    Yeh "choose, explore, un-choose" pattern hi backtracking ka poora core hai, aur yeh Section 14 (Backtracking) mein har problem mein dikhega. Yahan use pehli baar dekhna important hai.

    Aur ek zaroori detail: jab hum result mein path daalte hain, tab copy banani padti hai (path[:]), kyunki path aage badalta rahega. Yeh brute force ke ulta hai — wahan copy har call par thi, yahan sirf jab answer milta hai.

    Optimal solution

    def path_sum(root, target):
    result = []                                   # 1: saare valid paths
    path = []                                     # 2: EK hi list, shared aur mutated

    def dfs(node, remaining):                     # 3: `path` closure se aata hai
        if node is None:                          # 4
            return                                # 5

        path.append(node.val)                     # 6: CHOOSE -- path mein daalo
        remaining -= node.val                     # 7: local, immutable int

        if node.left is None and node.right is None and remaining == 0:   # 8: leaf + match
            result.append(path[:])                # 9: COPY save karo -- yeh line critical hai
        else:                                     # 10: leaf nahi ya match nahi
            dfs(node.left, remaining)             # 11: EXPLORE left
            dfs(node.right, remaining)            # 12: EXPLORE right

        path.pop()                                # 13: UN-CHOOSE -- backtrack

    dfs(root, target)                             # 14
    return result                                 # 15

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. result = [].
    2. path = [] — ek hi list, poore traversal mein shared. Yeh brute force se fundamental difference hai.
    3. def dfs(node, remaining): — path parameter mein nahi hai, closure se access hota hai. Isse yeh explicit ho jaata hai ki path shared mutable state hai. 4-5. Null guard. Note: yahan path.pop() nahi hai — kyunki path.append (line 6) abhi hua hi nahi. Agar guard ke baad pop likhte toh path corrupt ho jaata.
    4. path.append(node.val) — choose.
    5. remaining -= node.val — yeh local hai, path ki tarah shared nahi. Kyunki int immutable hai, -= ek naya binding banata hai jo sirf is call frame mein hai. Isliye remaining ko backtrack karne ki zaroorat nahi — sirf mutable state (path) ko backtrack karna hota hai. Yeh distinction bahut important hai aur log yahan confuse hote hain.
    6. Leaf plus match.
    7. result.append(path[:]) — path[:] ek shallow copy hai. Agar result.append(path) likh dein toh sab kuch toot jaata hai — kyunki result mein us same list ka reference chala jaata hai, aur line 13 ke pops us list ko khaali kar denge. Final output mein saare paths khaali lists honge. Yeh sabse classic backtracking bug hai. path[:], list(path), path.copy() — teenon barabar hain. 10-12. else zaroori hai? Nahi, technically. Agar leaf par dfs(None, ...) call karein toh woh turant return kar degi. Lekin else do faltu calls bachaata hai aur intent saaf karta hai: "yeh ek answer hai, isse aage nahi jaana." Ek important baat: agar leaf par match nahi hua toh else chalti hai aur dfs(None) do baar call hoti hai — jo harmless hai. Agar hum if leaf: ... return likh dete (line 13 se pehle return), toh path.pop() skip ho jaata aur path corrupt ho jaata. Isliye yahan return nahi hai — else hai.
    8. path.pop() — un-choose. Yeh line har raaste par chalni chahiye. Ismein sabse important yeh hai ki yeh line 9 ke baad bhi chalti hai (kyunki wahan return nahi hai) aur line 12 ke baad bhi. Har append ka exactly ek pop hona chahiye — yeh invariant hi backtracking ki correctness hai. 14-15.

    Backtracking ka mental model: path ek "current position on the map" hai. Aap aage badhte ho (append), explore karte ho, aur wapas aate waqt apna kadam wapas le lete ho (pop). Jab function return karta hai, path bilkul waisa hona chahiye jaisa function ke ghusne se pehle tha.

    Dry run — tree:

            5
       / \
      4   8
     /   / \
    11  13  4
   / \     / \
  7   2   5   1
    target = 22

    Step Call node remaining in path (after append) Leaf+match? Action
    1 dfs(5, 22) 5 22 [5] No explore
    2 dfs(4, 17) 4 17 [5,4] No explore
    3 dfs(11, 13) 11 13 [5,4,11] No explore
    4 dfs(7, 2) 7 2 [5,4,11,7] Leaf, 2-7=-5 != 0 else → dfs(None)×2 → pop
    5 — — — [5,4,11] — back in 11
    6 dfs(2, 2) 2 2 [5,4,11,2] Leaf, 2-2=0 Yes save [5,4,11,2] → pop
    7 — — — [5,4,11] — back in 11 → pop
    8 — — — [5,4] — back in 4 → pop
    9 — — — [5] — back in 5, ab right
    10 dfs(8, 17) 8 17 [5,8] No explore
    11 dfs(13, 9) 13 9 [5,8,13] Leaf, 9-13=-4 else → pop
    12 — — — [5,8] — back in 8
    13 dfs(4, 9) 4 9 [5,8,4] No explore
    14 dfs(5, 5) 5 5 [5,8,4,5] Leaf, 5-5=0 Yes save [5,8,4,5] → pop
    15 — — — [5,8,4] — back in 4
    16 dfs(1, 5) 1 5 [5,8,4,1] Leaf, 5-1=4 else → pop
    17 — — — [5,8,4] — → pop
    18 — — — [5,8] — → pop
    19 — — — [5] — → pop
    20 — — — [] — done

    Result [[5,4,11,2], [5,8,4,5]]. Sahi.

    Steps 6 aur 14 par path[:] ka role dekho: step 6 par [5,4,11,2] ki copy saved hui. Step 7-9 mein path shrink hoke [5] ban gaya. Agar copy nahi banayi hoti toh result[0] bhi [5] ban jaata — aur step 20 ke baad [] ban jaata. Poora output khaali lists ka list hota.

    Step 20 ka path == [] bhi important hai — yeh confirm karta hai ki har append ka pop hua. Agar aakhir mein path khaali nahi hai toh kahin ek pop reh gaya hai. Yeh ek accha self-check hai jo interview mein bol sakte ho.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n) traversal ke liye, plus O(number of valid paths × path length) copies ke liye. Worst case (jab har leaf ek valid path ho) yeh O(n * h) hai — jo output ka size hi hai, toh yeh avoidable nahi. Brute force ke ulta: brute force har node par copy banata tha; yeh sirf valid answers par banata hai. Agar 1000 leaves hain aur sirf 2 valid paths, toh brute force 1000 copies banata aur yeh 2.
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack plus path, plus O(output) result ke liye.

    Edge cases

    Case Input target Output Kyun
    Empty None 0 [] Null guard
    Single match 5 5 [[5]] Leaf + match
    Single no match 5 3 []
    Multiple paths same sum perfect tree with equal values multiple Sab milte hain
    Negative values -2 -> -3 -5 [[-2,-3]] Subtraction works
    Target 0 with 0 nodes 0->0 0 [[0,0]]
    Path exists but not to leaf 1->2 1 [] Leaf requirement
    Deep skewed 10^5 — RecursionError Iterative chahiye

    Variations

    • Sirf count chahiye, paths nahi — path list ki zaroorat hi nahi, ek counter kaafi.
    • Sirf pehla path chahiye — mil jaane par True return karke propagate karo (Problem 8.1 jaisa).
    • Any node se any node tak paths (LeetCode 437) — Problem 8.5, prefix sum plus hash map.
    • Sabse chhota path jiska sum target hai — sab collect karke min(key=len).
    • Path as strings — path.append(str(node.val)) aur "->".join(path).
    • Binary Tree Paths (257) — saare root-to-leaf paths, bina sum condition ke. Bilkul yehi code, bas line 8 se remaining == 0 hata do.

    Interview answer: "The naive version builds a fresh copy of the path at every node so that sibling branches don't see each other's state. That's correct but costs O(depth) per node, which is quadratic on a skewed tree.

    Instead I keep one shared path list and use backtracking: append the node's value on the way in, recurse, and pop it on the way out. That's the choose–explore–unchoose pattern, and the invariant is that when a call returns, the path is exactly as it found it.

    Two details that are easy to get wrong. When I record a match I have to append a copy of the path, not the path itself — otherwise every entry in the result is a reference to the same list, and the pops on the way back out empty all of them. And I must not return early after recording a match, because that would skip the pop and corrupt the path for everything after it; I use an else branch instead.

    Worth being explicit about which state needs backtracking: the path does, because it's a mutable list I'm sharing. The remaining target doesn't, because it's an integer — subtracting rebinds a local in this frame and the caller's value is untouched. Only mutable shared state needs undoing.

    Time is O(n) for the traversal plus the cost of copying the answers, which is unavoidable since it's the output size. The saving over the naive version is real though: it copies at every node, this one copies only at genuine matches. Space is O(height) for the stack.

    This choose–explore–unchoose shape is the same skeleton as every backtracking problem — subsets, permutations, N-Queens — so it's worth recognising here."

    Problem 8.3 — Sum Of Path Numbers¶

    Problem statement

    Har root-to-leaf path ek number banata hai (digits ko concatenate karke). Saare aise numbers ka sum lauta do.

    Input:      1
           / \
          0   1
         /   / \
        1   6   5

Paths: 1->0->1 = 101
       1->1->6 = 116
       1->1->5 = 115
Output: 101 + 116 + 115 = 332

Input:  1
       / \
      2   3
Paths: 12, 13
Output: 25

    Maan lo har node ki value ek single digit (0-9) hai.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Saare paths collect karo, har ek ko string banao, int mein convert karo, sum karo.

    def sum_numbers_brute(root):
    paths = []                                    # 1: saare root-to-leaf paths
    def collect(node, path):                      # 2
        if node is None:                          # 3
            return                                # 4
        path = path + [str(node.val)]             # 5: string ke roop mein jamā
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 6: leaf
            paths.append("".join(path))           # 7: "101" type string
            return                                # 8
        collect(node.left, path)                  # 9
        collect(node.right, path)                 # 10
    collect(root, [])                             # 11
    return sum(int(p) for p in paths)             # 12: har string ko int, phir sum

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-4. Standard. 5. path + [str(node.val)] — str() conversion abhi hi kiya, taaki line 7 mein join seedha kaam kare. int list par join TypeError deta. 6-8. Leaf par path ko string banao. 7. "".join(path) — + loop mein nahi, join. String concatenation loop mein O(n^2) hoti hai (Python Essentials section mein yeh discuss hua tha). 9-10. Recurse. 11. Start. 12. sum(int(p) for p in paths) — generator expression, poora list nahi banta.

    Complexity: Time O(n * h) — paths banane aur copy karne ki wajah se. Plus int() conversions. Space O(n * h) — saare path strings.

    Isme problem kya hai

    String banane, store karne, aur phir parse karne mein teen alag O(h) operations hain. Aur humein sirf ek number chahiye — poore paths nahi.

    The insight

    Number ko neeche jaate waqt hi banate jao, digit by digit, arithmetic se — string se nahi.

    Rule: agar parent tak ka number x hai aur current node ka digit d hai, toh current node tak ka number x * 10 + d hai.

    1        -> 1
1, 0     -> 1 * 10 + 0 = 10
1, 0, 1  -> 10 * 10 + 1 = 101

    Yeh exactly wahi hai jo int("101") internally karta hai, bas hum incremental kar rahe hain aur intermediate strings kabhi bante hi nahi.

    Aur leaf par pahunchte hi woh number result mein add karo. Koi list, koi string, koi copy — kuch nahi chahiye.

    Optimal solution

    def sum_numbers(root):
    def dfs(node, current):                       # 1: `current` = root se yahan tak ka number
        if node is None:                          # 2: khaali subtree
            return 0                              # 3: sum mein zero contribute karta hai
        current = current * 10 + node.val         # 4: digit shift + add
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 5: LEAF?
            return current                        # 6: poora number ban gaya
        return dfs(node.left, current) + dfs(node.right, current)   # 7: dono taraf ka sum
    return dfs(root, 0)                           # 8: shuruaat zero se

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. def dfs(node, current): — current woh number hai jo root se is node ke parent tak bana hai. 2-3. return 0 — None ka contribution zero hai. Yeh line 7 ke + ke liye neutral element hai. Agar hum return current likh dete toh ek missing child bhi apna number contribute kar deta aur sum double ho jaata. Example: node 1 with only left child 2. Sahi answer 12. Agar None par current return karte: dfs(None, 1) → 1, aur dfs(2, 1) → 12. Sum 13 — galat. Yeh Problem 8.1 wali hi baat hai, bas alag neutral value ke saath — wahan False (kyunki or), yahan 0 (kyunki +).
    2. current = current * 10 + node.val — poore solution ka core. * 10 purane digits ko ek jagah left shift karta hai, + node.val naya digit last mein daalta hai. Yeh local rebinding hai — parent ka current nahi badla, isliye left aur right subtrees dono ko same value milti hai. Backtracking ki zaroorat nahi.
    3. if node.left is None and node.right is None: — leaf.
    4. return current — number sirf leaf par "complete" hota hai. Beech ke nodes apna partial number contribute nahi karte.
    5. return dfs(left, current) + dfs(right, current) — + se dono subtrees ka sum jamā. Yahan None children safely handle ho jaate hain kyunki line 3 0 deti hai.
    6. dfs(root, 0) — 0 se shuru, kyunki 0 * 10 + first_digit = first_digit.

    Overflow: Python mein integers unbounded hain toh koi problem nahi. Java/C++ mein deep tree par long bhi overflow kar sakta hai — yeh mention karna acha hai, aur wahan modular arithmetic ya BigInteger chahiye.

    Dry run — tree:

          1
     / \
    0   1
   /   / \
  1   6   5

    Nodes ko naam dete hain: A(1) root, B(0) left, C(1) right, D(1) left-of-B, E(6) left-of-C, F(5) right-of-C.

    Step Call node current in current after line 4 Leaf? Returns
    1 dfs(A, 0) A=1 0 0*10+1 = 1 No (pending)
    2 dfs(B, 1) B=0 1 1*10+0 = 10 No (pending)
    3 dfs(D, 10) D=1 10 10*10+1 = 101 Yes 101
    4 dfs(None, 10) None — — — 0
    5 back in B — — — — 101 + 0 = 101
    6 dfs(C, 1) C=1 1 1*10+1 = 11 No (pending)
    7 dfs(E, 11) E=6 11 11*10+6 = 116 Yes 116
    8 dfs(F, 11) F=5 11 11*10+5 = 115 Yes 115
    9 back in C — — — — 116 + 115 = 231
    10 back in A — — — — 101 + 231 = 332

    Answer 332. Sahi.

    Step 4 sabse important hai — B ka right child None hai aur usne 0 contribute kiya. Agar woh current (= 10) contribute karta toh answer 342 aata — galat. Yeh neutral-value wali line hi correctness ka anchor hai.

    Steps 7 aur 8 par dekho — dono ko current = 11 mila. Kyunki line 4 ka rebinding local tha, E ke liye 11 -> 116 hone se F ke liye current kharab nahi hua. Agar current ek mutable list hota toh backtracking chahiye hoti — integer hone ki wajah se free mein mil gaya.

    Dry run — 1 with only left child 2 (expected 12)

    Step Call node current in current after Leaf? Returns
    1 dfs(1, 0) 1 0 1 left=2 exists → No (pending)
    2 dfs(2, 1) 2 1 1*10+2 = 12 Yes 12
    3 dfs(None, 1) None — — — 0
    4 back — — — — 12 + 0 = 12

    Answer 12. Sahi.

    Iterative version:

    def sum_numbers_iterative(root):
    if root is None:                              # 9
        return 0                                  # 10
    total = 0                                     # 11
    stack = [(root, 0)]                           # 12: (node, parent tak ka number)
    while stack:                                  # 13
        node, current = stack.pop()               # 14
        current = current * 10 + node.val         # 15: wahi arithmetic
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 16: leaf
            total += current                      # 17: sum mein jodo
        else:                                     # 18
            if node.right is not None:            # 19
                stack.append((node.right, current))   # 20: state stack entry mein
            if node.left is not None:             # 21
                stack.append((node.left, current)) # 22
    return total                                  # 23

    Line 12/20/22 mein current stack entry ke saath jaata hai — recursion ke parameter ka exact equivalent. Time O(n), Space O(h), no RecursionError.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node ek baar, per node O(1) arithmetic.
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack. Balanced O(log n), skewed O(n).

    Brute force ke O(n*h) time aur space se bahut better.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Empty None 0 Line 3
    Single node 5 5 0*10+5 = 5
    Single zero 0 0
    Leading zeros 0 -> 1 1 0*10+1 = 1 — leading zero apne aap gayab
    Only left chain 1->2->3 123 Ek hi path
    Perfect depth 3 1,(2,3),(4,5,6,7) 124+125+136+137 = 522
    All same digits 1,(1,1) 11+11 = 22
    Deep tree (>18 digits) — Python exact Java mein overflow

    Leading zeros wala row important hai — 0 -> 1 path ka number 01 nahi 1 hai, aur arithmetic yeh automatically sahi karta hai. String-based solution mein int("01") = 1 — woh bhi sahi hai, toh dono agree karte hain. Lekin agar problem "01" ko literal string chahti ho toh alag baat hai — clarify karo.

    Variations

    • Binary numbers ka sum (LeetCode 1022) — * 10 ki jagah * 2.
    • Kisi bhi base mein — * base.
    • Sirf paths lauta do, sum nahi (257) — string join karke collect.
    • Maximum path number — + ki jagah max.
    • Path numbers ka product — + ki jagah *, aur neutral value 1 (na ki 0). Yeh neutral-value ka concept dobara test karta hai.
    • Multi-digit node values — current * 10 ki jagah current * 10**len(str(node.val)).

    Interview answer: "Instead of building path strings and parsing them, I build the number arithmetically as I descend: the number at a node is its parent's number times ten, plus this node's digit. That's exactly what string-to-int does internally, done incrementally, so no strings or lists ever exist.

    At a leaf the number is complete, so I return it. Internal nodes return the sum of their two subtrees.

    The base case is the part I'd point at. A null child must return zero, not the running number — zero is the neutral element for addition, so a missing child contributes nothing. If it returned the running number instead, a node with only one child would count its path twice. This is the same shape as the path-sum problem, where the neutral element was false because the combiner was or. Picking the neutral element that matches the combiner is the general rule, and it's why the product variant of this problem would need one rather than zero.

    I also don't need any backtracking, because the state I'm carrying is an integer. Rebinding it inside a call is local, so both subtrees receive the parent's value unchanged. Backtracking is only needed for mutable shared state like a path list.

    O(n) time, O(height) space. In Python integers are unbounded so there's no overflow; in Java a deep enough tree would overflow even a long, which is worth flagging."

    Problem 8.4 — Path With Given Sequence¶

    Problem statement

    Binary tree aur ek array sequence diya hai. Bataao ki koi root-to-leaf path hai jiske values exactly sequence ke barabar hon (same order mein).

    Input:      1
           / \
          0   1
         /   / \
        1   6   5
sequence = [1, 0, 1]
Output: True

sequence = [1, 1, 6]
Output: True

sequence = [1, 0, 7]
Output: False   (path 1->0->1 hai, 7 nahi)

sequence = [1, 1]
Output: False   (yeh path leaf tak nahi jaata)

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Saare root-to-leaf paths banao, phir compare karo.

    def find_path_brute(root, sequence):
    all_paths = []                                # 1
    def collect(node, path):                      # 2
        if node is None:                          # 3
            return                                # 4
        path = path + [node.val]                  # 5: naya copy
        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 6: leaf
            all_paths.append(path)                # 7
            return                                # 8
        collect(node.left, path)                  # 9
        collect(node.right, path)                 # 10
    collect(root, [])                             # 11
    return sequence in all_paths                  # 12: list comparison

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-11. Problem 8.2 wala hi collect. 12. sequence in all_paths — in on a list of lists har path ko sequence se compare karta hai (element-wise). Har comparison O(len(sequence)) hai, toh total O(paths × len).

    Complexity: Time O(n * h) paths banane ke liye, plus O(paths × len) comparison. Space O(n * h).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Hum saare paths banate hain jabki ek path banate waqt hi pata chal jaata hai ki woh match karega ya nahi. Agar sequence[0] root se hi match nahi karta toh poora tree traverse karne ka koi matlab hi nahi hai.

    The insight

    Sequence ko ek index se track karo, aur jaise hi mismatch mile turant ruk jao.

    Do checks har node par: 1. Kya index sequence ke range mein hai? Agar index >= len(sequence) toh path sequence se lamba ho gaya — fail. 2. Kya node.val == sequence[index]? Agar nahi toh fail.

    Aur leaf par ek teesra check: kya index sequence ka aakhri index tha? Agar nahi toh path sequence se chhota hai — fail.

    Yeh early termination wala fayda deta hai jo brute force mein nahi hai. Ek galat first digit poore tree ko ek hi comparison mein reject kar deta hai.

    Optimal solution

    def find_path(root, sequence):
    if root is None:                              # 1: khaali tree
        return len(sequence) == 0                 # 2: khaali sequence hi match karegi

    def dfs(node, index):                         # 3: index = sequence mein kahan hain
        if node is None:                          # 4: khaali subtree -> koi path nahi
            return False                          # 5

        if index >= len(sequence):                # 6: sequence khatam, tree nahi
            return False                          # 7: path sequence se LAMBA hai
        if node.val != sequence[index]:           # 8: is position par mismatch?
            return False                          # 9: turant reject -- yeh hi optimisation hai

        if node.left is None and node.right is None:   # 10: LEAF par pahunche
            return index == len(sequence) - 1     # 11: sequence bhi khatam hui?

        return (dfs(node.left, index + 1)         # 12: aage ka index dono ko
                or dfs(node.right, index + 1))    # 13: `or` -> short circuit

    return dfs(root, 0)                           # 14: index 0 se shuru

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-2. root is None par len(sequence) == 0. Yeh ek design decision hai: khaali tree khaali sequence ko match karta hai? Zyadatar formulations kehti hain haan. Agar problem kehti "empty tree never matches" toh seedha False. Clarify karo. 3. def dfs(node, index):. 4-5. None par False — or ka neutral element. Problem 8.1 wali hi baat. 6-7. if index >= len(sequence): return False — yeh check line 8 se PEHLE hona zaroori hai. Kyunki line 8 sequence[index] access karti hai. Agar index range se bahar ho aur hum pehle check na karein toh IndexError. Aur and se short-circuit karke ek line mein bhi likh sakte the — if index >= len(sequence) or node.val != sequence[index]: return False — lekin do alag lines rakhne se do alag failure reasons saaf dikhte hain, jo debugging mein help karta hai. 8-9. if node.val != sequence[index]: return False — turant reject. Yeh line hi brute force se asli difference hai. Agar root ki value hi galat hai toh function ek comparison ke baad False de deta hai — poora tree kabhi traverse nahi hota. 10-11. Leaf par teen cheezein ek saath sach honi chahiye: node leaf hai, values ab tak match kiye (lines 6-9 ne guarantee kiya), aur index aakhri position par hai. index == len(sequence) - 1 — - 1 zaroori hai kyunki index 0-based hai. index == len(sequence) kabhi True nahi hoga yahan (line 6 pehle reject kar deti). Yeh check [1, 1] wale example ko handle karta hai — path 1 -> 1 values match karte hain lekin node 1 (right child) ek leaf nahi hai, toh line 10 False deti hai aur hum aage jaate hain. Aur agar leaf hota lekin sequence lambi hoti toh line 11 False deti. 12-13. or — short-circuit. Aur index + 1 dono ko diya jaata hai (dono branches same position se aage jaati hain). index ek int hai toh backtracking ki zaroorat nahi — Problem 8.3 wali hi baat. 14. dfs(root, 0).

    Dry run — tree:

          1
     / \
    0   1
   /   / \
  1   6   5
    sequence = [1, 0, 1] (expected True)

    Step Call node index index < 3? node.val == seq[index]? Leaf? Action
    1 dfs(1, 0) 1 0 Yes 1 == 1 Yes No recurse(left, 1)
    2 dfs(0, 1) 0 1 Yes 0 == 0 Yes No recurse(left, 2)
    3 dfs(1, 2) 1 2 Yes 1 == 1 Yes Yes 2 == 3-1 → True
    back 2 — — — — — — True or ... → True (right skip)
    back 1 — — — — — — True (right subtree skip)

    Answer True. Aur nodes 1(right), 6, 5 kabhi visit nahi hue — or ka short-circuit.

    Dry run — sequence = [1, 0, 7] (expected False)

    Step Call node index Check Result
    1 dfs(1, 0) 1 0 1 == 1 continue
    2 dfs(0, 1) 0 1 0 == 0 continue
    3 dfs(1, 2) 1 2 1 != 7 → line 9 False
    4 dfs(None, 2) None 2 — False (line 5)
    back 2 — — — False or False False
    5 dfs(1_right, 1) 1 1 1 != 0 → line 9 False
    back 1 — — — False or False False

    Answer False.

    Step 5 sabse important hai — right subtree ka poora exploration ek hi comparison mein khatam ho gaya (1 != 0). Nodes 6 aur 5 kabhi visit nahi hue. Brute force unhe zaroor visit karta.

    Dry run — sequence = [1, 1] (expected False)

    Step Call node index Checks Result
    1 dfs(1, 0) 1 0 1 == 1, not leaf recurse
    2 dfs(0, 1) 0 1 0 != 1 → line 9 False
    3 dfs(1_right, 1) 1 1 1 == 1, leaf? left=6 exists → No recurse(6, 2)
    4 dfs(6, 2) 6 2 2 >= 2 → line 7 False
    5 dfs(5, 2) 5 2 2 >= 2 → line 7 False
    back 3 — — — False or False False
    back 1 — — — False or False False

    Answer False. Sahi — sequence [1,1] ek valid prefix hai lekin leaf tak nahi jaata.

    Steps 4 aur 5 line 6-7 ka poora justification hain — bina us check ke sequence[2] par IndexError aata.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n) worst case, lekin practically bahut kam kyunki mismatch par turant pruning hoti hai. Agar sequence tree ke kisi bhi path se match nahi karti toh often ek ya do nodes mein hi khatam.
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack.

    Brute force ke O(nh) time aur O(nh) space se better, aur pruning ki wajah se real-world mein order-of-magnitude better.

    Edge cases

    Case Tree sequence Output Kyun
    Empty tree, empty seq None [] True Line 2 (design choice — clarify)
    Empty tree, non-empty seq None [1] False Line 2
    Non-empty tree, empty seq 1 [] False Line 6: 0 >= 0
    Single node match 5 [5] True Leaf, 0 == 0
    Single node mismatch 5 [3] False Line 9
    Sequence too long 1->2 [1,2,3] False Leaf par 1 != 2 (index 1 vs len-1=2)
    Sequence too short 1->2 [1] False Node 1 leaf nahi, phir index 1 par 2 vs OOB
    Duplicate values 1,(1,1) [1,1] True
    Negative values -1 -> -2 [-1,-2] True

    Variations

    • Sequence kahin se bhi shuru ho sakti hai (leaf tak nahi jaana) — leaf check hata do, index == len(sequence) par True.
    • Sequence tree mein kahin bhi (any node se any node) — har node se ek naya DFS shuru karo — O(n^2) worst case.
    • Saare matching paths lauta do — or ki jagah collect karo (Problem 8.2 ka backtracking).
    • Subsequence match (contiguous nahi) — bilkul alag problem, DP jaisa.
    • Word search in a grid (LeetCode 79) — bilkul yehi structure, bas grid par aur visited tracking ke saath. Section 14 mein.

    Interview answer: "Rather than building every root-to-leaf path and comparing, I walk the tree and the sequence together with an index, and bail out the moment they disagree.

    At each node there are three checks. First, is the index still within the sequence — if not, the path is longer than the sequence, so fail. That check has to come before the comparison, because the comparison indexes into the sequence and would throw otherwise. Second, does this node's value match the sequence at that index — if not, fail immediately. Third, if this is a leaf, the path only matches when the index is at the last position, otherwise the path is shorter than the sequence.

    That early rejection is the whole win. If the root doesn't match the first element, I return after one comparison instead of enumerating every path in the tree. And I combine subtrees with or, so a match on the left never explores the right.

    I'd confirm one thing about the empty case: does an empty tree match an empty sequence? I've assumed yes, but it's a design decision worth naming.

    No backtracking is needed because the index is an integer — passing index plus one into both children is a local rebinding, so the two subtrees don't interfere.

    O(n) worst case, O(height) space, but usually far less because of the pruning.

    Structurally this is the same skeleton as word search on a grid: match a target sequence step by step while walking a structure, and prune on the first mismatch."

    Problem 8.5 — Count Paths For A Sum¶

    Problem statement

    Binary tree aur ek target diya hai. Bataao ki kitne paths hain jinke values ka sum target hai. Path kisi bhi node se shuru ho sakta hai aur kisi bhi node par khatam — lekin hamesha neeche ki taraf jaana hai (parent se child, ulta nahi).

    Input:      10
           /  \
          5    -3
         / \     \
        3   2     11
       / \   \
      3  -2   1
target = 8

Output: 3
        Paths: 5 -> 3            = 8
               5 -> 2 -> 1       = 8
               -3 -> 11          = 8

    Dhyaan do: yeh Problem 8.1/8.2 se fundamentally alag hai — path root se shuru hone ki zaroorat nahi, aur leaf par khatam hone ki bhi nahi.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Har node ko ek possible starting point maano, aur wahan se neeche saare paths count karo.

    def count_paths_brute(root, target):
    def count_from(node, remaining):              # 1: `node` se SHURU hone wale paths
        if node is None:                          # 2
            return 0                              # 3
        remaining -= node.val                     # 4
        count = 1 if remaining == 0 else 0        # 5: yahan khatam hone wala ek path
        count += count_from(node.left, remaining) # 6: aur neeche continue karne wale
        count += count_from(node.right, remaining)# 7
        return count                              # 8

    if root is None:                              # 9
        return 0                                  # 10
    return (count_from(root, target)              # 11: root se shuru hone wale
            + count_paths_brute(root.left, target)    # 12: left subtree mein kahin se shuru
            + count_paths_brute(root.right, target))  # 13: right subtree mein kahin se shuru

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. count_from(node, remaining) — is node ko starting point maan kar neeche jaane wale paths gino. 2-3. Null → 0.
    2. remaining -= node.val.
    3. count = 1 if remaining == 0 else 0 — return nahi kiya. Yeh critical hai: agar yahan sum match hua toh ek path mila, lekin hum ruk nahi sakte — kyunki aage negative values ho sakti hain jo sum ko wapas target par le aayein. Example: [5, 3, -3, 3] mein target = 5 ke liye do paths hain (5 aur 5,3,-3). Yeh sabse zyada miss hone wali baat hai. 6-7. Neeche continue karo.
    4. Return. 9-10. Guard.
    5. Root se shuru hone wale paths. 12-13. Har dusre node ko bhi starting point banana hai — isliye poora function left aur right par dobara call.

    Complexity: Time O(n^2) — har node ke liye count_from chalta hai jo O(n) hai. Balanced tree par O(n log n), skewed par O(n^2). Space O(h).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Har node se ek naya downward scan. Bahut sa kaam repeat ho raha hai: node X se neeche jaane wala scan aur uske parent se neeche jaane wala scan lagbhag same nodes visit karte hain.

    The insight

    Yeh problem actually "Subarray Sum Equals K" (LeetCode 560) ka tree version hai — aur uska solution prefix sum plus hash map hai. (Section 21 mein array version detail mein hai.)

    Idea yeh hai: root se current node tak ka running sum S rakho. Ab agar kisi ancestor tak ka running sum S - target tha, toh us ancestor ke turant baad se current node tak ka path ka sum exactly target hai.

    root ......... ancestor ......... current
|<--- S - target --->|
|<---------------- S ----------------->|
                     |<-- target -->|

    Toh: ek hash map rakho {running_sum: kitni baar dekha}, aur har node par prefix_counts[S - target] dekh lo — wahi is node par khatam hone wale paths ki count hai.

    Aur ek critical detail — backtracking. Map mein sirf current path ke ancestors hone chahiye, saare visited nodes nahi. Kyunki ek sibling subtree ka node current node ka ancestor nahi hai, aur usse path banana galat hoga. Isliye node se wapas jaate waqt uska running sum map se hataana padta hai. Yeh Problem 8.2 wala hi choose-explore-unchoose hai, bas list ki jagah map par.

    Optimal solution

    from collections import defaultdict

def count_paths(root, target):
    prefix_counts = defaultdict(int)              # 1: {running_sum: kitni baar current path par}
    prefix_counts[0] = 1                          # 2: SEED -- "khaali prefix" ek baar exist karta hai

    def dfs(node, running_sum):                   # 3: running_sum = root se yahan tak
        if node is None:                          # 4
            return 0                              # 5

        running_sum += node.val                   # 6: is node ko shaamil karo
        paths_here = prefix_counts[running_sum - target]   # 7: kitne ancestors se match?

        prefix_counts[running_sum] += 1           # 8: CHOOSE -- khud ko map mein daalo

        paths_here += dfs(node.left, running_sum) # 9: EXPLORE left
        paths_here += dfs(node.right, running_sum)# 10: EXPLORE right

        prefix_counts[running_sum] -= 1           # 11: UN-CHOOSE -- backtrack

        return paths_here                         # 12

    return dfs(root, 0)                           # 13

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. prefix_counts = defaultdict(int) — defaultdict isliye ki line 7 mein missing key par 0 mile, KeyError nahi. Normal dict ke saath prefix_counts.get(x, 0) likhna padta.
    2. prefix_counts[0] = 1 — poore solution ki sabse important aur sabse aasani se miss hone wali line. Iska matlab: "root se pehle, jab kuch bhi include nahi kiya, tab running sum 0 tha — aur woh ek baar exist karta hai." Kyun zaroori hai: agar path root se hi shuru hota hai, toh us path ke liye running_sum - target == 0 hoga, aur prefix_counts[0] mein ek entry honi chahiye. Example: tree [5] with target = 5. running_sum = 5. prefix_counts[5 - 5] = prefix_counts[0]. Agar seed nahi hota toh 0 milta aur answer 0 aata — galat. Seed ke saath 1 milta hai — sahi.
    3. def dfs(node, running_sum):. 4-5. Null → 0 paths.
    4. running_sum += node.val — local rebinding, isliye backtrack nahi chahiye. (Map ko backtrack chahiye kyunki woh shared mutable hai.)
    5. paths_here = prefix_counts[running_sum - target] — yeh line hi algorithm hai. Kitne ancestors (ya "khaali prefix") ka running sum running_sum - target tha? Utne hi paths is node par khatam hote hain jinka sum target hai. += 1 nahi likha, = likha — kyunki yeh count already sahi hai, aur baad mein subtree ke results isme add honge (lines 9-10).
    6. prefix_counts[running_sum] += 1 — choose. Yeh line 7 ke BAAD honi chahiye. Agar pehle likh dein aur target == 0 ho, toh node khud ko apna ancestor maan lega aur ek jhoota path count ho jaayega. Order matter karta hai. 9-10. Explore. Results ko paths_here mein add karo.
    7. prefix_counts[running_sum] -= 1 — un-choose. Yeh line hata do toh answer galat aayega. Kyunki tab left subtree ke running sums right subtree ko dikhenge, aur woh ancestors nahi hain — un se "path" banana galat hai (path neeche ki taraf hona chahiye, side mein nahi). Note: -= 1 kiya, del nahi. Dono kaam karte hain lekin -= 1 simpler hai (count zero ho jaayegi aur line 7 mein 0 milega, jo sahi hai). del karna bhi theek hai aur map ko chhota rakhta hai — micro-optimisation.
    8. return paths_here.
    9. dfs(root, 0) — running sum 0 se shuru.

    Dry run — tree:

            10
       /  \
      5    -3
     / \     \
    3   2     11
   / \   \
  3  -2   1
    target = 8

    Nodes: A(10), B(5), C(-3), D(3), E(2), F(11), G(3), H(-2), I(1).

    Initial: prefix_counts = {0: 1}.

    Step Node running_sum sum - target prefix_counts[sum-target] paths_here (initial) Map after choose
    1 A(10) 10 2 0 0 {0:1, 10:1}
    2 B(5) 15 7 0 0 {0:1, 10:1, 15:1}
    3 D(3) 18 10 1 (A) 1 {0:1,10:1,15:1,18:1}
    4 G(3) 21 13 0 0 {...,21:1}
    5 (G leaves) — — — 0 pop 21 → {0:1,10:1,15:1,18:1}
    6 H(-2) 16 8 0 0 {...,16:1}
    7 (H leaves) — — — 0 pop 16
    8 (D returns) — — — 1 + 0 + 0 = 1 pop 18 → {0:1,10:1,15:1}
    9 E(2) 17 9 0 0 {...,17:1}
    10 I(1) 18 10 1 (A) 1 {...,17:1,18:1}
    11 (I returns) — — — 1 pop 18
    12 (E returns) — — — 0 + 1 = 1 pop 17 → {0:1,10:1,15:1}
    13 (B returns) — — — 0 + 1 + 1 = 2 pop 15 → {0:1,10:1}
    14 C(-3) 7 -1 0 0 {0:1,10:1,7:1}
    15 F(11) 18 10 1 (A) 1 {...,18:1}
    16 (F returns) — — — 1 pop 18
    17 (C returns) — — — 0 + 0 + 1 = 1 pop 7 → {0:1,10:1}
    18 (A returns) — — — 0 + 2 + 1 = 3 pop 10

    Answer 3. Sahi.

    Step 3 ko detail mein samjho: node D(3) par running_sum = 18. 18 - 8 = 10, aur map mein 10 ki count 1 hai (node A). Matlab: A tak ka prefix sum 10 tha, aur A ke baad se D tak ka sum 18 - 10 = 8 hai — yaani path B(5) -> D(3). Bilkul sahi.

    Step 13 par backtracking ka role dekho: B se wapas jaate waqt 15 map se hata diya. Agar na hataate, toh step 15 par node F ke liye 18 - 8 = 10 dekhte waqt sab theek rehta, lekin agar sum - target kabhi 15 hota toh C ke subtree se B ke prefix par path ban jaata — jo galat hai kyunki B, F ka ancestor nahi hai.

    Ek chhota case jahan seed prefix_counts[0] = 1 bachaata hai: tree [8], target = 8. Step: running_sum = 8, 8 - 8 = 0, prefix_counts[0] = 1 → paths_here = 1. Answer 1. Bina seed ke 0 aata — galat.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Har node exactly ek baar, aur har node par O(1) hash operations.
    • Space: O(h) — map mein ek waqt par sirf current path ke prefix sums hote hain (backtracking ki wajah se), plus O(h) recursion stack.

    Brute force ke O(n^2) se fundamentally better — yeh linear hai.

    Edge cases

    Case Input target Output Kyun
    Empty None 0 0 Line 5
    Single match 8 8 1 Seed ki wajah se
    Single no match 8 5 0
    target = 0 0 -> 0 0 3 [0], [0], [0,0] — line 8 ka order matter karta hai
    Negative values 1 -> -1 -> 1 1 multiple Negatives paths ko continue hone dete hain
    All zeros, k=0 0,(0,0) 0 6 Har prefix aur suffix
    Large sums 10^9 values — Python exact
    Deep skewed 10^5 — RecursionError Iterative chahiye

    target = 0 wala case sabse achi sanity check hai — kyunki wahan line 7 aur line 8 ka order galat hone par node khud ko count kar leta hai.

    Variations

    • Subarray Sum Equals K (LeetCode 560) — bilkul yehi algorithm, array par. Section 21 mein.
    • Paths jo upar bhi ja sakte hain — tree ko undirected graph banao, phir DFS with visited.
    • Maximum length path with sum k — map mein count ki jagah depth store karo.
    • Saare paths lauta do, count nahi — map mein ancestors ki list store karni padegi, O(n^2) space worst case.
    • Path Sum III with node values as strings — parse pehle.
    • Contiguous subarray with sum divisible by k — running_sum % k ko key banao. Same trick, alag key.

    Interview answer: "The key reframe is that this is subarray-sum-equals-k, just on a tree instead of an array. So the tool is prefix sums with a hash map.

    I carry a running sum from the root down. At each node, if some ancestor had a running sum of current-sum minus target, then the segment strictly below that ancestor down to here sums to exactly the target. So I keep a map from running sum to how many times it appears on the current path, and at each node I look up current-sum minus target — that count is the number of qualifying paths ending here.

    Two things carry the correctness.

    First, I seed the map with sum zero mapping to count one. That represents the empty prefix before the root, and it's what lets a path that starts at the root be counted. Without it, a single-node tree matching the target returns zero.

    Second, the map has to be backtracked — I increment my running sum's count on the way in and decrement it on the way out. Only ancestors of the current node may be in the map. If I left a sibling subtree's sums in there, I'd count paths that go sideways, which isn't a path at all. Same choose-explore-unchoose shape as collecting root-to-leaf paths, just with a map instead of a list.

    One ordering detail: I do the lookup before inserting my own sum. Otherwise, with a target of zero, a node would match against itself and inflate the count.

    That's O(n) time and O(height) space, versus the naive approach of starting a fresh downward scan from every node, which is O(n squared) on a skewed tree.

    I'd also confirm whether values can be negative, because they can here — which is why I can't stop descending once I hit a match; a later negative value could bring the sum back to the target."

    Problem 8.6 — Diameter Of A Binary Tree¶

    Problem statement

    Tree ka diameter nikaalo — do nodes ke beech ka sabse lamba path (edges mein maapa gaya). Yeh path root se guzarne ki zaroorat nahi hai.

    Input:      1
           / \
          2   3
         / \
        4   5

Output: 3

Input:  1
       /
      2
Output: 1

    Yahan candidates do hain: path 4 -> 2 -> 5 mein 2 edges hain, aur path 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3 mein 3 edges. Sabse lamba 3 hai, toh diameter 3.

    Dhyaan do: kuch problem statements diameter ko nodes mein maapti hain (tab answer 4 hota is example mein). Yeh clarify karna zaroori hai — "edges or nodes?"

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Har node ko "path ka top point" maano, aur wahan ke left aur right subtrees ki heights jodo.

    def diameter_brute(root):
    def height(node):                             # 1: subtree ki height (edges mein)
        if node is None:                          # 2
            return -1                             # 3: khaali subtree ki height -1 (edges)
        return 1 + max(height(node.left),         # 4
                       height(node.right))        # 5

    def solve(node):                              # 6
        if node is None:                          # 7
            return 0                              # 8
        through_me = height(node.left) + height(node.right) + 2   # 9: mere through path
        return max(through_me,                    # 10: ya mere through
                   solve(node.left),              # 11: ya left subtree mein kahin
                   solve(node.right))             # 12: ya right subtree mein kahin
    return solve(root)                            # 13

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-5. height — edges mein maapi gayi. Line 3 mein -1 isliye ki ek single node ki height 0 edges hai (1 + max(-1, -1) = 0). Agar nodes mein maapte toh 0 hota aur single node ki height 1. 6-8. solve — is subtree ka diameter. 9. height(left) + height(right) + 2 — +2 kyun? height(left) = left subtree ke andar sabse lamba downward path (edges mein). Us subtree ke root tak pahunchne ke liye ek aur edge chahiye. Same right ke liye. Toh +1 + 1 = +2. Check: single node 1 with children 2, 3. height(2) = 0, height(3) = 0. 0 + 0 + 2 = 2. Path 2 -> 1 -> 3 mein 2 edges. Sahi. 10-12. Teen candidates: mere through, left mein kahin, right mein kahin. max lo. 13. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n^2) — solve har node par chalta hai aur har baar height bhi chalta hai jo O(n) hai. Skewed tree par O(n^2). Space O(h).

    Isme problem kya hai

    height bar bar recompute ho raha hai. Node X ki height uske parent ke solve mein bhi nikalti hai, uske grandparent ke solve mein bhi, aur khud X ke solve mein bhi.

    The insight

    Yeh Type B (bottom-up) problem hai — aur ismein ek trick hai jo poore section ki sabse important technique hai.

    Recursion do cheezein deal karti hai: 1. Jo woh return karti hai — parent ke liye useful information (yahan: is subtree ki height). 2. Jo woh side effect ke roop mein update karti hai — global answer (yahan: ab tak ka best diameter).

    Kyun do alag? Kyunki parent ko "diameter" nahi chahiye — parent ko "height" chahiye. Parent apna diameter khud calculate karega. Lekin diameter kisi bhi node par ho sakta hai, toh use ek jagah track karna padega.

    Toh: height() function likho jo normal height return kare, aur uske andar har node par diameter check karke ek outer variable update karo.

    Ek hi traversal, har node ek baar. O(n).

    Yeh "return one thing, track another" pattern DP-on-trees ka core hai aur Problem 8.7 mein bhi dikhega.

    Optimal solution

    def diameter_of_binary_tree(root):
    best = 0                                      # 1: ab tak ka sabse lamba path (edges)

    def height(node):                             # 2: is subtree ki height LAUTATA hai
        nonlocal best                             # 3: bahar wale `best` ko modify karna hai
        if node is None:                          # 4: khaali subtree
            return 0                              # 5: NODES mein maapa -- neeche dekho

        left = height(node.left)                  # 6: left subtree ki height
        right = height(node.right)                # 7: right subtree ki height

        best = max(best, left + right)            # 8: MERE through path (edges mein)

        return 1 + max(left, right)               # 9: parent ke liye MERI height

    height(root)                                  # 10: traversal chalao
    return best                                   # 11: side effect mein jamā hua answer

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. best = 0 — answer yahan jamā hota hai, return value mein nahi.
    2. def height(node): — naam "height" hai, "diameter" nahi. Yeh deliberate hai: function ka contract hai "apni height lautao", aur diameter ek side effect hai.
    3. nonlocal best — Python-specific aur zaroori. Bina nonlocal ke line 8 ka best = ... ek naya local variable banata aur outer best kabhi update nahi hota — function 0 return karta hamesha. Yeh sabse common Python bug hai is pattern mein. Alternatives: best ko ek single-element list banao (best = [0], phir best[0] = ...) — tab nonlocal nahi chahiye kyunki list mutate ho rahi hai, rebind nahi. Ya class attribute (self.best). Teenon chalte hain; nonlocal sabse saaf hai. 4-5. return 0 for None — yahan height NODES mein maapi ja rahi hai, edges mein nahi. height(None) = 0, height(single node) = 1. Yeh brute force ke -1 convention se alag hai, aur isliye line 8 ka formula bhi alag hai (+2 nahi, kuch bhi nahi). Kyun yeh convention chuni: kyunki isse line 8 sabse simple ho jaati hai. Dekho:
    4. Node 1 with children 2, 3: left = height(2) = 1, right = height(3) = 1. left + right = 2. Path 2->1->3 mein 2 edges. Sahi, bina kisi + ke.
    5. Node with no children: left = right = 0, left + right = 0. Sahi (akela node, 0 edges).
    6. Yeh conveniently kaam karta hai kyunki "left subtree ki node-height" exactly "left ki taraf ke edges ki count" hai (root se left subtree ke sabse gehre node tak). 6-7. Bachchon ki heights. Dono ko lena zaroori hai — max nahi le sakte kyunki line 8 ko dono chahiye.
    7. best = max(best, left + right) — is node se guzarne wale sabse lambe path ki length. Yeh line 9 se pehle honi chahiye conceptually (dono independent hain, lekin padhne mein pehle theek lagti hai). Yeh line har node par chalti hai, isliye diameter chahe tree mein kahin bhi ho, pakda jaata hai.
    8. return 1 + max(left, right) — parent ke liye height. max isliye kyunki ek path parent tak jaayega toh sirf ek side se ja sakta hai. 1 + khud ke liye. Line 8 mein + hai aur line 9 mein max hai — yeh farq hi poori problem hai. Line 8 "path mere through jaata hai, dono side use kar sakta hai" hai. Line 9 "path mere upar jaayega, ek hi side use kar sakta hai" hai.
    9. height(root) — return value discard kar rahe hain. Humein root ki height nahi chahiye, humein best chahiye.
    10. return best.

    Nodes mein diameter chahiye toh: line 8 ko best = max(best, left + right + 1) kar do.

    Dry run — tree:

          1
     / \
    2   3
   / \
  4   5

    Post-order traversal hoti hai (bachche pehle), toh order: 4, 5, 2, 3, 1.

    Step Node left right left + right best after Returns 1 + max(l,r)
    1 4 height(None)=0 0 0 0 1 + 0 = 1
    2 5 0 0 0 0 1
    3 2 1 (from 4) 1 (from 5) 2 2 1 + max(1,1) = 2
    4 3 0 0 0 2 1
    5 1 2 (from 2) 1 (from 3) 3 3 1 + max(2,1) = 3

    best = 3. Sahi — path 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3, jismein 3 edges hain.

    Step 3 aur step 5 ka contrast dekho: - Step 3: node 2 par best 2 hua (path 4->2->5), lekin return 2 hua (na ki 2 ka "diameter"). - Step 5: node 1 ko 2 ki height mili (2), diameter nahi. Aur usne apna left + right = 2 + 1 = 3 calculate kiya.

    Agar height diameter return karta toh step 5 galat ho jaata — kyunki 1 ko 2 ka diameter (2) milta aur woh 2 + 1 = 3 calculate karta... sanyog se same aata is case mein. Ek aur example lete hain jahan farq dikhega.

    Dry run — jahan return value aur answer alag hote hain — tree:

            1
       /
      2
     / \
    3   4
   /     \
  5       6

    Order: 5, 3, 6, 4, 2, 1.

    Step Node left right left+right best after Returns
    1 5 0 0 0 0 1
    2 3 1 (from 5) 0 1 1 1 + max(1,0) = 2
    3 6 0 0 0 1 1
    4 4 0 1 (from 6) 1 1 1 + max(0,1) = 2
    5 2 2 (from 3) 2 (from 4) 4 4 1 + max(2,2) = 3
    6 1 3 (from 2) 0 3 4 1 + max(3,0) = 4

    best = 4. Path 5 -> 3 -> 2 -> 4 -> 6 — 4 edges. Sahi.

    Step 6 sabse important hai: node 1 par left + right = 3 + 0 = 3, jo best (4) se kam hai — toh best nahi badla. Diameter root se guzarta hi nahi. Yeh exactly woh case hai jo "answer ko alag se track karo" wali technique justify karta hai. Agar hum sirf root ka return value dekhte toh 4 mil jaata (sanyog se), lekin best alag track karna hi general solution hai.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Ek hi post-order traversal, har node par O(1) kaam.
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack. Balanced O(log n), skewed O(n).

    Brute force ke O(n^2) se fundamentally better.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output (edges) Kyun
    Empty None 0 best kabhi update nahi hua
    Single node 1 0 0 + 0 = 0
    Two nodes 1 -> 2 1 left=1, right=0 → 1
    Three nodes (V) 1,(2,3) 2 1 + 1
    Left skewed 5 chain 4 Ek hi path
    Diameter not through root Upar wala dry run 4 best tracking ki wajah se
    Perfect depth 3 7 nodes 4 2 + 2
    All negative values — same Values matter nahi karti, structure matter karti

    Empty tree ka case: best = 0 return hota hai. Kya yeh sahi hai? Ek khaali tree ka diameter 0 hai — haan, generally accept hota hai. Agar problem -1 ya error chahti ho toh clarify karo.

    Variations

    • Diameter in nodes — left + right + 1.
    • Diameter ka actual path lauta do — har node par path store karna padega, O(n) space per node — ya parent pointers se reconstruct.
    • N-ary tree diameter (LeetCode 1522) — sabhi children ki heights nikaalo, top do lo aur jodo.
    • Weighted edges — 1 + ki jagah edge_weight +.
    • Longest path in a general graph (tree) — do BFS: kisi bhi node se sabse door node dhoondo, phir wahan se sabse door node dhoondo. Yeh ek bilkul alag aur bahut elegant technique hai aur mention karne layak.
    • Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (124) — Problem 8.7, exactly yehi structure lekin heights ki jagah sums.

    Interview answer: "First I'd confirm whether the diameter is counted in edges or in nodes, because that's a plus-one difference.

    The naive approach treats every node as the top of a candidate path and computes both subtree heights there. That recomputes heights over and over — quadratic on a skewed tree.

    The technique that fixes it is the one I'd emphasise: the recursion returns one thing and tracks another. It returns the subtree's height, which is what the parent actually needs, and as a side effect it updates an outer variable holding the best diameter seen so far.

    They have to be separate because the parent can't use a child's diameter — a path continuing up to the parent can only use one side of the child. But the diameter itself might sit anywhere in the tree and never touch the root, so it needs its own accumulator.

    Concretely, at each node: left height plus right height is the longest path through this node, so I max that into the answer. And I return one plus the max of the two heights, because a path going up can only take one branch. That contrast — sum for the answer, max for the return — is the whole problem.

    One Python detail: I need nonlocal on the accumulator. Without it the assignment creates a fresh local and the outer variable never changes, so the function silently returns zero. Alternatives are a one-element list or an instance attribute.

    O(n) time with a single post-order traversal, O(height) space.

    This same shape — return the upward-usable value, accumulate the best-anywhere value — is exactly what maximum path sum needs too, with sums instead of heights."

    Problem 8.7 — Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum¶

    Problem statement

    Tree mein sabse zyada sum wala path dhoondo. Path kisi bhi node se shuru ho sakta hai aur kisi bhi node par khatam — bas connected hona chahiye aur koi node do baar use nahi hona chahiye. Values negative ho sakti hain.

    Input:      1
           / \
          2   3
Output: 6        (2 -> 1 -> 3)

Input:     -10
           /  \
          9    20
              /  \
             15   7
Output: 42       (15 -> 20 -> 7)

Input:  -3
Output: -3       (kam se kam ek node lena hi hoga)

    Yeh Problem 8.6 (diameter) ka twin hai — bilkul same structure, bas "count edges" ki jagah "sum values" hai. Lekin negatives ki wajah se ek extra twist hai.

    Pehla instinct — brute force

    Har node ko path ka "top" maano, aur uske dono taraf ka best downward sum nikaalo.

    def max_path_sum_brute(root):
    def best_down(node):                          # 1: is node se neeche jaane wala best sum
        if node is None:                          # 2
            return 0                              # 3: khaali -> kuch contribute nahi
        return node.val + max(0,                  # 4: negative branch chhod do
                              best_down(node.left),
                              best_down(node.right))

    def solve(node):                              # 5
        if node is None:                          # 6
            return float('-inf')                  # 7: koi path nahi -> sabse chhota
        through_me = (node.val                    # 8: mere through jaane wala path
                      + max(0, best_down(node.left))
                      + max(0, best_down(node.right)))
        return max(through_me,                    # 9: teen candidates
                   solve(node.left),
                   solve(node.right))
    return solve(root)                            # 10

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1-4. best_down — node se neeche jaane wala best path sum. Line 4 mein max(0, ...) — negative branch ko chhod dena hai. Agar left subtree ka best sum -5 hai toh usse jodne se sum kam ho jaayega; behtar hai use bilkul na lein. 0 ka matlab "us direction mein bilkul mat jao." 5-7. solve — is subtree ka best path sum. Line 7 mein float('-inf') — 0 nahi. Kyunki agar saari values negative hon toh 0 ek jhoota candidate ban jaata. Empty subtree se koi path banta hi nahi. 8. node.val + max(0, left) + max(0, right) — dono taraf ka best, negatives skip karke. 9. Teen candidates ka max. 10. Return.

    Complexity: Time O(n^2) — solve har node par, aur andar best_down bhi O(n). Space O(h).

    Isme problem kya hai

    Wahi jo diameter mein tha — best_down bar bar recompute ho raha hai.

    The insight

    Bilkul Problem 8.6 wali hi technique: recursion ek cheez return kare (upar jaane wala best downward sum) aur doosri cheez track kare (ab tak ka best complete path sum).

    Aur do negativity-related decisions jo is problem ko diameter se alag banate hain:

    Pehla — negative branches ko chhod do. Agar ek subtree ka best downward sum negative hai, toh use include karna nuksaan hai. max(0, child_result) se yeh handle hota hai.

    Dusra — best ko float('-inf') se seed karo, 0 se nahi. Kyunki agar tree ki saari values negative hain (jaise single node -3), toh answer -3 hona chahiye, 0 nahi. 0 se seed karne par function 0 return karta — galat, kyunki khaali path allowed nahi hai (kam se kam ek node chahiye).

    Optimal solution

    def max_path_sum(root):
    best = float('-inf')                          # 1: 0 se NAHI -- negatives handle karne ke liye

    def max_down(node):                           # 2: is node se NEECHE jaane wala best sum
        nonlocal best                             # 3: bahar wala `best` update karna hai
        if node is None:                          # 4: khaali subtree
            return 0                              # 5: 0 contribute karta hai (path skip)

        left = max(0, max_down(node.left))        # 6: negative branch -> 0 (chhod do)
        right = max(0, max_down(node.right))      # 7: same

        best = max(best, node.val + left + right) # 8: MERE THROUGH path -- dono side

        return node.val + max(left, right)        # 9: UPAR jaane wala -- ek hi side

    max_down(root)                                # 10: traversal
    return best                                   # 11

    Line by line — kyun aise likha hai

    1. best = float('-inf') — 0 se seed karna sabse common bug hai. float('-inf') Python ka "sabse chhota number" hai; koi bhi real value usse badi hogi, toh pehla comparison hamesha best ko update karega. Test: tree [-3]. Line 8 par best = max(-inf, -3 + 0 + 0) = -3. Sahi. Agar best = 0 se seed karte toh max(0, -3) = 0 — galat.
    2. def max_down(node): — naam bata raha hai ki yeh "neeche jaane wala" sum lautata hai, "best path sum" nahi.
    3. nonlocal best — Problem 8.6 wali hi zaroorat. 4-5. return 0 for None — yahan 0 sahi hai. Kyunki line 6/7 mein hum max(0, ...) kar rahe hain, aur "khaali subtree" ka matlab hai "is direction mein 0 contribute hua." Yeh line 1 ke -inf se alag hai — do alag cheezein hain: "koi path nahi mila" (-inf) aur "is direction se 0 contribute" (0).
    4. left = max(0, max_down(node.left)) — max(0, ...) hi negativity ka handling hai. Agar left subtree ka best -7 hai toh max(0, -7) = 0 — matlab "left mein mat jao." Yeh ek clean tarika hai "optional branch" ko express karne ka, bina if conditions ke.
    5. Same for right.
    6. best = max(best, node.val + left + right) — is node se guzarne wala poora path. Yeh path left subtree se neeche shuru hota hai, node se upar aata hai, aur right subtree mein neeche jaata hai. Yeh path apne parent ke liye useless hai (kyunki node do baar use nahi ho sakta), isliye ise sirf best mein record karte hain, return nahi. node.val hamesha shaamil hai — chahe negative ho. Kyunki path kam se kam ek node ka hona chahiye, aur node hi is path ka top hai.
    7. return node.val + max(left, right) — parent ke liye. max isliye ki parent tak jaane wala path sirf ek branch use kar sakta hai (warna woh path nahi, ek "Y" shape ho jaata). Line 8 mein left + right hai aur line 9 mein max(left, right) — yehi is problem ka poora core hai, bilkul diameter jaisa.
    8. max_down(root) — return value discard.
    9. return best.

    Do max ka summary (yeh table interview mein bolne layak hai):

    Line Expression Kyun
    6/7 max(0, child) Negative branch skip karo — optional include
    8 node.val + left + right Path mere through, dono side use
    9 node.val + max(left, right) Path mere upar, ek side use

    Dry run — tree:

         -10
     /  \
    9    20
        /  \
       15   7

    Post-order: 9, 15, 7, 20, -10.

    Step Node left right Line 8: val+l+r best after Line 9 returns
    init — — — — -inf —
    1 9 max(0, 0)=0 max(0,0)=0 9+0+0 = 9 9 9 + max(0,0) = 9
    2 15 0 0 15+0+0 = 15 15 15
    3 7 0 0 7+0+0 = 7 15 7
    4 20 max(0,15)=15 max(0,7)=7 20+15+7 = 42 42 20 + max(15,7) = 35
    5 -10 max(0,9)=9 max(0,35)=35 -10+9+35 = 34 42 -10 + max(9,35) = 25

    best = 42. Sahi — path 15 -> 20 -> 7.

    Step 4 aur 5 ka contrast hi poora insight hai: - Step 4 par node 20 ne 42 record kiya (dono bachche use karke), lekin 35 return kiya (sirf ek bachcha). - Step 5 par node -10 ko 35 mila (na ki 42), aur usne 34 calculate kiya — jo 42 se kam hai. - Agar node 20 42 return karta, toh -10 -10 + 9 + 42 = 41 calculate karta — jo ek invalid path hai kyunki usme node 20 do baar use hota (ek baar 15->20->7 mein, ek baar -10 tak jaane ke liye).

    Yeh exactly woh reason hai ki return value aur answer alag hain.

    Dry run — saari values negative — tree:

        -3
   /  \
 -5   -2
    Step Node left right Line 8 best after Line 9 returns
    init — — — — -inf —
    1 -5 0 0 -5+0+0 = -5 -5 -5 + 0 = -5
    2 -2 0 0 -2+0+0 = -2 -2 -2
    3 -3 max(0,-5)=0 max(0,-2)=0 -3+0+0 = -3 -2 (kyunki -2 > -3) -3 + 0 = -3

    best = -2. Sahi — sabse achha path akela node -2 hai.

    Step 3 par max(0, -5) = 0 aur max(0, -2) = 0 dekho — dono bachchon ko skip kar diya kyunki dono negative the. Aur best -2 hi raha kyunki -3 usse chhota hai.

    Bina max(0, ...) ke kya hota: step 3 par left = -5, right = -2, line 8 -3 + (-5) + (-2) = -10 — jo best ko affect nahi karta (-2 bada hai), lekin line 9 -3 + max(-5,-2) = -5 return karta, jo kisi bade tree mein galat propagate hota.

    Bina -inf seed ke kya hota: best = 0 se shuru karte toh answer 0 aata (kyunki -2 < 0) — galat, kyunki khaali path allowed nahi hai.

    Complexity

    • Time: O(n). Ek post-order traversal, per node O(1).
    • Space: O(h) recursion stack.

    Edge cases

    Case Input Output Kyun
    Single positive 5 5 5+0+0
    Single negative -3 -3 -inf seed ki wajah se
    All negative -3,(-5,-2) -2 Upar wala dry run
    Mixed with big negative root -10,(9,20...) 42 Root skip ho jaata
    All positive 1,(2,3) 6 Poora tree
    Zeros 0,(0,0) 0
    Left skewed positive 1->2->3 6 Ek hi chain
    Empty tree None -inf Clarify karo — kuch versions 0 chahti hain, kuch error

    Empty tree ka case sabse worth-asking hai. Yeh code float('-inf') return karega. Agar problem 0 chahti hai toh ek guard chahiye. LeetCode 124 guarantee deta hai ki tree khaali nahi hoga, isliye yeh case nahi aata — lekin poochna acha hai.

    Variations

    • Path root se guzarna chahiye — sirf root par best update karo.
    • Path root-to-leaf hona chahiye — Problem 8.1/8.2 family, bilkul alag.
    • Path ka actual node sequence lauta do — har node par path store karna padega, ya parent pointers se reconstruct.
    • Maximum path sum with at most k nodes — DP with an extra dimension, bahut mushkil.
    • Diameter (LeetCode 543) — Problem 8.6, exactly yehi structure with heights.
    • Longest ZigZag Path (1372) — same "return one, track another", alag state.
    • House Robber III (337) — same structure, lekin har node do values return karta hai (rob / don't rob).

    Interview answer: "This is structurally identical to the diameter problem — the recursion returns one value and accumulates a different one — with sums instead of edge counts, plus two complications from negative numbers.

    At each node, the best path through it uses both subtrees: node value plus the best downward sum on the left plus the best on the right. That's a candidate for the global answer. But that path can't be extended upward, because the node would be visited twice. So what I return is node value plus the max of the two sides — only one branch can continue upward. Sum for the answer, max for the return.

    The first negativity handling: I clamp each child's contribution with max of zero and the child's result. If a subtree's best downward sum is negative, including it only hurts, so zero means 'don't go that way'. That expresses an optional branch without any if statements.

    The second: I seed the global best with negative infinity, not zero. If every value in the tree is negative — say a single node of minus three — seeding with zero would return zero, which corresponds to an empty path, and the problem requires at least one node. Note the asymmetry: zero is correct for the null base case, because that genuinely means 'this direction contributes nothing', but it's wrong as the answer seed, because that would mean 'an empty path is a valid answer'. Two different zeros with different meanings.

    Concretely on the minus-ten example: node twenty records forty-two as the answer using both children, but returns thirty-five using only one. If it returned forty-two, the root would compute a path that goes through node twenty twice.

    Python detail again: nonlocal on the accumulator, or the assignment creates a local and the answer never escapes.

    O(n) time, O(height) space. And I'd ask whether the tree can be empty, since that changes what to return."

    Aur tree DFS problems — practice list¶

    Path problems (Type A — top-down state):

    1. Path Sum (LeetCode 112) — Problem 8.1. Base pattern.
    2. Path Sum II (113) — Problem 8.2. Backtracking ka pehla exposure.
    3. Sum Root to Leaf Numbers (129) — Problem 8.3.
    4. Binary Tree Paths (257) — 8.2 ka simpler version, bina sum condition ke.
    5. Path With Given Sequence — Problem 8.4.
    6. Path Sum III (437) — Problem 8.5. Prefix sum plus hash map, bahut poocha jaata hai.
    7. Smallest String Starting From Leaf (988) — 8.3 jaisa lekin strings aur comparison.

    Subtree aggregate problems (Type B — bottom-up):

    1. Maximum Depth of Binary Tree (104) — teen line ka base.
    2. Diameter of Binary Tree (543) — Problem 8.6. "Return one, track another" ka intro.
    3. Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (124) — Problem 8.7. Hard tag, top-20 problem.
    4. Balanced Binary Tree (110) — height return karo plus -1 sentinel se imbalance signal karo.
    5. Count Univalue Subtrees (250) — bachchon se boolean plus value.
    6. House Robber III (337) — har node do values return karta hai.
    7. Longest Univalue Path (687) — 8.6 ka variant with value constraint.
    8. Binary Tree Tilt (563) — sum return, tilt accumulate.

    Structural problems:

    1. Invert Binary Tree (226) — classic, do line ka.
    2. Same Tree (100) / Symmetric Tree (101) — do trees ko saath traverse karo.
    3. Subtree of Another Tree (572) — nested traversal.
    4. Lowest Common Ancestor (236) — bahut important, bottom-up with three cases.
    5. Validate Binary Search Tree (98) — min/max bounds neeche le jao, ya inorder karke sorted check karo.
    6. Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree (297) — preorder with null markers.
    7. Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder (105) — index map plus recursion.
    8. Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List (114) — in-place restructuring.
    9. Delete Nodes And Return Forest (1110) — postorder plus collection.

    Ek line mein poore pattern ka summary: Pehle poocho — "kya node ka answer bachchon ke answers se banta hai (bottom-up) ya parent se state neeche jaati hai (top-down)?" Agar answer kahin bhi ho sakta hai lekin parent ko kuch aur chahiye, toh "ek cheez return karo, doosri track karo."

    9. Two Heaps¶

    Recognition signals — aap two heaps dekh rahe ho jab problem bole¶

    • "median" — kisi bhi form mein: stream ka median, sliding window ka median. Yeh sabse direct signal hai.
    • "middle element" ya "balance the two halves".
    • Aapko ek saath sabse chhote elements mein se sabse bada aur sabse bade elements mein se sabse chhota chahiye ho.
    • "maximize / minimize" with do alag criteria — jaise "capital ke hisaab se affordable, phir profit ke hisaab se best" (IPO problem).
    • "next interval", "schedule with two constraints".
    • Data stream mein aa raha ho aur har addition ke baad ek query ka jawab chahiye ho.
    • Aapka natural solution "har baar sort karo" ho — aur woh O(n log n) per operation ho.

    Yeh pattern kaam kyun karta hai — asli intuition¶

    Median ka matlab: data ko do barabar hisson mein baanto, aur beech wala element (ya beech wale do ka average) hi answer hai.

    Sorted array mein yeh trivial hai — bas arr[n // 2] dekh lo. Lekin stream mein sorted rakhna mehnga hai (har insertion O(n) shift).

    Insight: humein poora sorted order chahiye hi nahi. Humein sirf do cheezein chahiye: 1. Chhote aadhe hisse ka maximum, 2. Bade aadhe hisse ka minimum.

    Aur exactly yeh do cheezein heaps O(1) mein dete hain (peek) aur O(log n) mein maintain karte hain (insert).

    Toh: - Max-heap rakho chhote aadhe ke liye — uska top chhote hisse ka sabse bada element hai. - Min-heap rakho bade aadhe ke liye — uska top bade hisse ka sabse chhota element hai. - Dono ke tops hi median ke aas paas ke elements hain.

            max-heap (small half)        min-heap (large half)
              [1, 3, 5]                  [7, 9, 11]
                   ^                      ^
                   |                      |
              top = 5                 top = 7
                        median = (5 + 7) / 2 = 6

    Python mein max-heap kaise banate hain — yeh har baar poocha jaata hai¶

    Python ke heapq mein sirf min-heap hai. Max-heap ke liye values ko negate kar do:

    import heapq

max_heap = []
heapq.heappush(max_heap, -5)      # 5 daalne ke liye -5 push karo
heapq.heappush(max_heap, -1)
largest = -max_heap[0]            # nikaalte waqt wapas negate karo -> 5

    Kyun kaam karta hai: agar a > b toh -a < -b. Toh sabse bada element negate hone ke baad sabse chhota ban jaata hai, aur min-heap use top par le aata hai.

    Do jagah galti hoti hai: 1. Push karte waqt negate karna bhool jaana. 2. Peek/pop karte waqt wapas negate karna bhool jaana.

    Alternative: ek wrapper class jismein __lt__ ulta ho. Zyada clean hai lekin zyada code. Interview mein negation hi standard hai — bas comment likh do taaki clear rahe.

    Balancing invariant — yeh do rules poore pattern ko chalate hain¶

    Rule 1 (size): len(small) == len(large) ya len(small) == len(large) + 1. Yaani small mein ya toh barabar elements hain ya ek zyada. (Ulta convention bhi chalta hai — bas consistent raho.)

    Rule 2 (ordering): small ka har element large ke har element se <= hona chahiye. Practically sirf -small[0] <= large[0] check karna kaafi hai (dono tops).
